latest.title: Parasocial Interaction and Perceived Value as Determinants of Intention to Buy Made-in-Thailand Products through Live- Streaming Personal Shoppers
latest.venue: International Review of Management and Marketing
latest.abstract: This research investigates the rising trend of live shopping and jasa titipan (jastip) in Southeast Asian digital commerce, focusing on the growing popularity of Made in Thailand products among Indonesian consumers. Livestream commerce has changed consumer behaviour by offering immediacy, interactivity, and immersive digital experiences that lessen psychological distance between sellers and buyers. In Indonesia, live personal shopper sessions have become a key method for cross-border purchases of Thai cosmetics, fashion items, herbal supplements, and packaged foods, which are widely viewed as authentic and high-quality. Despite the market's rapid growth, previous research has mostly examined individual aspects like interactivity, trust, or entertainment, with limited attention to understanding the combined psychological factors influencing purchase intentions in livestream shopping. This study develops and tests a structural equation model (SEM) that includes social presence, parasocial interaction, perceived trust, perceived value, and perceived enjoyment to explain Indonesian consumers’ willingness to buy Thai products via live personal shoppers. The model captures both utilitarian and hedonic evaluation aspects, showing how relational bonding, immediacy, credibility cues, and experiential enjoyment collectively reduce uncertainty in cross-border transactions. This work contributes to theory by providing a comprehensive framework for understanding purchase intention formation in livestream commerce. Practically, the findings suggest strategic approaches for personal shoppers and digital platforms to enhance credibility and build consumer trust. latest.title: Beyond Stimulation: A Motivation-Based Segmentation of Coffee Purchasing and Drinking Behaviour
latest.venue: International Review of Management and Marketing
latest.abstract: This study aims to segment Turkish coffee consumers residing in Northern Cyprus by their motivations for coffee consumption and to examine how these segments differ in coffee attributes, information sources, consumption and purchasing behaviours, and socio-demographic characteristics. Data were collected using a structured online questionnaire and purposive sampling between April and June 2025. A total of 649 valid responses were analysed. Exploratory factor analysis was employed to identify underlying motivational dimensions of coffee consumption, followed by hierarchical and K-means cluster analysis to classify consumers into homogeneous segments. Five distinct motivational consumer segments were identified. Chi-square tests and ANOVA results revealed significant differences among these segments in preferred coffee attributes, information sources, consumption occasions, purchasing behaviour, consumption frequency, and socio-demographic characteristics. The findings demonstrated that motivations for coffee consumption in Northern Cyprus are multidimensional and strongly associated with behavioural and demographic profiles. Although coffee consumption has been widely examined in global literature, limited research has addressed it from a motivational segmentation perspective within a Mediterranean cultural context. By providing a comprehensive characterisation of consumer segments, this study contributes to the literature on coffee consumption and purchasing behaviour from a consumer psychology perspective.

latest.title: Social Media Marketing, Personal Selling, and Price Perception on Purchase Decision through Purchase Intention with Experience Environment as a Moderator
latest.venue: International Review of Management and Marketing
latest.abstract: This study examines the influence of social media marketing, personal selling, and price perception on purchase decision, mediated by purchase intention and moderated by experience environment, within the Indonesian residential property sector. Drawing on the Theory of Planned Behavior, Servicescape theory, and the Stimulus-Organism-Response framework, an integrative model is tested using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) and Necessary Condition Analysis (NCA) on data collected from 304 confirmed buyers at CitraLand Tallasa City Makassar. Results confirm that price perception constitutes the dominant predictor of purchase intention, followed by social media marketing, while personal selling yields a non-significant sufficiency-based effect. Purchase intention and experience environment both exert significant direct effects on purchase decision. Purchase intention fully mediates the effects of price perception and social media marketing on purchase decision, whereas the hypothesised moderating role of experience environment is not supported. NCA establishes that all five constructs represent necessary conditions of medium magnitude, with experience environment imposing the most binding prerequisite constraint. The integrated NCA–PLS-SEM approach reveals that achieving superior purchase decision outcomes demands simultaneously adequate performance across all conditions. These findings advance theoretical understanding of high-involvement consumer decision-making and provide actionable guidance for property developers in emerging residential markets.

latest.title: Impact of Packaging Attributes on Brand Love: Evidence from the Luxury Fashion Industry in Egypt
latest.venue: International Review of Management and Marketing
latest.abstract: This study examines the influence of Packaging Attributes on Brand Love in the luxury fashion industry in Egypt, building upon literature on the effect of packaging attributes as a multidimensional concept that extends beyond its protective function to include visual, functional, environmental, and experiential attributes on brand love towards luxury fashion brands. This study is theoretically grounded in the combination of the Cue Utilization Theory, Signaling Theory, and Attachment Theory to examine how packaging attributes shape consumers' emotional responses and strengthen brand love. This research employed a quantitative approach, using an online questionnaire to collect data from 440 luxury fashion consumers via River sampling, and the relationships were analyzed using IBM SPSS Statistics software using Multiple linear regression. Results demonstrated that packaging attributes have significant impact on brand love, with each packaging attribute contributing differently to brand love; thereby, visual, functional, and experiential packaging attributes positively impact brand love, whereas environmental packaging attributes were not a statistically significant predictor of brand love. Findings contribute evidence from the Egyptian market, offering practical implications for luxury fashion brands and marketers, highlighting packaging as a strategic tool to strengthen consumers’ emotional attachment to the brand, and supporting competitiveness in the luxury fashion market.

latest.title: Advancing Digital Banking in Albania: Trust, Financial Literacy and Regulatory Readiness in the FinTech Ecosystem
latest.venue: International Review of Management and Marketing
latest.abstract: Digital transformation is reshaping banking systems worldwide, yet the pace and depth of adoption remain uneven across emerging financial markets. Albania has made visible progress in electronic payments, online banking access and regulatory alignment with European digital finance standards; however, the transition from formal access to sustained digital banking adoption remains incomplete. This study examines the factors influencing digital banking and FinTech adoption in Albania, with a specific focus on consumer trust, financial literacy, perceived barriers and regulatory readiness. The paper applies a mixed-methods research design. Quantitative data were collected through a structured consumer survey with 151 respondents and analyzed through descriptive statistics and Spearman correlation analysis. Qualitative evidence was gathered through 15 semi-structured interviews with representatives from commercial banks, electronic money institutions, public institutions, regulators, sectoral organizations and academic experts. Thematic analysis was used to identify common institutional, technological and regulatory patterns. The findings show that digital banking services are widely accessible, but usage intensity remains moderate. Weekly and monthly use are more common than daily use, while trust, financial knowledge and perceived barriers significantly shape adoption patterns. The correlation analysis indicates a positive relationship between financial knowledge and digital banking use, and a negative relationship between perceived barriers and usage. latest.title: Mindful consumption in a Hyper-connected world: Digital detox as a moderator of consumer behavior
latest.venue: Social Science & Humanities International
latest.abstract: The modern consumer ecosystem is portrayed by constant connectivity, algorithmic personalization, and digital action among various platforms. Although digital technologies have transmuted consumer involvements by cumulative convenience, information availability, and personalized communications, hyper-connectivity has instantaneously contributed to cognitive burden, compulsive consumption pattern, digital exhaustion, and reduced cognizant decision-making. In these circumstances, mindful consumption has surfaced as an essential context for understanding intentional and value-driven consumption behaviors. Mindful consumption lays emphasis on perception, intentional, and importance of the broader consequences of consumption decisions on individuals, society, and the environment. Contemporary research implies that consumers gradually obtain profound and stable consumption experiences that associate with psychological well-being and sustainability goals [1]. Digital detox, defined as the intended decline or temporary detachment from digital devices and social media platforms, has obtained attention as a behavioral intrusion capable of rebuilding cognitive and emotional equilibrium. Evolving evidence reveals that digital detox practices can enhance psychological well-being, lower information overload, and boost self-regulation among consumers [2]. This chapter observes the association linking mindful consumption and consumer behavior in a hyper-connected environment and intends digital detox as a moderating mechanism that controls consumer decision-making processes. Particularly, the chapter investigates how decreased digital exposure can modify impulsive purchasing trends, boost conscious assessment of consumption substitutes, and stimulate sustainable behavioral consequences

latest.title: Customer Focus Program (CFP) in a Regulation-Constrained Category: A Field-Based Qualitative Study of Distribution and Merchandising Execution in India's Organized Cigarette Trade
latest.venue: International Journal of Creative and Open Research in Engineering and Management
latest.abstract: Purpose: In categories where mass advertising and open promotion are legally prohibited, the sales and distribution system becomes the main route through which a firm can express customer orientation. This paper examines how a Customer Focus Program (CFC) operates at the point of sale in the cigarette sales and distribution network of a large Indian fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) organisation. Design/methodology/approach: The study is a descriptive, qualitative, field-observation-based case study conducted over a two-month period (15 May to 15 July 2026) in the Sambhajinagar (Aurangabad) territory of Maharashtra. Observations were recorded during accompanied market visits across convenience, grocery, wholesale, sub-wholesale, stockist, moped and van direct-selling channels, using a four-field recording format (objective, activity observed, practical observation, relevance to customer focus). Observations were mapped to an Availability–Visibility–Freshness (AVF) framework and to an eight-step CFC field-execution flow. Findings: Four findings emerge. (1) Availability is produced by layered, complementary coverage formats rather than by any single actor. (2) Effective execution must be segment-aware and margin-aware, because retailers' stocking and promotion choices respond jointly to product segment and trade pricing structure. (3) Merchandising and planogram discipline is the primary visibility lever when above-the-line promotion is unavailable. (4) The salesman–retailer relationship is the mechanism that sustains the program. Originality/value: The paper offers a field-grounded account of customer orientation as enacted at the last mile in a heavily regulated category, an area where the marketing-channels and customer-orientation literatures rarely meet. The Influence of Membership Programs and Application Ease of Use on Consumer Purchasing Decisions in Modern Retail
latest.venue: International Journal of Integrated Science and Technology
latest.abstract: This study aims to analyze the influence of membership programs and application ease of use on consumer purchasing decisions in modern retail. The subjects of this study were consumers using the membership application at Indomaret in Tangerang. A quantitative approach was employed using purposive sampling with 100 respondents. Data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares (PLS) with SmartPLS version 4.1.1.8. The results indicate that, partially, the membership program does not have a significant effect on consumer purchasing decisions, while application ease of use has a positive and significant effect. These findings indicate that although membership provides various benefits, consumers may consider other factors such as price, needs, store location, product quality, and direct promotions when making purchases. Meanwhile, an application that is easy to learn, understand, operate, flexible, and practical can facilitate the purchasing process and support consumer purchasing decisions.

latest.title: LOW-PURCHASE LONG-STAY BEHAVIOUR AT ZUS COFFEE: CROWDING, FAIRNESS AND REVISIT INTENTION
latest.venue: Quantum Journal of Social Sciences and Humanities
latest.abstract: This study examines how low-purchase long-stay behaviour influences customer experience in urban coffee chains, using ZUS Coffee customers in Malaysia as the research context. As cafés increasingly function as informal work, study and social spaces, customers who purchase minimally but occupy seats for extended periods may affect other customers’ perceptions of crowding, service fairness, satisfaction and revisit intention. Drawing on servicescape, perceived crowding and service fairness perspectives, this study develops a conceptual model linking low-purchase long-stay behaviour to perceived crowding, perceived service fairness, customer satisfaction and revisit intention. A quantitative survey design is proposed among ZUS Coffee customers who have recently visited physical outlets in Malaysia. The study contributes to consumer behaviour and service management literature by examining café space consumption as part of the customer experience. The findings are expected to provide practical implications for coffee chain operators in managing seating, customer comfort and fairness without weakening the café’s role as a flexible third place.

latest.title: The Influence of TikTok Social media marketing and Service Quality on Purchase Decisions at De.u Coffee Dago
latest.venue: International Journal of Managemen Analytics (IJMA)
latest.abstract: The growth of coffee shop businesses in Indonesia shows a significant trend in line with the lifestyle changes of urban communities, where coffee shops have increasingly become places for socializing, working, or simply relaxing. One widely used strategy is social media marketing, particularly through TikTok, which is currently popular across various demographics. This study aims to examine the influence of TikTok social media marketing and service quality on consumer purchase decisions at De.u Coffee Dago. The research method employed is quantitative, with data collected through questionnaires distributed to 100 respondents. Data analysis was conducted using multiple linear regression tests. The results indicate that TikTok social media marketing has a significant effect on purchase decisions with a significance value of 0.000 (<0.05). Similarly, service quality also has a significant effect on purchase decisions with a significance value of 0.000 (<0.05). Simultaneously, both independent variables contribute 63.9% to purchase decisions, while the remaining 36.1% is influenced by other factors outside this study. These findings highlight the importance of digital marketing strategies through TikTok and the implementation of optimal service quality in enhancing consumer purchase interest. The benefits of this research not only provide academic insights into consumer behavior but also serve as a practical reference for coffee shop businesses in designing effective marketing strategies and maintaining service quality to increase consumer loyalty.

latest.title: Analyzing the Impact of Product Quality, Brand Image, and Location on Consumer Purchase Decisions: Evidence from Tepian Kopi Semarang, Indonesia
latest.venue: Mabsya Jurnal Manajemen Bisnis Syariah
latest.abstract: This study aims to analyse the influence of product quality, brand image, and location on consumer purchase decisions at Tepian Kopi Coffee Shop in Semarang, Indonesia. A quantitative survey approach was employed, with 103 respondents selected through purposive sampling based on the criteria of being at least 17 years old and having made a purchase within the previous six months. Data were collected through a structured questionnaire and analysed using multiple linear regression with SPSS version 26. The results indicate that product quality (t = 2.167; sig. = 0.033), brand image (t = 2.868; sig. = 0.005), and location (t = 4.852; sig. = 0.000) all have a positive and significant effect on purchase decisions. Location contributes the strongest relative effect, with a standardised beta coefficient of 0.426, compared to brand image (0.250) and product quality (0.199). The F-test confirms that the three variables simultaneously influence purchase decisions (F = 44.023; sig. = 0.000), while the adjusted R² of 0.559 indicates that 55.9% of the variance in purchase decisions is explained by the model. These findings suggest that location advantages serve as the most immediate source of competitive advantage for local coffee shops competing against larger chains. Managers are advised to prioritise location enhancement, brand experience consistency, and product quality reinforcement, while future research may incorporate additional variables such as price, promotion, and store atmosphere.

latest.title: Influence of Perceived Brand Image on Students’ Choice of Health and Allied Sciences Colleges in Tanzania: A Case of Selected Colleges in Mwanza City
latest.venue: East African Journal of Business and Economics
latest.abstract: The study investigated the influence of perceived brand image on students' choice of health and allied sciences colleges in Tanzania, focusing on selected colleges in Mwanza City. The study was guided by Brand Equity Theory to examine the influence of brand awareness, perceived quality, and brand association on students’ choice. A quantitative approach and cross-sectional design were used. The study targeted 1,993 undergraduate students, of whom 333 respondents were selected through stratified random sampling. A total of 320 questionnaires were successfully returned and analysed using SPSS version 26. Descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, and multiple linear regression analysis were employed to analyse quantitative data. The findings showed that perceived brand image had a positive and statistically significant influence on students’ choice of Health and Allied Sciences Colleges. Perceived quality had the strongest positive effect, with β = 0.352 and p = 0.001. Brand awareness had a positive significant effect on students’ choice, with β = 0.286 and p = 0.000. Brand association also had a positive significant effect, with β = 0.271 and p = 0.000. The model explained 62.3% of the variation in students’ choice, as shown by R Square = 0.623. The study concluded that students’ choice of Health and Allied Sciences Colleges was influenced by institutional awareness, perceived quality, and association. The study recommended that Health and Allied Sciences Colleges should strengthen institutional visibility, improve academic and clinical training quality, and build strong positive associations to attract students and strengthen marketing strategies.

latest.title: How Collaborative Marketing Communications and Aesthetic Design Influence Purchase Intention: The Sequential Mediating Roles of Nostalgic Emotion and Brand Love
latest.venue: Journal of Promotion Management
latest.abstract: This study investigates how aesthetic design and collaborative marketing shape consumer purchase intention through emotional and relational mechanisms in an emerging market setting. Drawing on the Stimulus–Organism–Response (S-O-R) framework, the study develops and tests a moderated serial mediation model in which nostalgic emotion and brand love explain how marketing stimuli translate into behavioral outcomes. Data were collected from 326 Generation Y female consumers in Thailand and analyzed using structural equation modeling and conditional process analysis. The findings reveal that both aesthetic design and collaborative marketing positively influence nostalgic emotion, which subsequently strengthens brand love and enhances purchase intention. Brand love further emerges as a significant predictor of purchase intention, highlighting the importance of emotional attachment in consumer decision-making. Furthermore, aesthetic sensory consumption was found to moderate selected relationships within the proposed model rather than all structural paths, indicating that its influence is context dependent. However, although the sequential indirect effects through nostalgic emotion and brand love were significant at specific levels of aesthetic sensory consumption, pairwise comparisons revealed no significant differences across these levels. Thus, the hypothesized moderated sequential indirect effects were not supported. This study extends promotion management research by explaining how aesthetic design and collaborative marketing function as complementary promotional mechanisms that stimulate nostalgic emotion, strengthen brand love, and enhance purchase intention, while identifying aesthetic sensory consumption as a selective boundary condition rather than a uniform moderator

latest.title: Discursive Institutional Work and the Social Control of Dangerous Objects
latest.venue: Journal of Business Ethics
latest.abstract: Abstract Across societies and over time, the social control of objects deemed “dangerous”—i.e., as threats to public order, morality, or physical and psychological well-being—varies, from regulation to prohibition, with implications for responsibility, potential harm, and affected communities. Drawing on U.S. Congressional hearings on the issue of cannabis regulation and prohibition (1906–1951), we examine how shifts in social control track changing configurations of discursive institutional work. Our work demonstrates how configurations of rationalization, moralization, and syncretization shaped the meaning of cannabis as a dangerous object: rationalization calculates the risk, supporting calibrated regulation; moralization absolutizes the danger, promoting prohibition; and syncretization balances these two. We refer to this reciprocal dynamic as an epistemic ratchet, whereby rationalization and moralization each weaken the epistemic foundations of the alternative regime, making movement between regulation and prohibition difficult in either direction. Our study makes three contributions: (a) it extends the organizing-of-risk account of how danger is rendered governable to the form and reversibility of control; (b) it adds to research on discursive institutional work by identifying epistemology, complexity, and responsibility as the object-level qualities through which discourse becomes consequential for governance; and (c) it contributes to debates on responsibility, ethics, and harm by showing how the discursive redistribution of responsibility shapes the scope and coerciveness of control.

latest.title: Responsible communication in sustainable fashion: a mixed-methods neuromarketing study of young consumers
latest.venue: Sustainable Futures
latest.abstract: Sustainable fashion claims are communicated through labels, visual cues, traceability signals, and brand narratives that shape how consumers interpret responsibility, credibility, and product value. Their effectiveness is nevertheless constrained when sustainability information competes with aesthetic and functional product cues or when claims are perceived as vague or weakly substantiated. This study examines how young consumers process sustainable fashion claims and how visual attention, emotional response, and perceived credibility contribute to that process. Using a mixed-methods neuromarketing design, the study combines a pretest (N = 22), face-coding (N = 30), eye-tracking (N = 31), and focus groups (N = 20) with consumers aged 18–25 in Bogotá, Colombia. Each component was analysed at the method-specific level and the findings were subsequently integrated through triangulation. Results show that product and perceptual cues capture initial attention, whereas sustainability information receives greater engagement when it is visually integrated and connected to functional product value. Facial-expression analysis indicates that sadness was the most prominent average emotional category across the stimuli examined. Qualitative evidence further suggests that, within this study, socially framed sustainability messages were perceived as more concrete and emotionally accessible than more abstract environmental claims. Across methods, claim credibility and perceived congruence with the product emerged as important conditions in the interpretation of sustainability communication. By integrating attentional, affective, and interpretive evidence, the study advances understanding of how sustainability claims are processed without assuming direct effects on purchase behaviour. T

latest.title: From Free to Paid: Public Attitude Change and Mechanism Evidence around Doubao's Charging Announcement
latest.venue: Media studies.
latest.abstract: As generative AI moves from free access to paid subscription, how charging shapes public attitude bears on platform commercialization. Taking Doubao's monthly subscription as the setting, this paper builds a dual-path framework of “product experience - price perception”. Using the announcement date (May 4, 2026) as the breakpoint, we collect public Weibo discussions from 30 days before to 30 days after it (2-day periods; the 14 days on each side form the main window), measure attitude with aspect-based sentiment analysis, and test changes at the breakpoint by regression discontinuity in time. Negative evaluation is robust in direction for Payment Willingness (τ = +0.751, p < 0.001) and Corporate Brand (τ = +0.647, p = 0.011), but rests on only 27 and 7 pre-breakpoint texts, so the magnitudes are read as direction only. The negative share for Price & Charging shows no significant increase (τ = -0.161, p = 0.123), so the price-fairness path is not supported. The difference between the two aspect jumps is -0.532 (clustered SE 0.437, p = 0.245), opposite to expectation and underpowered given the small pre-breakpoint sample; we report only that no larger negative change was found for the price path than for the feature path. The overall negative share rises by 0.317 (p = 0.041) but depends on a pre-breakpoint period with 3 relevant texts and falls to 0.043 (p = 0.517) without it, so it is not robustly supported. The conclusions are limited to a marked change in attitude, with no persistent shift and no strict causal claim.

latest.title: The impact of ai recommendation systems on impulsive buying behaviour in electronic marketplaces: The mediating moderating role of fear of missing out
latest.venue: International Journal of Informatics and Communication Technology (IJ-ICT)
latest.abstract: Artificial intelligence has spread rapidly across e-commerce, and in doing so it has reshaped how consumers reach purchase decisions. Scholarship to date concentrates mainly on what shoppers gain from algorithmic recommenders, whereas far fewer studies ask whether such systems also push buyers toward unplanned spending. The present work therefore tests how perceived attributes of AI recommendation engines relate to impulsive buying, treating fear of missing out (FOMO) simultaneously as an intervening variable and as a boundary condition. Survey evidence was gathered from 823 Vietnamese shoppers who regularly transact on AI-enabled marketplaces. Results show impulsive purchasing rising together with perceived AI authority, perceived task complexity, and with perceived personalization. FOMO carries a significant portion of each effect and, at the same time, amplifies its magnitude. These outcomes ground several managerial recommendations for platforms seeking to reconcile recommender deployment with responsible consumer conduct.

latest.title: BEYOND THE SCROLL: HOW MARKETING TURNS ATTENTION INTO TRUST
latest.venue: Middle European Scientific Bulletin
latest.abstract: The article examines how consumer attention on social media can be transformed into brand trust, laying the groundwork for lasting customer relationships. Amid information overload and competition for users’ attention, it explores marketing communication approaches that combine engaging content, practical value, and relevance to audience expectations. The article aims to explain how content and consistent consumer interaction contribute to brand trust and the transition from initial interest to a purchase decision.Particular attention is paid to the content and communication factors that sustain audience interest after the first encounter with a brand’s post. These include useful and credible messages, transparent offers, consistency between brand promises and customer experience, and timely responses to questions and feedback. The article discusses the role of social proof, including reviews, recommendations, and user-generated content, in reducing uncertainty when choosing products or services. It also stresses the need to assess such materials critically and avoid manipulative communication practices.The article further considers approaches to evaluating marketing communication effectiveness. It distinguishes reach and engagement metrics from indicators related to inquiries, conversions, repeat purchases, and customer retention. Views and reactions alone provide insufficient grounds for conclusions about trust or commercial outcomes. The practical value of the article lies in outlining principles for content creation and customer interaction that support stronger brand–consumer relationships. latest.title: Determinants of Sustainable Fast Fashion Purchase Intention Among Generation Z Consumers
latest.venue: Cureus Journal of Business and Economics.
latest.abstract: The increasing environmental concerns associated with the fast fashion industry have intensified the need to understand the factors that encourage sustainable consumption, particularly among Generation Z, one of the largest and most influential consumer segments.This study examines the determinants of purchase intention towards sustainable fast fashion by investigating the effects of sustainability awareness, perceived green value, social influence, fashion involvement, and sustainability attitude.Drawing on the Theory of Planned Behaviour and the Value-Attitude-Behaviour framework, a conceptual model was developed and empirically tested using survey data collected from 1,000 Generation Z consumers in the Mumbai Metropolitan Region, India.The measurement model was validated through reliability analysis, exploratory factor analysis, and confirmatory factor analysis, while the proposed hypotheses were tested using structural equation modelling with the diagonally weighted least squares estimation method.The findings reveal that all five constructs significantly and positively influence purchase intention towards sustainable fast fashion.Sustainability attitude emerged as the strongest predictor (β = 0.351), followed by social influence (β = 0.303), sustainability awareness (β = 0.280), green perceived value (β = 0.252), and fashion involvement (β = 0.222).The model demonstrated excellent goodness of fit (comparative fit index = 0.991; Tucker-Lewis index = 0.989; root mean square error of approximation = 0.031), confirming the robustness of the proposed framework.The study contributes to the sustainable fashion literature by integrating cognitive, social, evaluative, and attitudinal factors into a comprehensive behavioural model that explains the transition from sustainabi

latest.title: The role of crowding and decision comfort during sales periods
latest.venue: Management Decision
latest.abstract: Purpose Sales periods simultaneously attract consumers through price reductions and trigger avoidance behaviors: a paradox this study addresses by examining decision comfort as a potential mediator of the effects of human and spatial crowding on visit postponement and store-switching. Gender is also examined as a moderator of these relationships. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative approach was adopted, with data collected from 378 consumers in France during official sales periods across several retail locations. The conceptual model was tested using structural equation modeling (SEM) to examine relationships among perceived crowding, decision comfort, visit postponement, and store-switching. Multi-group analysis assessed gender differences. Findings Both human and spatial crowding were negatively associated with decision comfort. Lower decision comfort was associated with higher levels of visit postponement and, less robustly, with store-switching. The indirect effect of spatial crowding on visit postponement through decision comfort was supported; the indirect effects of human crowding on both avoidance behaviors were also supported but modest in magnitude, whereas the indirect effect of spatial crowding on store-switching was not supported. Gender differences were detected in the crowding–decision comfort relationships, whereas no gender differences were detected in the decision comfort–avoidance paths. Originality/value This research contributes to the marketing literature by showing that the mediating role of decision comfort depends on the form of crowding and the avoidance response considered. It extends the application of decision comfort as an emerging construct in the retail context, offering new insights into how crowding shapes consumer decision-makin

latest.title: Ex-Ante Regulation of Systemically Significant Digital Enterprises: A Legal Appraisal of India's Draft Digital Competition Bill vs. the EU's Digital Markets Act
latest.venue: International Journal of Law Management & Humanities
latest.abstract: As platform economies grow increasingly concentrated, competition law struggles to keep pace with the emergence of ‘Big Tech’ companies. Traditional ex-post enforcement measures are increasingly seen by regulators worldwide as too slow. This paper presents a legal appraisal of India’s draft Digital Competition Bill, focusing on its proposals for identifying Systemically Significant Digital Enterprises within the country’s digital market, and compares it with the European Union’s Digital Markets Act, 2022. Both frameworks adopt a proactive, forward-looking approach to controlling anti-competitive conduct by major technology firms. Still, the analysis reveals significant differences between the two in the designation of companies, the obligations imposed on them, and the rules of enforcement, differences that reflect distinct economic priorities. The European Union framework targets gatekeepers, that is, large technology platforms that control crucial online services, on the basis of their market position and the risk of anti-competitive behaviour, whereas India’s Digital Competition Bill focuses on preventing broader harms to the digital ecosystem. The paper suggests that although the Competition Act can deal effectively with unfair practices, a more flexible, rule-based regulatory framework would better equip authorities to handle market unpredictability, legal challenges and procedural delays, ultimately fostering fairer competition. It concludes with a series of recommendations aimed at strengthening the design of India’s digital competition framework.

latest.title: 云南咖啡商标与地理标志协同机制
latest.venue: 亚太社会科学
latest.abstract: 为明确云南咖啡面向东南亚市场时企业商标与地理标志协同运用的条件，基于声誉、集体行动和全球价值链治理理论，采用整合性综述方法，对消费者评价、质量行为及收益分配证据进行比较与主题归纳。研究表明，标识协同包括信息互补与治理互补，分别取决于新增产地信息的购买相关性及共同规范与企业责任的衔接；消费者估价、交易成交和生产者净回报处于不同环节，组织服务、渠道控制与成本分担影响收益传递。据此提出境外权利衔接、质量责任落实、市场信息转化和成本收益协调四项条件及相应研究命题。云南咖啡应将标识运用落实到具体交易，在原料采购中衔接验收与结算，在终端销售中检验信息增量，在跨境加工中明确用标权限与责任。

latest.title: To What Extent Does the Layout of a Departmental Store Affect Consumer Decision Fatigue?
latest.venue: Reinvention an International Journal of Undergraduate Research
latest.abstract: A departmental store layout and product placement shape the consumer decision-making process. This paper begins by charting the psychological flow of decision making and identifying the critical points that lead to decision fatigue, a cognitive stage where repeated or complex choices exhaust mental resources and lead to suboptimal decisions. This paper further aims to provide a nuanced understanding of how the retail environment of a department store influences consumer behaviour and cognitive load. Three types of store layouts are analysed: free form, grid and racetrack. A free-form layout allows the consumer to explore products and integrates various departments together for higher sales; this configuration causes comparatively high levels of decision fatigue among consumers as it encourages browsing and they are left to navigate products by themselves. A grid layout eases the navigation process by arranging aisles in a parallel structure. However, retailers can achieve the best shopping experience with low levels of decision fatigue among shoppers by implementing a racetrack layout, which not only reduces the need for consumers to decide their path but also reduces cognitive overload by guiding the consumer along one main aisle.

latest.title: Comparative Financial and Strategic Analysis of Selected Companies in the Indian Auto (Four-Wheeler) Sector
latest.venue: International Journal of Creative and Open Research in Engineering and Management
latest.abstract: The Indian four-wheeler automobile sector is among the largest in the world and is being reshaped by sport utility vehicle (SUV) demand, electrification, connected technologies and tighter regulation. This study presents a comparative financial and strategic analysis of five leading listed companies: Maruti Suzuki India Limited, Mahindra & Mahindra Limited, Hyundai Motor India Limited, Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles and Ashok Leyland Limited. A descriptive, secondary-data research design was adopted. Company reports, investor presentations, exchange filings, industry publications and government sources were used to build company profiles and to compute and compare revenue, net profit, market capitalisation, earnings per share, return on equity, return on capital employed, debt–equity ratio, current ratio, net profit margin and five-year passenger vehicle market share. Strategic tools, namely PESTEL, Porter’s Five Forces and SWOT analysis, were used to interpret the financial evidence. The results show that Maruti Suzuki combines market leadership, the highest market valuation among the five firms, negligible debt and a strong distribution network, although its passenger vehicle share has eased from 47% to about 41% over five years. Mahindra & Mahindra records the largest revenue and net profit among the firms with comparable data and the fastest share gain, rising from 7% to 14%. Hyundai Motor India delivers the highest return on capital employed (38.4%) with very low leverage, while Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles leads electric mobility but shows weak liquidity and capital-efficiency indicators. latest.title: Determining Household Savings Preferences: The Case of Türkiye
latest.venue: Namık Kemal Üniversitesi Sosyal Bilimler Meslek Yüksek Okulu Dergisi
latest.abstract: This study examines the socio-demographic factors that influence household saving preferences in Türkiye. A multinomial logit model was used to analyse data from 3354 households with complete information in the Turkish Statistical Institute’s 2020 Household Budget Survey micro-dataset. Savings preferences were categorized into four groups: real estate, gold/foreign currency, bank accounts, and capital market instruments. The findings suggest that families with children are more likely to prefer real estate and capital market instruments, while families without children are less likely to choose gold or foreign currency and bank accounts. Spending amount did not significantly affect preferences for real estate or gold/foreign currency but increased the likelihood of choosing a bank account and decreased the likelihood of choosing capital market instruments. Tenants were more likely to prefer gold, foreign currency, bank accounts, and capital market instruments, while homeowners tended to prefer real estate. Those with private insurance preferred capital market instruments, while those without preferred real estate, gold, foreign currency, and bank accounts. As household size increased, the likelihood of choosing real estate or gold/foreign currency increased, while the likelihood of having a bank account decreased. These results are informative for policymakers.

latest.title: Sustainable consumption: The moderating role of perceived inconvenience and trust
latest.venue: European Journal of Sustainable Development Research
latest.abstract: Sustainable purchasing represents one of the most tangible manifestations of sustainable consumption. This study applies the Stimulus–Organism–Response (SOR) and Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) frameworks to examine the moderating roles of perceived inconvenience and trust in the relationship between sustainable purchase intention and sustainable purchase behavior. It also investigates the moderating effect of perceived inconvenience on the relationships between contextual stimuli and organism factors (emotional value and social value). A quantitative research approach was employed to collect data from 398 consumers in Ho Chi Minh City and Da Nang, Vietnam, who had purchased sustainable products. The structural equation model was analyzed using SmartPLS 4. The results indicate that both individual and contextual factors positively influence emotional value and social value, which, in turn, enhance sustainable purchase intention and sustainable purchase behavior. Furthermore, the moderating effects of perceived inconvenience and trust are statistically supported. These findings provide business managers and marketers with deeper insights into consumers’ sustainable purchasing behavior and offer practical implications for promoting sustainable consumption.

latest.title: Spatial optimization of vaccine supply networks in complex terrains: balancing economic feasibility and public health equity
latest.venue: Frontiers in Public Health
latest.abstract: Background Vaccine supply planning in hazard-prone terrains faces compounding geographic, socioeconomic, and operational barriers. Conventional models relying on planar distances and static metrics often fail to capture true accessibility disparities, often driving inefficient infrastructure allocation and exacerbating health inequities. Purpose This study develops an integrated decision-making framework coupling spatial equity, economic feasibility, and multi-scenario resilience to systematically reconfigure the vaccine supply network across 183 counties in Sichuan, China. Methods Using high-resolution road network data from the AMap Application Programming Interface (API), we model actual geographic impedance based on travel time. An adapted two-step floating catchment area (2SFCA) method, embedded with socioeconomic vulnerability indicators, pinpoints baseline accessibility disparities. Candidate hubs are selected via entropy-weighted Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS) combined with spatial-equity quotas, and a candidate-pool capacity-sufficiency check (α coefficient) determines the final candidate-pool size. A multi-objective mixed-integer linear programming (MO-MILP) model then co-optimizes hub configuration, capacity scaling, and cross-regional dispatch, endogenously balancing operational efficiency, equity penalties, and capacity expansion costs. Results Under entropy-weighted TOPSIS ranking with spatial-equity quotas, the initial 61-hub pool (including 21 existing CDC anchors) provides aggregate capacity equal to 82% of total demand. latest.title: Deep Learning-Driven Consumer Intelligence: Predictive Modeling of Customer Behavior for Data-Centric Marketing Decisions
latest.venue: Computer and decision making.
latest.abstract: Consumer-intelligence architecture that can predict the purchase behavior of customers based on e-commerce interaction data and aid data-driven marketing decision making in a large-scale environment. It was done with 455,401 labeled consumer observations, including 25 variables that encompass browsing, basket, checkout, delivery, account, device and other behavioral interactions. The conventional machine-learning models, such as logistic regression, random forest, and XGBoost were compared with the deep neural network and 1-D convolutional neural network models. The results showed high class imbalance, where purchases only accounted for 4.19% of observations. However, models produced high model discrimination. Random forest had the highest precision-recall AUC of 0.906 and logistic regression had the highest F1-score of 0.926, while XGBoost had a recall of 0.987. Check out viewing and checking out details were the most significant factors in purchase propensity. The results illustrate the effectiveness of behavioral consumer intelligence in predicting purchase intent and in assisting customer prioritization, personal targeting, remarketing, conversion optimization and efficient marketing resource allocation, and indicate that more complex models can be as successful as simpler ones in predicting consumer behavior.

latest.title: Reconstructing Consumer Protection Against Dark Patterns in Indonesian E-Commerce Law
latest.venue: Legalis Journal of Law Review
latest.abstract: The expansion of electronic commerce has shifted consumer risk from conventional misinformation toward manipulation of the digital decision-making environment. This study examines whether Indonesian law adequately addresses dark patterns and develops a legally operational reconstruction model. The study's distinctive contribution is not merely the recognition of dark patterns, which has already been discussed in Indonesian scholarship, but the formulation of a four-part regulatory architecture that connects (i) an effect-based legal definition of dark patterns, (ii) fair digital interface duties, (iii) meaningful consent standards, and (iv) behavioural accountability of electronic-system and platform providers, together with a defined allocation of legislative, administrative, and remedial functions. The normative analysis covers Law No. 8 of 1999 on Consumer Protection, the Civil Code, Law No. 1 of 2024 amending the Electronic Information and Transactions Law, Law No. 27 of 2022 on Personal Data Protection, Government Regulation No. 71 of 2019, Government Regulation No. 80 of 2019, and the current Minister of Trade Regulation No. 19 of 2026 on Electronic Commerce. Comparative analysis examines the European Union, the United States, the United Kingdom, and Singapore through common functional criteria: recognition of manipulative conduct, consent standard, interface obligations, platform responsibility, enforcement authority, and remedies. The findings show that Indonesian law can indirectly reach several dark-pattern practices through information, good-faith, contract, consumer-protection, and data-protection norms, but it lacks an explicit cross-cutting standard for manipulative choice architecture and a coordinated enforcement pathway. latest.title: The Effect of Niche Perfume Selection Attributes on the Consume Happiness: The Moderating Effect of Generation through Multi-Group Analysis
latest.venue: Journal of the Korean Society of Cosmetology
latest.abstract: Niche perfume has emerged as a mainstream segment of the perfume market, moving beyond mass-market offerings by reflecting Millennials and Generation Z’s strong preference for individuality and distinctive scent identities. This study aims to analyze the effects of niche perfume selection attributes on consumer happiness. In addition, Millennials and Generation Z are proposed as a moderator affecting the niche perfume selection attributes on consumer happiness. An online survey targeted Korean women from Millennials and Generation Z who have experience using niche perfume. A total of 296 survey responses were analyzed using structural equation modeling with AMOS 26.0 and SPSS 25.0. The results revealed that four key selection attributes emerged from the analysis: trend orientation, brand awareness, premium price perception, and scent. In addition, scent, brand awareness, and premium price perception had significant effects on consumer happiness. Furthermore, the moderating effect of generation was confirmed through multi-group analysis. Specifically, Among Millennials, trend orientation, brand awareness, and premium price perception influenced consumer happiness, whereas scent was the most influential factor among Generation Z. By identifying these causal relationships, this study contributes to expanding the advancement of research on niche perfume and provides implications for developing differentiated strategies tailored to generational characteristics of the Millennials and Generation Z.

latest.title: The Relationship Between Perceived Value of Beauty Curation Commerce and Consumer Behavior: The Mediating Effect of Brand Awareness
latest.venue: Journal of the Korean Society of Cosmetology
latest.abstract: This study systematically investigates the structural relationships between the perceived value dimensions (convenience, choice, and customization) of beauty curation commerce and consumer behavior (purchase and recommendation intentions), while examining the mediating mechanism of brand awareness. Empirical data were collected from 320 adult consumers with actual experience in beauty curation commerce and analyzed using SPSS 25.0 software to perform frequency, factor, reliability, correlation, and multi-step regression analyses. The results indicate that convenience, choice, and customization significantly enhance brand awareness, with customization identified as the primary determinant. In terms of direct influence on consumer behavior, customization and convenience positively affect both purchase and recommendation intentions, whereas choice options yield no statistically significant direct impact. Furthermore, brand awareness acts as a critical cognitive bridge, partially mediating the relationship between convenience/customization and consumer behavior, while fully mediating the relationship between choice option and consumer behavior. Academically, this research demonstrates that reducing cognitive search fatigue through convenience and personalized curation is far more effective than simply expanding product variety. Practically, beauty platform marketers must pivot from traditional inventory-listing strategies to ultra-personalized solutions, such as AI-driven skin diagnostics and streamlined purchasing interfaces, to build brand equity and cultivate long-term customer relationships, thereby securing a sustainable competitive advantage in the rapidly evolving beauty tech industry.

latest.title: Green strategy and firm performance: The mediating role of competitive advantage in emerging economy SMEs
latest.venue: Innovative Marketing
latest.abstract: Type of the article: Research ArticleAbstractSustainability transitions are a strategic imperative for SMEs in emerging economies, where institutional and resource constraints limit the direct translation of environmental strategies into performance outcomes. This study explores how green marketing and eco-innovation are associated with business performance through competitive advantage. Data were collected through a quantitative cross-sectional survey, yielding 474 valid questionnaires from owners, managers, and specialists of Vietnamese SMEs in the consumer goods sector. Environmental regulation strengthens the green marketing–competitive advantage relationship, and customer green awareness and market dynamics positively moderate the competitive advantage–performance relationship. The findings showed positive associations of eco-innovation (β = .597, p < .001) and green marketing (β = .230, p < .001) with competitive advantage, which was positively associated with business performance (β = .461, p < .001). The corresponding indirect effects through competitive advantage were significant (β = .275 and .106, respectively; both p < .001), while environmental regulation (β = .164), customer green awareness (β = .083), and market dynamics (β = .091) showed positive moderating effects. The cross-sectional design, non-probability sampling, and industry-specific focus may limit this study’s scope and generalizability in broader contexts. This study advances the sustainability and strategic management literature by providing a mechanism-based account of how environmental strategy, when extended from the Natural Resource-Based View and translated into competitive positioning, generates economic gains for SMEs in resource-constrained emerging economies.AcknowledgmentsThis articl

latest.title: Ambient lighting and basket construction in an immersive supermarket
latest.venue: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
latest.abstract: Retailers use store atmospherics to influence how shoppers construct baskets, yet isolating and testing atmospheric effects in operating stores is costly and difficult to standardize. Across two studies, this research examines whether an ambient lighting configuration alters basket size. Study 1 used an immersive virtual reality supermarket and showed that bright (vs. dim) lighting increased basket size and raised the basket-level Nutri-Score total, with no reliable difference in average Nutri-Score per item. Study 2 conceptually replicated the basket-size effect in a larger online sample using video and product images from the same virtual supermarket. Bright lighting again increased basket size but neither the basket-level Nutri-Score total nor average Nutri-Score per item differed reliably. Across both studies, bright lighting increased how many products shoppers selected without reliable evidence that the average selected product had a less favorable Nutri-Score. Together, the studies show that a digitally rendered ambient lighting configuration can affect basket size across two virtual-store implementations. Virtual supermarkets can therefore serve as controlled testbeds for early-stage evaluation of programmable atmospherics and basket-level outcomes.

latest.title: Algılanan Satın Alma Engellerinin Çevrimiçi İkinci El Giysi Satın Alma Niyetindeki Rolü
latest.venue: Bucak İşletme Fakültesi Dergisi
latest.abstract: Bu çalışma, Türkiye’deki tüketicilerin çevrimiçi ikinci el giysi pazarındaki satın alma engellerine yönelik algılarını belirlemeyi ve bu engellerin satın alma niyeti üzerindeki rolünü ortaya koymayı amaçlamaktadır. Çalışmada öncelikle ikinci el giysi tüketimi ve çevrimiçi ikinci el tüketim literatüründe tanımlanan farklı engel boyutlarından yola çıkılarak, çevrimiçi ikinci el giysi tüketimine özgü engellere ait bir çerçeve oluşturulmuştur. Çalışmada hem çevrimiçi bağlamı hem de giysi kategorisinin yapısal özelliklerini dikkate alan kontaminasyon etkisi, ürünün düşük güvenilirliği, zaman ve çaba, aşınma ve yıpranma, utanç ve çevrimiçi mağazalara yönelik güven eksikliği olmak üzere altı temel engel boyutundan oluşan bu çerçeveden yararlanılmıştır. Ardından çalışmanın amacı doğrultusunda çevrimiçi anket yöntemiyle 18 yaş ve üzeri 397 katılımcıdan elde edilen veriler, çoklu regresyon analizi kullanılarak sınanmıştır. Bulgular, çevrimiçi ikinci el giysi satın alma niyetinin özellikle kontaminasyon etkisi, aşınma ve yıpranma ile çevrimiçi mağazalara yönelik güven eksikliği algıları ile aralarında anlamlı ve negatif yönlü ilişkiler bulunduğunu göstermektedir. Buna karşılık, zaman ve çaba ile ürünün düşük güvenilirliğine ilişkin algılar görece yüksek düzeyde olmasına rağmen, bu değişkenler ile çevrimiçi ikinci el giysi satın alma niyeti arasında istatistiksel olarak anlamlı bir ilişki bulunmadığı tespit edilmiştir. Araştırma sonuçları, çevrimiçi ikinci el platformlarının güven inşası ve ürün bilgisi şeffaflığına yönelik stratejiler geliştirmesinin, Türkiye’de ikinci el giysi tüketiminin yaygınlaşmasına katkı sağlayabileceğini ortaya koymaktadır. latest.title: ЦИФРОВА МОНЕТИЗАЦІЯ МІЖНАРОДНОЇ ТОРГІВЛІ КРІЗЬ ПРИЗМУ СПОЖИВЧИХ РІШЕНЬ
latest.venue: Підприємництво та інновації
latest.abstract: Стаття присвячена дослідженню механізмів цифрової монетизації міжнародної торгівлі та їх впливу на споживчі рішення в умовах розвитку цифрових ринків. Встановлено, що глобальна електронна торгівля стрімко зростає: до 2026 р. її обсяг перевищить 6,88 трлн дол. США, а цифрові послуги вже формують понад половину світового експорту. Це підтверджує трансформацію цифрової монетизації на ключовий напрям глобальної економіки. Систематизовано основні моделі монетизації (рекламну, freemium, підписну, маркетплейси, монетизацію даних) та обґрунтовано їх диференційований вплив на поведінку споживачів. Показано, що freemium-модель створює бар’єри конкуренції, а підписна — формує інерційну лояльність. Виявлено багаторівневу структуру монетизації, що охоплює транзакції, увагу, дані та лояльність. Доведено, що алгоритмічна персоналізація трансформує споживчий вибір. Визначено специфіку українського ринку в умовах воєнного стану та окреслено стратегії цифрової присутності бізнесу.

latest.title: ANALISIS PENGARUH HARGA, INOVASI PRODUK, DAN SOCIAL MEDIA MARKETING TERHADAP KEPUTUSAN PEMBELIAN PADA KINIEAST CAFE DI KOTA TIMIKA
latest.venue: JEBIMAN : Jurnal Ekonomi, Bisnis, Managemen dan Akuntansi
latest.abstract: This study aims to analyse the influence of price, product innovation and social media marketing on consumer purchasing decisions at KiniEast Cafe. This study employs an associative method using a quantitative approach. The data used in this study consist of quantitative data, with primary sources being utilised. Primary data were obtained directly from KiniEast Cafe customers by distributing questionnaires to 100 respondents selected as the research sample. The research instrument used was a questionnaire employing a 1–5 Likert scale. The data were analysed using multiple linear regression, supported by validity tests, reliability tests, classical assumption tests, t-tests, F-tests and the coefficient of determination (R²). The results indicate that price, product innovation and social media marketing have a partial, positive and significant influence on consumer purchasing decisions at KiniEast Cafe. Simultaneously, price, product innovation and social media marketing also have a significant influence on purchasing decisions. The coefficient of determination (R²) value of 0.557 indicates that price, product innovation and social media marketing collectively account for 55.7 per cent of the variation in consumer purchasing decisions, whilst the remaining 44.3 per cent is explained by other factors not examined in this study. The results of this study indicate that appropriate pricing, the development of product innovation, and the effective utilisation of social media marketing are factors that play a role in increasing consumer purchasing decisions at KiniEast Cafe.

latest.title: Is impulsive buying the missing link? Family financial socialization and financial well-being among young adults in Türkiye
latest.venue: International Journal of Business and Economic Studies
latest.abstract: This study aims to examine the factors determining the financial well-being of university students in Türkiye within the frameworks of social learning theory and family financial socialization theory. Data collected via a survey through the YOUREPLY platform from 395 participants selected from the population using convenience sampling were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM, SmartPLS 4). Results indicate that family financial socialization is negatively related to cognitive but not affective impulsive buying, while in the main model only affective impulsive buying is significantly and negatively related to financial well-being; no indirect associations were supported in the main model. Unexpectedly, family financial socialization is negatively related to financial well-being. This pattern is primarily driven by the family financial distress dimension (β = −.463), whereas instructing money management is positively related to financial well-being (β = .191). When the five dimensions are modelled separately, cognitive impulsive buying is also positively related to financial well-being (β = .219), and one dimension-level indirect association is significant (stressing on savings → cognitive impulsive buying → financial well-being), although its sign runs opposite to the hypothesized mechanism. These results indicate that the aggregate construct masks both positive and negative dimension-level associations. To sum up, these findings point to a family financial socialization boundary condition: specific kinds of guidance behaviors are associated with more deliberative purchasing and, for money-management guidance, with greater well-being. latest.title: Socio Technical Drivers of Impulse Buying in Live Streaming Fashionpreneurship
latest.venue: Aptisi Transactions On Technopreneurship (ATT)
latest.abstract: This study addresses the rapid growth of live-streaming commerce in Indonesia and its impact on impulse buying behavior within emerging digital economies. Integrating the Stimulus–Organism–Response (S-O-R) framework with Socio-Technical Systems (STS) theory, this research aims to examine how socio technical stimuli streamer factors, platform affordances, and perceived brand value, influence consumers’ emotional (shopping happiness) and cognitive (ongoing trust) states, which subsequently drive impulse buying. A quantitative approach was employed using survey data from 300 consumers who purchased local fashion products via Shopee Live and TikTok Shop. Data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) to assess measurement validity and structural relationships. The results indicate that all hypothesized relationships are statistically significant. Socio-technical stimuli significantly influence both shopping happiness and ongoing trust, which in turn positively affect impulse buying, with shopping happiness emerging as the strongest predictor. This study contributes by offering an integrated socio-technical perspective on consumer behavior in live commerce and provides practical implications for enhancing engagement and trust. It also supports the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), particularly SDG 8 and SDG 9, by promoting sustainable digital commerce and empowering local fashion businesses through technology-driven innovation.

hot.title: Sustainable Consumption and Branding for Gen Z: How Brand Dimensions Influence Consumer Behavior and Adoption of Newly Launched Technological Products
hot.abstract: Generation Z is emerging as a powerful force in shaping global consumer behavior, particularly in the market of digital and technological products. This study examines how specific branding dimensions, such as online brand experience, engagement, image, trust, loyalty, awareness, behavioral intention, and brand knowledge, influence Gen Z’s purchase intention, emphasizing sustainable consumption. Sustainable consumption, in this context, refers to the preference for tech products that minimize the environmental impact through eco-friendly design, energy efficiency, and responsible sourcing. Using a quantitative approach, this cross-sectional research explores the effects of online brand experience, engagement, image, trust, loyalty, awareness, behavioral intention, and knowledge on purchasing newly launched technological products that align with sustainability. Data were collected from a Gen Z sample using a combination of convenience and systematic sampling, and multiple regression analysis identified the most significant predictors of purchase intention. The results indicate that online brand experience, brand image, brand trust, and brand loyalty play the most crucial roles, having a greater effects on Gen Z’s purchase intention, while brand awareness and knowledge also contribute. However, brand engagement and behavioral intention have weaker effects. These findings suggest that brands targeting Gen Z should prioritize building a strong, trustworthy, and engaging online presence while highlighting their sustainability efforts, and when Gen Z consumers have favorable digital interactions with a brand, perceive its image positively, trust it, and feel loyal to it, they are more likely to consider purchasing its sustainable offerings. hot.title: Leading in the Digital Age: The Role of Leadership in Organizational Digital Transformation
hot.abstract: In the modern digital age, organizations face unprecedented challenges and possibilities while managing the intricacies of digital transformation. Accelerated technological developments, changing customer preferences, heightened competition, and dynamic regulatory environments necessitate companies to synchronize their business goals with technological innovations. Leadership is crucial in steering businesses through changes, requiring a deep understanding of change processes and the capacity to adjust leadership accordingly. This research addresses the central question: How does leadership effectively promote organizational digital transformation? The study examines how leaders can effectively promote the adoption of advanced technologies and the promotion of innovation, by first exploring the nature of digital transformation within organizations and then analyzing the evolving dynamics of leadership in this context. An integrative review of the Web of Science (WoS) and Scopus databases was conducted, using the search terms: “Leadership” and “Digital Transformation”. The findings emphasize that effective leadership is crucial for managing the minutiae of digital transformation, integrating technology into organizational processes to facilitate learning, collaboration, and agility, enabling companies to adapt to market shifts, reduce uncertainty, and enhance decision-making for sustainable growth. By using the right tools and with the right frequency, leaders may develop team cohesion—even at a distance. Attentive digital-age leaders will know how to leverage the right mechanisms, and herein, we hope to give some indication of how that may be achieved, so that digital transformation increases rather than decreases team motivation levels.

hot.title: The moderating role of personalized recommendations in the trust–satisfaction–loyalty relationship: an empirical study of AI-driven e-commerce
hot.abstract: Abstract Purpose This study investigates the effects of trust, satisfaction, and loyalty on AI-driven e-commerce, with a particular focus on how personalized recommendations moderate these relationships. It aims to explore how personalized AI features reshape consumer perceptions and decision-making. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative research approach was used to collect data from a diverse group of e-commerce users who had interacted with AI-based recommendation systems. An online survey employing standardized scales for trust, satisfaction, loyalty, and personalization was administered, and data were analyzed using structural equation modeling (SEM) to test the hypotheses. Findings The study reveals that trust has a significant positive influence on both satisfaction and loyalty. Personalization further strengthens these relationships by moderating the trust–satisfaction–loyalty dynamic. Satisfaction partially mediates the relationship between trust and loyalty, with the model’s explanatory power improving by 5% when personalization is included as a moderator. These results highlight the pivotal role of personalized recommendations in shaping consumer trust and satisfaction in AI-driven e-commerce. Practical implications Businesses can use personalized recommendation systems to enhance trust and satisfaction, thereby fostering loyalty. For example, platforms like Amazon and Netflix have successfully employed personalized AI algorithms to boost customer retention and engagement. hot.title: Mapping the greenwashing research landscape: a theoretical and field analysis
hot.abstract: Abstract This study provides a comprehensive overview of greenwashing research in business and management, focusing on its conceptual and theoretical foundations. Through a systematic literature review of 97 peer-reviewed articles from Scopus and Web of Science, we use bibliometric analysis to map the evolution of greenwashing studies and network analysis and identify four thematic clusters: (1) symbolic management and CSR communication, (2) environmental regulations and institutional complexity, (3) performance and sustainable practices, and (4) marketing, perception, and trust. Additionally, we perform a full-text analysis to map the theoretical frameworks employed across these clusters, revealing the dominance of macro-level theories (e.g., legitimacy, institutional, and stakeholder theories) and their cross-level interactions with meso- and micro-level approaches. By developing a multi-level theoretical framework, we provide a structured approach to understanding greenwashing across different analytical layers. Then, focusing on the theories used to investigate greenwashing, we identify some avenues for future research. This study has practical implications for understanding how greenwashing affects corporate governance, financial performance, and stakeholder trust, providing insights for enhancing transparency and accountability in sustainable business practices.

hot.title: The Role of Environmental Certification in the Hospitality Industry: Assessing Sustainability, Consumer Preferences, and the Economic Impact
hot.abstract: Hotel certifications have become increasingly vital in promoting sustainability within the hospitality industry, providing frameworks that guide hotels toward reducing their environmental footprint, enhancing operational efficiency, and gaining a competitive edge in the marketplace. This review explores the development, types, and impact of hotel certifications, with a focus on prominent schemes, such as LEED, Green Key, and EarthCheck. Through an analysis of case studies from globally recognized hotels, we highlight how certifications contribute to significant reductions in energy and water use, improved waste management, and enhanced biodiversity protection, while also delivering economic benefits through cost savings and increased guest loyalty. Our paper also examines consumer perceptions of certifications and their willingness to pay (WTP) for certified hotels. The findings suggest that eco-conscious travelers, particularly younger generations, are willing to pay a premium for hotels that demonstrate a commitment to sustainability; however, consumer awareness of certification schemes remains limited. The barriers to adopting certifications, such as high initial costs, resource limitations, and management resistance, are also discussed, along with the challenges posed by greenwashing and the proliferation of certification schemes. Looking to the future, this review identifies key trends that will shape the evolution of hotel certifications, including increased transparency, the integration of smart technologies, the expanding role of social responsibility, and their alignment with global sustainability goals, such as the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).
