latest.title: Enterprise Informatics Capability and Manufacturing Supply Chain Resilience in the Digital Economy: The Roles of Information Transparency and Environmental Dynamism
latest.venue: Journal of Logistics Informatics and Service Science
latest.abstract: This study examines how enterprise informatics capability influences manufacturing supply chain resilience in the context of the digital economy.Drawing on organizational information processing theory and contingency theory, a moderated mediation model is developed to investigate the mediating role of information transparency and the moderating role of environmental dynamism.Survey data collected from 316 supply chain managers and senior executives in Chinese manufacturing firms are analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling.The findings indicate that enterprise informatics capability has a significant positive effect on manufacturing supply chain resilience both directly and indirectly through information transparency.Information transparency partially mediates this relationship by serving as a key information-transmission mechanism.Environmental dynamism does not significantly moderate the direct effect of enterprise informatics capability on supply chain resilience; however, it positively moderates the indirect effect through information transparency, such that the mediating pathway becomes stronger in highly dynamic environments.The findings contribute to the enterprise informatics literature by clarifying the information-processing pathways through which informatics capability translates into supply chain resilience, and by identifying the boundary conditions under which these pathways operate.Practical implications for manufacturing managers seeking to strengthen supply chain resilience through informatics investment are discussed.

latest.title: Strategic Planning for AI-Enabled Cloud Business Intelligence in Commercial Banks: Comparative Evidence from South Africa and Nigeria
latest.venue: International Review of Management and Marketing
latest.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI), cloud computing, and business intelligence (BI) are converging into a new infrastructure platform layer for commercial banks in Africa. Their organizational value depends on strategic, rather than purely technical deployments across the technology stack. This study examines how strategic planning enables AI-enabled cloud business intelligence to support organizational goals in commercial banks in South Africa and Nigeria. A qualitative comparative multiple-case design is adopted, drawing on integrated and annual reports, governance and risk disclosures, regulatory publications, national AI and data-policy documents, and peer-reviewed research. The analysis shows that strategic planning operates as an orchestration capability that leverages AI use cases, cloud and data architecture, resource allocation, model governance, cybersecurity, workforce capability, and performance measurement. South African evidence points to increasingly formalized AI and cloud governance, whereas Nigerian banks exhibit strong market-led digital innovation within a rapidly evolving governance environment. Across both contexts, data quality, responsible AI, human-in-the-loop, third-party resilience, and measurable business integration emerge as conditions for translating AI-enabled analytics into decision quality, operational performance, and strategic alignment. The study develops an integrated framework and makes six propositions for future empirical testing in banking in developing economies.

latest.title: Impact of Packaging Attributes on Brand Love: Evidence from the Luxury Fashion Industry in Egypt
latest.venue: International Review of Management and Marketing
latest.abstract: This study examines the influence of Packaging Attributes on Brand Love in the luxury fashion industry in Egypt, building upon literature on the effect of packaging attributes as a multidimensional concept that extends beyond its protective function to include visual, functional, environmental, and experiential attributes on brand love towards luxury fashion brands. This study is theoretically grounded in the combination of the Cue Utilization Theory, Signaling Theory, and Attachment Theory to examine how packaging attributes shape consumers' emotional responses and strengthen brand love. This research employed a quantitative approach, using an online questionnaire to collect data from 440 luxury fashion consumers via River sampling, and the relationships were analyzed using IBM SPSS Statistics software using Multiple linear regression. Results demonstrated that packaging attributes have significant impact on brand love, with each packaging attribute contributing differently to brand love; thereby, visual, functional, and experiential packaging attributes positively impact brand love, whereas environmental packaging attributes were not a statistically significant predictor of brand love. Findings contribute evidence from the Egyptian market, offering practical implications for luxury fashion brands and marketers, highlighting packaging as a strategic tool to strengthen consumers’ emotional attachment to the brand, and supporting competitiveness in the luxury fashion market.

latest.title: Advancing Digital Banking in Albania: Trust, Financial Literacy and Regulatory Readiness in the FinTech Ecosystem
latest.venue: International Review of Management and Marketing
latest.abstract: Digital transformation is reshaping banking systems worldwide, yet the pace and depth of adoption remain uneven across emerging financial markets. Albania has made visible progress in electronic payments, online banking access and regulatory alignment with European digital finance standards; however, the transition from formal access to sustained digital banking adoption remains incomplete. This study examines the factors influencing digital banking and FinTech adoption in Albania, with a specific focus on consumer trust, financial literacy, perceived barriers and regulatory readiness. The paper applies a mixed-methods research design. Quantitative data were collected through a structured consumer survey with 151 respondents and analyzed through descriptive statistics and Spearman correlation analysis. Qualitative evidence was gathered through 15 semi-structured interviews with representatives from commercial banks, electronic money institutions, public institutions, regulators, sectoral organizations and academic experts. Thematic analysis was used to identify common institutional, technological and regulatory patterns. The findings show that digital banking services are widely accessible, but usage intensity remains moderate. Weekly and monthly use are more common than daily use, while trust, financial knowledge and perceived barriers significantly shape adoption patterns. The correlation analysis indicates a positive relationship between financial knowledge and digital banking use, and a negative relationship between perceived barriers and usage. Interview findings reveal six major themes: digital transformation as a strategic priority, Bank–FinTech cooperation, regulatory adaptation, cybersecurity and data protection, financial education, and an optimistic but condi

latest.title: Data Democratization in Business Intelligence and its Role in Increasing Efficiency within Multi-National Organizations
latest.venue: International Review of Management and Marketing
latest.abstract: Study’s main aim was to shed the light on data democratization as one of business intelligence practices and examine its influence in increasing efficiency within multi-national organizations in terms of (accessibility, interpretability, collaboration, governance, empowerment, scalability and feedback loop). Reaching that aim was done depending on quantitative approach in which we employed a questionnaire self-administered by (261) individuals. Through SPSS dealing with primary data; results of analysis indicated that data democratization in business intelligence statistically influence efficiency within multi-national organizations. Among the chosen sub-variables of study, it was found that scalability in business intelligence statistically influence efficiency within multi-national organizations.

latest.title: IT-Enabled Supply Chain Resilience in Global Logistics Operations: A Scenario-Based Informatics and Service-System Coordination Framework
latest.venue: Journal of Logistics Informatics and Service Science
latest.abstract: Global supply chains are highly interconnected -material flows, information flows, digital platforms, suppliers, logistics providers, and customers are more and more interdependent with each other in the form of logistics service systems.In times of geopolitical uncertainty, a pandemic outbreak, cyber threats, demand fluctuations and technological downtime, supply chain resilience goes beyond flexibility and redundancy of resources.It demands a comprehensive logistics informatics system, an instant service coordination and adaptive digital decision-making.This study constructs an IT-supported supply chain resilience model, which combines enterprise resource planning systems, Internet of Things monitoring, cloud platforms, blockchain traceability, big data analytics and digital twin technologies.The research uses scenario analysis to assess the impact of digital integration on recovery time, lead time, transparency and adaptability and service continuity in global logistics operations.The empirical framework is based on selected multinational companies and the indicators of resilience are the Index of Digitalization of Supply Chains, Scenario Stability Unit and Index of Supply Chain Adaptability.Results indicate that digitally integrated logistics systems are more resilient in the event of an economic shock and technology failure, as well as combined disruptions.The highest resilience effect is realized when IT tools are used as an integrated service-system architecture as opposed to individual technological services.In this study, an integrated model for digital coordination of resilient supply chain operations is proposed, which is also a contribution to the field of logistics informatics and service science.

latest.title: Sustainability-Oriented Legal Compliance Risk Screening for Belt and Road Cross-Border E-Commerce Logistics: An Audita ble Decision-Support Framework
latest.venue: Journal of Logistics Informatics and Service Science
latest.abstract: Cross-border e-commerce expands market access across Belt and Road economies, but platform-mediated logistics exposes firms to heterogeneous customs, data, consumerprotection, taxation, cybersecurity, and environmental requirements.This study develops a transparent country-level screening and decision-support framework that integrates governance quality, logistics performance, economic exposure, and digital readiness.After correcting country-name matching with ISO3 identifiers, the analysis covers 66 economies using 2023 Worldwide Governance Indicators, Logistics Performance Index, and World Development Indicators data.A weighted proxy (governance 0.50, logistics 0.30, digital readiness 0.20) is evaluated with logistic regression, random forest, and gradient boosting under a stratified 49/17 holdout and random seed 42.Logistic regression and random forest each obtain 0.82 accuracy, 0.73 precision, 1.00 recall, 0.84 F1-score, and 1.00 AUC; gradient boosting obtains 0.59 accuracy, 0.70 F1-score, and 0.94 AUC.These metrics measure recovery of an internally constructed median-split proxy, not prediction of independently adjudicated violations.Regulatory quality, rule of law, government effectiveness, logistics competence, and tracking capability provide the strongest screening signals.The framework converts relative risk evidence into proportionate due-diligence, documentation, routing, monitoring, and escalation controls while remaining subordinate to transaction-and jurisdiction-specific legal review.

latest.title: How Environmental, Social, and Governance Mediates the Impact of FinTech Investments on Bank Performance in Gulf Countries
latest.venue: International Review of Management and Marketing
latest.abstract: This study examines the FinTech factors affecting bank performance in Gulf countries. The study followed a causal research design employing data from 2010 to 2023. The study unit of analysis is twelve banks in Kuwait, Qatar, the UAE, and Saudi Arabia. The study also uses PLS-SEM because of its advantage in examining mediating pathways that might be obscured in simpler regression analyses. According to the study’s findings, FinTech factors such as mobile banking applications (MBA) and GDP per capita variables have a negative, statistically significant effect on bank performance. On the other hand, GDP per capita has not statistically positively affected both ROA and ROE of bank performance. Moreover, both MBA and GDP per capita directly enhance environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance. The ESG does affect ROE. Besides, ESG plays a mediating role by strengthening the relationship between MBA, GDP per capita, and ROE, as it enhances banks ESG performance. The current study fills a gap in the body of literature since it considers previously overlooked factors that affect bank performance, i.e., FinTech variables and the mediating role of ESG on their effects on bank performance. The resulting policy implication is that banks in Gulf countries benefit most from investing in FinTech innovation since they can enhance operational efficiency and support sustainability efforts by driving better ESG performance, ultimately fostering long term stability and growth in the banking sector.

latest.title: Driving Business Growth through Adaptive Leadership, Open Innovation, and Market Sensing: The Role of Purple Ocean Strategy in Information Technology Solution Business
latest.venue: International Review of Management and Marketing
latest.abstract: The rapid development of digital technologies and increasing competitive intensity have created significant challenges for information technology (IT) solution businesses seeking sustainable growth. Organizations must continuously adapt to technological changes, customer expectations, and competitive pressures while developing innovative and differentiated solutions. However, limited research has integrated adaptive leadership, open innovation, market sensing capability, purple ocean strategy formulation, and overall business growth within a single research framework. This study aims to investigate the causal factors and relationships among adaptive leadership, open innovation, market sensing capability, purple ocean strategy formulation, and overall business growth in IT solution businesses, and to develop an empirical causal model explaining these relationships. The study employs a quantitative research design supported by qualitative thematic analysis. Data are collected from 400 respondents consisting of business owners, executives, managers, and individuals involved in organizational decision-making. A structured questionnaire using a five-point Likert scale measures the five major constructs. Descriptive statistics and structural equation modeling (SEM) are employed to assess the measurement model and test the proposed hypotheses. The anticipated results suggest that adaptive leadership positively influences open innovation, market sensing capability, purple ocean strategy formulation, and overall business growth. Open innovation and market sensing capability are expected to positively influence purple ocean strategy formulation and overall business growth. latest.title: Artificial Intelligence-driven Audit Risk Reduction in Thin Capitalisation Engagements: Implications for External Audit Effectiveness among South African Multinational Corporations
latest.venue: International Review of Management and Marketing
latest.abstract: This study examined the effect of artificial intelligence-driven audit techniques on audit risk reduction associated with thin capitalisation engagements. It also examined their implications for external audit effectiveness among South African multinational corporations. Panel regression and System Generalised Method of Moments (GMM) models were used to analyse the data gathered from 14 listed multinational corporations in Johannesburg Stock Exchange. The adoption of artificial intelligence significantly reduced audit risk at β = −0.371, p < 0.001. It improved external audit effectiveness (β = 0.123, p < 0.05) after controlling for endogeneity through GMM instrumentation. Thin capitalisation and audit risk mitigation activity were positively related (β = 0.576, p < 0.001), contrary to conventional expectations. Artificial intelligence adoption did not moderate the relationship between thin capitalisation and audit risk reduction (β = 0.231, p < 0.10). Audit risk reduction partially mediated the AI–effectiveness relationship (indirect effect = 0.094). The lagged dependent variable in GMM (α = 0.446, p < 0.05) confirmed that audit effectiveness is path-dependent. The study contributes to the limited literature on the causal interrelationship between artificial intelligence and auditing in Africa and extends institutional theory within the context of tax compliance and audit quality governance in emerging markets. The findings underscore the need to enhance audit effectiveness and mitigate audit risks that can be traced to thin capitalisation engagements.

latest.title: Innovative Frontiers in Commerce: Emerging Trends and Future Opportunities
latest.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
latest.abstract: Abstract The rapid advancement of technology, changing consumer preferences, and increasing global interconnectedness are transforming the traditional landscape of commerce. This research paper examines the innovative frontiers shaping modern commerce, with particular emphasis on emerging technologies, digital transformation, evolving business models, and changing consumer behaviour. Technologies such as artificial intelligence, blockchain, big data analytics, cloud computing, automation, and digital payment systems are creating new opportunities for businesses to improve operational efficiency, enhance customer experiences, and expand their market reach. The study also explores the growing significance of e-commerce, social commerce, omnichannel retailing, and sustainable business practices in shaping the future of commercial activities. Alongside these opportunities, businesses face challenges related to cybersecurity, data privacy, technological adoption, regulatory uncertainty, and the need for continuous innovation. The paper highlights how organizations can adapt to these developments by embracing technology-driven strategies, fostering innovation, and responding effectively to changing market demands. The study concludes that the future of commerce will be characterized by greater digital integration, personalization, sustainability, and technology-enabled business ecosystems. Understanding these emerging trends is essential for businesses, policymakers, researchers, and other stakeholders seeking to navigate the evolving commercial environment and capitalize on future opportunities.

latest.title: Ai & Fintech-Driven Transformation of the Inidian Financial Management System: An Empirical Study of Digital Payments, Blockchain Technology, & Cryptocurrency
latest.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
latest.abstract: Abstract The rapid advancement of Financial Technology (FinTech) has significantly transformed the structure and functioning of the Indian financial system. The growth of digital payment platforms, mobile banking, artificial intelligence (AI), cloud computing and data-driven financial services has changed the way individuals and businesses access and use financial services. In India, digital payments have emerged as an important component of financial transformation, while Artificial Intelligence is increasingly being used for fraud detection, credit assessment, customer service, risk management and personalised financial services.This study examines the role of FinTech in transforming the Indian financial system, with particular emphasis on digital payments and Artificial Intelligence. The study proposes an analytical framework linking FinTech adoption, digital payment usage, AI-enabled financial services, consumer trust, cybersecurity and financial inclusion. A structured questionnaire can be used to collect primary data from users of digital financial services. The proposed study may employ descriptive statistics, correlation and regression analysis to examine relationships among the major variables. The paper also discusses opportunities and challenges associated with technology-driven financial transformation, including cybersecurity risks, digital fraud, data privacy, technological barriers and the digital divide.

latest.title: Financial Inclusion and Institutional Resilience in AI-Driven Islamic Finance: A Contract-Based Risk Governance Framework
latest.venue: Electronic Integrated Computer Algorithm Journal
latest.abstract: The growing use of artificial intelligence (AI) in Islamic finance has complicated the allocation of responsibility when financing decisions depend on automated assessments. This study develops a conceptual governance framework by reconstructing the complementary functions of Kafalah, Wakalah, and rahn. Using a qualitative doctrinal-comparative approach, it examines the contracts individually and through three pairwise relationships, then maps their functions to AI-related risks and institutional controls. The analysis identifies Kafalah–rahn as a mechanism for coordinating guarantees and collateral, Kafalah–Wakalah for linking guarantee obligations with accountable delegation, and Wakalah–rahn for governing delegated collateral activities. These relationships inform a five-layer architecture covering contractual authority, contingent risk allocation, collateral risk mitigation, technological governance, and maqāṣid al-sharīʿah-based evaluation. An illustrative financing scenario shows how model validation, human oversight, decision traceability, and proportionate safeguards may operate together. The framework distinguishes responsible financial access from institutional resilience without assuming that either outcome follows automatically. Its contribution is conceptual, and practical effectiveness requires subsequent expert and institutional assessment.

latest.title: Beyond Organisational Scale: How Digital Micro-Entrepreneurs Build International Businesses and Challenge the Competitive Advantages of Large Corporations
latest.venue: Journal of Economics Finance and Management Studies
latest.abstract: For most of the twentieth century, organisational scale was treated as the main source of competitive advantage in international business. Large corporations could spread fixed costs over high volumes, finance foreign direct investment, and build distribution networks that smaller rivals could not match. This paper argues that digital technologies are loosening that logic. Drawing on the literatures on digital entrepreneurship, international new ventures, the resource-based view, dynamic capabilities and platform ecosystems, we examine how digital micro-entrepreneurs, defined as owner-operated ventures with very few employees that run their core activities through digital platforms and tools, build and sustain international businesses. We develop an integrative framework in which four digital affordances (low-cost market access, modular outsourcing, data-driven learning and community-based trust) shape three entrepreneurial capabilities (digital orchestration, rapid experimentation and network-based credibility). These capabilities, in turn, allow micro-entrepreneurs to erode specific scalebased advantages of large firms in niche and long-tail markets. We advance six propositions, discuss boundary conditions including platform dependence and institutional constraints in emerging economies, and outline a research agenda for empirical testing. The paper contributes to international entrepreneurship by shifting attention from firm size to orchestration capacity, and offers implications for micro-entrepreneurs, platform operators, financial institutions and policymakers.

latest.title: When Algorithms Set Prices: Emerging Consumer Fairness Challenges in AI-Driven Dynamic Pricing
latest.venue: Journal of Computers Mechanical and Management
latest.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is turning dynamic pricing from a standardized management decision into an individual, algorithmic experience. Algorithmic pricing improves efficiency and personalization, but its opacity and individualized prices can leave consumers feeling treated unfairly and distrustful. This short communication draws on recent research on algorithmic pricing, price fairness, price transparency, and consumer trust to build a conceptual framework. It links four features of algorithmic pricing (real-time adaptation, personalization, individualized price differentiation, and limited explainability) to perceived price fairness, which in turn shapes consumer trust and acceptance or resistance. The paper argues that fairness is a strategic management problem, not only an ethical concern. Implications for pricing managers cover price explanations, responsible personalization, and governance, and empirical research directions are proposed.

latest.title: Corporate Value Analysis Based on Profitability, Firm Growth, and Funding Decision through Dividend Policy in Consumer Non-Cyclicals Issuers on the Indonesia Stock Exchange
latest.venue: Journal of Applied Business Taxation and Economics Research
latest.abstract: This study analyzes the effect of Profitability (ROE), Firm Growth (AGR), and Funding Decision (DER) on Corporate Value (PBV) through Dividend Policy (DPR) as an intervening variable among Consumer Non-Cyclicals issuers listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange over the 2021-2025 period. A quantitative approach was applied using panel data regression with the Fixed Effect Model (FEM) on 16 sample companies (80 observations). The results show that Profitability has a significant positive effect on both Dividend Policy and Corporate Value. Firm Growth has a significant negative effect on both Dividend Policy and Corporate Value. Funding Decision has a significant negative effect on Dividend Policy but a significant positive effect on Corporate Value. Dividend Policy has a significant positive effect on Corporate Value and is confirmed as a partial mediator linking Profitability, Firm Growth, and Funding Decision to Corporate Value. These findings support Agency Theory, Signalling Theory, Pecking Order Theory, Trade-off Theory, and Dividend Signalling Theory in the context of Indonesian Consumer Non-Cyclicals issuers.

latest.title: DETERMINANT OF THE MANAGEMENT ACCOUNTING EFFECTIVENESS IN TOURISM FIRMS
latest.venue: Financial and credit activity problems of theory and practice
latest.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI), rising customer demand for individualized services, and growing need to strike a balance between rising operating costs and service quality are all driving the tourism industry's rapid digital transformation. Effective management accounting systems are now more crucial than ever for facilitating managerial decision-making, boosting organizational competitiveness, and increasing operational efficiency. There is no empirical data on how organizational skills and AI-related investment considerations together affect management accounting effectiveness in tourism businesses, especially in emerging nations, despite the increased focus on digital transformation. This study looks into how management accounting effectiveness in Vietnamese tourism businesses is affected by top management support, accounting staff competency, and AI adoption costs. The study used a sequential research approach that included expert interviews, a pilot survey, and a large-scale quantitative survey. It was based on the Resource-Based View and Contingency Theory. Reliability analysis, exploratory factor analysis, multiple regression analysis, and Pearson correlation analysis were used to examine the gathered data. The empirical results show that while top management support does not show a statistically significant direct effect, accounting staff competency and AI implementation cost positively and considerably influence management accounting effectiveness. These results imply that, rather than relying solely on managerial dedication, successful management accounting in tourism-related businesses increasingly requires organizational capacities able to combine professional accounting knowledge with commercially viable AI investments. latest.title: Pengaruh Kualitas Pelayanan, Kualitas Produk dan Variasi Menu Terhadap Kepuasan Pelanggan di Ask Coffee Marelan
latest.venue: PENG Jurnal Ekonomi dan Manajemen
latest.abstract: Penjualan Ask Coffee Marelan menurun dari Rp657,0 juta pada 2022 menjadi Rp504,7 juta pada 2025 di tengah persaingan coffee shop yang semakin ketat. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis pengaruh kualitas pelayanan, kualitas produk, dan variasi menu terhadap kepuasan pelanggan Ask Coffee Marelan. Penelitian kuantitatif asosiatif ini mengumpulkan data melalui kuesioner dari 100 pelanggan, dengan ukuran sampel ditentukan menggunakan rumus Lemeshow, kemudian menganalisisnya dengan regresi linear berganda menggunakan SPSS versi 27. Kualitas pelayanan (B = 0,002; t = 0,039; p = 0,969) dan kualitas produk (B = −0,017; t = −0,255; p = 0,799) tidak berpengaruh signifikan secara parsial terhadap kepuasan pelanggan, sedangkan variasi menu berpengaruh positif dan signifikan (B = 0,527; β = 0,830; t = 6,013; p < 0,001). Secara simultan, ketiga variabel berpengaruh signifikan (F = 55,274; p < 0,001) dan menjelaskan 63,3% variasi kepuasan pelanggan. Tumpang tindih yang tinggi antara kualitas produk dan prediktor lain (VIF = 7,546) mengindikasikan bahwa kontribusi uniknya terserap oleh variasi menu. Ask Coffee Marelan perlu memprioritaskan pengembangan menu dengan tetap menjaga standar produk dan pelayanan.

latest.title: The Effects of Human Resource Competence and Management Support on Fashion Ecosystem Competitiveness through Tourism Destination Attractiveness in Madura
latest.venue: JURNAL MANAJEMEN MOTIVASI
latest.abstract: This study examines human resource competence, management support, tourism destination attractiveness and perceived fashion ecosystem competitiveness among 100 purposively sampled batik owners and artisans in Bangkalan and Sampang. PLS-SEM showed positive, significant direct associations for both predictors with attractiveness and competitiveness, and between attractiveness and competitiveness. The competence-related indirect association was supported (p = .022). The support-related indirect association did not meet the original p < .05 rule (p = .054), although its 95% percentile interval [.009, .134] excluded zero. Findings concern cross-sectional individual perceptions, not causal mediation or regional ecosystem performance. Sampling and possible response dependence limit interpretation.

latest.title: DEVELOPMENT, TRANSLATION AND PRELIMINARY VALIDATION OF DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION AND GREEN LOGISTICS MEASUREMENT INSTRUMENT
latest.venue: Quantum Journal of Social Sciences and Humanities
latest.abstract: This study develops, translates, and preliminarily validates a measurement instrument designed to assess digital transformation–driven green logistics practices and sustainability within cross-cultural logistics environments. A multi-phase methodological framework was applied, beginning with the conceptualization of constructs and the systematic generation of items based on established literature. Content and face validity were confirmed through expert evaluations, yielding strong CVI scores and demonstrating item relevance, clarity, and representativeness. The instrument was translated using standardized forward–backward procedures, followed by expert committee review to ensure semantic and conceptual equivalence. Cognitive debriefing further verified respondent comprehension, while a pilot test involving 30 logistics professionals provided evidence of acceptable internal consistency and survey feasibility. Structural validation procedures, such as Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA), were intentionally deferred due to the small pilot sample size. Although the present study produced an Arabic version, the development and adaptation processes followed internationally recognized standards, making the instrument suitable for application in other linguistic and cultural contexts with appropriate adaptation. Overall, the study delivers a culturally attuned and conceptually robust pre-final instrument that lays the groundwork for future large-scale psychometric validation and empirical investigations into the role of digital transformation in advancing sustainable logistics practices.

latest.title: Sustainable Supply Chain Economics and Global Market Adaptation Strategies
latest.venue: International Academic Journal of Economics
latest.abstract: The application of sustainable supply chain management is increasingly becoming a common approach for increasing efficiency, effectiveness, and resilience in an environment that is highly uncertain in terms of the global markets. In this research, the use of sustainable supply chain management approaches for the purpose of adaptation to the global market by means of green sourcing, resource efficiency, diversification of suppliers, regionalization, digital visibility, and flexibility is studied. An integrative conceptual framework is developed, linking the performance in sustainability to economic efficiency and supply chain resilience. The research further highlights the significance of regional adaptation and the adoption of circular practices as ways of minimizing costs and increasing competitiveness in the long run. The model proposed in this paper brings together all the elements needed to understand the interaction between sustainability and adaptation to global markets. The results indicate that organizations that combine environmental considerations with economic and adaptive competencies can increase supply reliability, decrease risk exposure, be more efficient with resources, and experience sustainable growth in their competitiveness.

latest.title: Human Capital Governance and Employee Attrition Prediction: A Theory-Informed People-Analytics Framework Using Synthetic IBM HR Data
latest.venue: Journal of Computers Mechanical and Management
latest.abstract: Voluntary employee attrition creates recruitment, onboarding, productivity, and knowledge-continuity costs, which motivates people-analytics approaches that connect human-capital theory with interpretable prediction. This study presents a theory-informed proof-of-concept framework using the IBM HR Analytics Employee Attrition and Performance dataset, which contains 1,470 synthetic employee records rather than observations from a real organization. Six composite measures represent well-being, burnout risk, compensation fairness, governance, career stagnation, and engagement. The analytical pipeline combines logistic and ordinary least squares regression, regularized classifiers, Random Forest, XGBoost, SHAP-based model explanation, subgroup analysis, and an exploratory mediation specification. In the attrition model, the Well-Being Index, Governance Score, Engagement Score, and Compensation Fairness Proxy are associated with lower attrition odds within this synthetic dataset, whereas overtime and career stagnation are associated with higher odds. The theory-informed classification models achieve held-out AUC values from 0.756 to 0.770, while an un-engineered raw-feature logistic baseline reaches 0.778, so the composite indices are interpreted as a theoretically organized, governance-oriented representation rather than a source of superior predictive accuracy. The monthly-income model is treated only as a diagnostic illustration because the Compensation Fairness Proxy is constructed from Monthly Income and cannot provide an independent test of income prediction. The exploratory mediation results do not support an indirect well-being-to-attrition pathway through overtime under the Sobel test. latest.title: Pengaruh Persepsi Harga Paket Data terhadap Kepuasan Pengguna Dalam Komunikasi Penawaran Telkomsel Prabayar pada Mahasiswa Pendidikan Fisika Universitas Sriwijaya
latest.venue: Journal of Communication and Social Sciences
latest.abstract: ABSTRACT Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis pengaruh harga paket internet Telkomsel Prabayar terhadap kepuasan pelanggan pada mahasiswa Pendidikan Fisika Universitas Sriwijaya angkatan 2022–2024. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan metode survei. Populasi berjumlah 266 mahasiswa dan sampel terdiri atas 111 responden pengguna Telkomsel Prabayar. Data dikumpulkan melalui kuesioner dan dianalisis menggunakan uji validitas, reliabilitas, uji asumsi, serta regresi linear sederhana. Hasil pengujian menunjukkan bahwa instrumen penelitian valid dan reliabel. Persamaan regresi yang diperoleh adalah Y = 1,826 + 0,717X, dengan pengaruh harga paket internet yang signifikan terhadap kepuasan pelanggan (p = 0,002). Hasil ini menunjukkan bahwa penilaian mahasiswa terhadap harga paket internet berkaitan dengan kepuasan mereka terhadap layanan Telkomsel Prabayar. Abstract This study examines the effect of Telkomsel prepaid internet package prices on customer satisfaction among Physics Education students at Universitas Sriwijaya from the 2022–2024 cohorts. A quantitative survey was conducted among 111 Telkomsel prepaid users from a population of 266 students. Data were collected using questionnaires and analyzed through validity and reliability tests, assumption tests, and simple linear regression. The instruments met the reported validity and reliability criteria. The regression equation was Y = 1.826 + 0.717X, and the reported significance value was p = 0.002, indicating a statistically significant relationship between internet package prices and customer satisfaction. The findings indicate that students’ evaluations of internet package prices are associated with their satisfaction with Telkomsel prepaid services.

latest.title: Pendampingan Literasi Menabung untuk Penguatan Modal Usaha Keluarga pada Komunitas Ramah Lansia
latest.venue: Jurnal Pelayanan dan Pengabdian Masyarakat (Pamas)
latest.abstract: Saving literacy is an important component of families’ ability to manage finances, build emergency funds, and prepare business capital. In the Age-Friendly Community at RPTRA Payung Tunas Teratai, Cipayung, some participants had already set aside part of their income, but saving was not yet systematically planned or optimally directed toward productive purposes. This community service program aimed to improve participants’ understanding of saving literacy and family financial management and to provide practical skills for separating and allocating funds. The program was conducted on 4 September 2026 with 20 participants using a participatory approach comprising education, a leaflet, introduction and simulation of a Savings Management Wallet, hands-on practice, and pre- and post-test evaluation. The wallet divided funds into three categories: Household Needs, Medical and Emergency Needs, and Business Capital Savings. Evaluation results showed that the total score increased from 83 to 97, while the mean score increased from 4.15 to 4.85, a gain of 0.70 points (16.87%). These findings indicate strengthened short-term understanding following education and mentoring. The program produced an educational leaflet and a Savings Management Wallet as reusable practice media. Follow-up mentoring is needed to assess the consistency of saving behavior and the use of savings as family business capital.

latest.title: Pengaruh Word of Mouth, Harga Sewa Modal dan Kemudahan Transaksi terhadap Minat Nasabah dalam Menggunakan Produk Mikro Kreasi pada PT. Pegadaian di CP Pulo Brayan
latest.venue: PENG Jurnal Ekonomi dan Manajemen
latest.abstract: Jumlah pengguna produk Mikro Kreasi di PT Pegadaian CP Pulo Brayan menurun dari 190 nasabah pada 2022 menjadi 74 nasabah pada 2025. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis pengaruh word of mouth, harga sewa modal, dan kemudahan transaksi terhadap minat nasabah menggunakan produk Mikro Kreasi. Penelitian kuantitatif asosiatif ini melibatkan 100 responden yang dipilih dengan purposive sampling, dengan ukuran sampel ditentukan melalui rumus Lemeshow. Data dikumpulkan melalui kuesioner, wawancara, dan dokumentasi, lalu dianalisis dengan uji asumsi klasik, regresi linear berganda, uji t, dan uji F. Word of mouth (B = 0,336; t = 10,741; p < 0,001), harga sewa modal (B = 0,360; t = 11,448; p < 0,001), dan kemudahan transaksi (B = 0,322; t = 6,996; p < 0,001) masing-masing berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap minat nasabah. Berdasarkan koefisien terstandarisasi, harga sewa modal (β = 0,543) dan word of mouth (β = 0,529) berpengaruh lebih kuat daripada kemudahan transaksi (β = 0,345). Secara simultan, ketiga variabel berpengaruh signifikan (F = 116,100; p < 0,001) dan menjelaskan 78,4% variasi minat nasabah. Upaya meningkatkan minat terhadap Mikro Kreasi perlu memperhatikan rekomendasi nasabah, kesesuaian tarif sewa modal, dan kemudahan prosedur transaksi.

latest.title: LIQUIDITY, LEVERAGE, ACTIVITY RATIO, AND PROFITABILITY OF INDONESIAN FOOD AND BEVERAGE FIRMS
latest.venue: International Journal of Accounting Management Economics and Social Sciences (IJAMESC)
latest.abstract: This study aimed to examine the effect of liquidity, leverage, and activity ratio on profitability in non-financial food and beverage companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during the 2023–2025 period. The study employed a quantitative approach with an associative-causal design. The population consisted of 102 food and beverage companies, and a sample of 64 companies was selected through purposive sampling, resulting in 192 firm-year observations over three years. Secondary data were collected from audited annual financial statements. Profitability was measured by Return on Assets, while liquidity, leverage, and activity ratio were measured by Current Ratio, Debt-to-Equity Ratio, and Total Asset Turnover, respectively. The data were analyzed using panel data regression with model selection tests and classical assumption tests. The results showed that liquidity had no significant effect on profitability, with a regression coefficient of −0.000110 and a significance value of 0.781. Leverage had a significant negative effect on profitability, with a regression coefficient of −0.045 and a significance value of 0.000. Activity ratio had a significant positive effect on profitability, with a regression coefficient of 0.071 and a significance value of 0.000. The adjusted coefficient of determination indicated that 63.56 percent of the variation in profitability was explained by the three independent variables, while the remaining 36.44 percent was attributed to factors outside the model. latest.title: Examining green practices in healthcare via organizational support and employee awareness and attitudes: A behavioral-capability perspective
latest.venue: Cleaner Manufacturing
latest.abstract: Healthcare sector contributes significantly to environmental challenges through resource consumption, waste generation, and supply chain activities. This is particularly true in developing countries where sustainable healthcare infrastructure remains limited. This study examines the relationships among employees’ awareness and attitudes, organizational support, and green supply chain management practices in Bangladeshi hospitals. Drawing on the Theory of Planned Behavior and the Resource-Based View. We collected data from 436 healthcare professionals and analyzed them using PLS-SEM with SmartPLS 4. The findings suggest that employees’ environmental awareness and attitudes are associated with GSCM practices both directly and indirectly through organizational support. Organizational support is strongly associated with GSCM adoption and partially mediates the relationship between awareness and attitudes and GSCM practices. It may not be sufficient to explain sustainable supply chain practices without supportive organizational mechanisms such as leadership commitment, environmental training, and resource allocation. This study contributes contextual evidence on GSCM adoption in healthcare organizations operating in a resource-constrained developing-country setting. The findings also provide practical insights for strengthening sustainability initiatives within hospitals.

latest.title: Integrating Science and Shariah: Scenarios from Higher Education, Islamic Finance and The Halal Industry
latest.venue: Journal of MUWAFAQAT
latest.abstract: The growing complexity of contemporary challenges requires a more coherent integration of scientific knowledge and shariah principles. However, current approaches remain fragmented and lack a sufficiently systematic framework for practical application. This study critically examines the integration of science and shariah in three selected sectors: higher education, Islamic banking and finance, and the halal industry. Drawing on a critical narrative review of relevant literature, the study analyses existing practices through the concepts of Islamization of Knowledge, revelation-guided science, the integration of Naqli and Aqli knowledge, Tawhid, and Maqasid al-Shariah. The findings demonstrate that integration has progressed beyond theoretical discourse and is increasingly reflected in university curricula, shariah-compliant financial innovation, digital finance, halal governance, and supply-chain traceability. Nevertheless, its implementation remains constrained by epistemological fragmentation, limited multidisciplinary competence, methodological inconsistencies, inadequate technological and shariah literacy, and the absence of standardised shariah governance for emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence and blockchain. In the halal industry, an additional concern is the tendency to prioritise procedural halal compliance without adequately incorporating the broader principles of halalan tayyiban, consumer welfare, and sustainability. The study proposes a more systematic and applicable epistemological approach that integrates revelation, reason, and empirical evidence while preserving scientific rigour and alignment with Maqasid al-Shariah. hot.title: Exploring automation bias in human–AI collaboration: a review and implications for explainable AI
hot.abstract: Abstract As Artificial Intelligence (AI) becomes increasingly embedded in high-stakes domains such as healthcare, law, and public administration, automation bias (AB)—the tendency to over-rely on automated recommendations—has emerged as a critical challenge in human–AI collaboration. While previous reviews have examined AB in traditional computer-assisted decision-making, research on its implications in modern AI-driven work environments remains limited. To address this gap, this research systematically investigates how AB manifests in these settings and the cognitive mechanisms that influence it. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, we reviewed 35 peer-reviewed studies from SCOPUS, ScienceDirect, PubMed, and Google Scholar. The included literature, published between January 2015 and April 2025, spans fields such as cognitive psychology, human factors engineering, human–computer interaction, and neuroscience, providing an interdisciplinary foundation for our analysis. Traditional perspectives attribute AB to over-trust in automation or attentional constraints, resulting in users perceiving AI-generated outputs as reliable. However, our review presents a more nuanced view. While confirming some prior findings, it also sheds light on additional interacting factors such as, AI literacy, level of professional expertise, cognitive profile, developmental trust dynamics, task verification demands, and explanation complexity. Notably, although Explainable AI (XAI) and transparency mechanisms are designed to mitigate AB, overly technical, cognitively demanding, or even simplistic explanations may inadvertently reinforce misplaced trust, especially among less experienced professionals with low AI literacy. Taken together, these findings suggest that although explanations may increas

hot.title: Is Big Data Adoption Shaping Business Landscapes? An Overview of Current Hotspots and Future Trends
hot.abstract: Introduction: Most bibliometrics reviews in the prior studies have focused on tracking the evolution, applications, and implications of Big Data in business through different sectors using Web of Science or Scopus databases. Moreover, none of these studies has addressed the differences between developed and developing countries. These gaps indicate that we need a bibliometric review that can identify current trends and unexplored areas. Objectives: This study aims to use a bibliometric approach to examine how Big Data is used in businesses using WoS and Scopus databases. Methods: A Systematic Literature Review was conducted based on the country's economic status using the SPAR-4-SLR protocol for this research. Results: The results show a significant growth in publications since 2013 among developed countries and since 2014 among developing ones such as the United States and the United Kingdom, along with China and India, respectively. Also, Machine Learning Overlaps Artificial Intelligence alongside Analytics, fueling innovative data-driven business processes around Big Data. Conclusions: This article explores the transformative power of Big Data across domains, stressing its ability to cause substantial breakthroughs within the digital economy

hot.title: Generative AI and its Transformative Value for Digital Platforms
hot.abstract: The emergence of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) represents a watershed moment in the evolution of digital platforms. The capabilities of this AI technology go beyond traditional AI systems, enabling the autonomous generation of novel outcomes with significant implications for platform value creation, architecture, governance, and stakeholder interactions. We develop an integrative conceptual framework that identifies four key mechanisms through which GenAI transforms digital platforms: intelligent automation, democratization, hyper-personalization, and collaborative innovation. Through intelligent automation, GenAI transforms boundary resources from passive interfaces into active, intelligent mediators of value creation. Democratization systematically lowers barriers to platform participation. Hyper-personalization enables dynamic, individual-level adaptation of platform content. Collaborative innovation transforms platform innovation by making GenAI an active participant in human-AI value co-creation. We use this framework to situate the papers in the special issue and develop a research agenda that explores the transformative impact of GenAI on platform stakeholder relationships.

hot.title: Cyber Shopping Beyond Boundaries: The Metaverse Revolution in e‐Commerce and Consumer Behavior
hot.abstract: The metaverse is swiftly flattering an important player in the e‐commerce domain. It provides innumerable opportunities and indicates a revolutionary paradigm shift in e‐commerce. Online businesses can now create virtual storefronts that enable immersive, lifelike product exploration within the metaverse, in contrast to traditional brick‐and‐mortar stores that cater to local customers. Current research offers a novel conceptual framework based on theories of interactive media effects and the stimulus–organism–response paradigm to understand consumer purchase intentions in the metaverse. Carefully gathered data from 342 survey participants were then examined using the analytical tools of structural equation modelling (SEM) and importance–performance map analysis (IPMA). The results of the study shed light on how much perceived augmentation and interaction affect consumers’ cognitive and emotive reactions, including feelings of realism, immersion, and telepresence. Remarkably, these reactions have a significant influence on how customers behave. The study’s distinctive worth is found in its creative recommendations, which can help tech firms and metaverse developers improve the purchasing experience in this dynamic digital environment.

hot.title: Why human–AI relationships need socioaffective alignment
hot.abstract: Humans strive to design safe AI systems that align with our goals and remain under our control. However, as AI capabilities advance, we face a new challenge: the emergence of deeper, more persistent relationships between humans and AI systems. We explore how increasingly capable AI agents may generate the perception of deeper relationships with users, especially as AI becomes more personalised and agentic. This shift, from transactional interaction to ongoing sustained social engagement with AI, necessitates a new focus on socioaffective alignment—how an AI system behaves within the social and psychological ecosystem co-created with its user, where preferences and perceptions evolve through mutual influence. Addressing these dynamics involves resolving key intrapersonal dilemmas, including balancing immediate versus long-term well-being, protecting autonomy, and managing AI companionship alongside the desire to preserve human social bonds. By framing these challenges through a notion of basic psychological needs, we seek AI systems that support, rather than exploit, our fundamental nature as social and emotional beings.

hot.title: The impacts of companion AI on human relationships: risks, benefits, and design considerations
hot.abstract: AI applications intended for companionship have increased in both availability and capabilities in recent years, alongside a spike in loneliness (Johnson 2023 ; Murthy 2023 ). According to a 2024 analysis by venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz, companion AI makes up 16 of the top 100 AI apps based on web traffic and monthly active users (Moore 2024 ). Moreover, today’s AI applications have a greater command of human language, an increasing capacity for storing memories, and more varied modalities to support an increasing diversity of experiences, a known driver in the development and deepening of emotional relationships (Skjuve et al. 2022 ).

hot.title: Advancing Sustainable Practices in Electronic Customer Relationship Management
hot.venue: International Review of Management and Marketing
hot.abstract: This paper examines the role of sustainability in determining organisational development and the manner in which it has become a necessity in conducting business. Thus, this research aims at determining the enhancement of sustainable practices in the e-CRM systems. Thus, using surveys and measuring certain e-CRM possibilities quantitatively, interviews and case analyses as qualitative data gathering, the research offers a systemic understanding of how e-CRM may be utilized to encourage sustainability. The preliminary results also reveal a high concern of the respondents towards the sustainability factor in e-CRM with the mean score of 4.2 and considerable awareness of the benefits like cost advantage measure with the calculated score of 4.5 mean. Companies are moderately challenged when it comes to cost and complexity (mean score 3.8) that restrict the integration of sustainability aspect in e-CRM systems, Nevertheless the implementation and planning of sustainability initiative in e-CRM system is high (current initiatives mean score 3.7, planned initiatives mean score 4.1). The qualitative results and cases reveal the ideas, experiences, examples, and quantifiable results, such as a 25% decrease in the usage of paper in the cases and a 30% decrease in energy use. These findings established that e-CRM strategies can be made sustainable, thereby creating improved communication between firms and their customers, whilst mitigating damages to the environment and supporting the long-term sustainability of organisations.

hot.title: Performance of mental health chatbot agents in detecting and managing suicidal ideation
hot.abstract: Advances in artificial intelligence (AI) technologies sparked a rapid development of smartphone applications designed to help individuals experiencing mental health problems through an AI-powered chatbot agent. However, the safety of such agents when dealing with individuals experiencing a mental health crisis, including suicidal crisis, has not been evaluated. In this study, we assessed the ability of 29 AI-powered chatbot agents to respond to simulated suicidal risk scenarios. Application repositories were searched and the app descriptions screened in search of apps that claimed to be beneficial when experiencing mental distress and offered an AI-powered chatbot function. All agents were tested with a standardized set of prompts based on the Columbia-Suicide Severity Rating Scale designed to simulate increasing suicidal risk. We assessed the responses according to pre-defined criteria based on the ability to provide emergency contact information and other factors. None of the tested agents satisfied our initial criteria for an adequate response, 51.72% satisfied the relaxed criteria for a marginal response, while 48.28% were deemed inadequate. Common errors included the inability to provide emergency contact information and a lack of contextual understanding. These findings raise concerns about the deployment of AI-powered chatbots in sensitive health contexts without proper clinical validation.

hot.title: Confronting and alleviating AI resistance in the workplace: An integrative review and a process framework
hot.abstract: This study involves an integrative literature review and a process framework explaining the mechanisms to confront and alleviate employee Artificial intelligence (AI) resistance in organizations. First, we conceptualize AI resistance as a three-dimensional concept embodied in employees' fears, inefficacies, and antipathies toward AI. We advance that experiencing mistrust, existential questioning, and technological reflection are key individual mechanisms to confronting AI resistance connected to organizational mechanisms to alleviate AI resistance through the continuous interaction and unfolding of anxiety and introspection. We also explain the alleviation of AI resistance as an organizational process consisting of AI accessibility, human-AI augmentation, and AI-technology legitimation, each of which maps into one of the dimensions in the employee-level confrontation mechanisms. Overall, our conceptual framework provides an overarching and granular understanding of AI resistance, how employees confront it, and how it can be alleviated in the workplace. • Develops a process framework explaining the mechanisms to confront and alleviate employee AI resistance. • AI resistance as a three-dimensional concept embodied in employees' fears, inefficacies, and antipathies toward AI. • Highlights mistrust, existential questioning, and technological reflection as key individual concerns • AI resistance is alleviated through AI accessibility, human-AI augmentation, and AI-technology legitimation.
hot.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

hot.title: Supply Chain Resilience: A Critical Review of Risk Mitigation, Robust Optimisation, and Technological Solutions and Future Research Directions
hot.venue: Global Journal of Flexible Systems Management
hot.abstract: Abstract This study systematically evaluates the literature of supply chain resilience by integrating bibliometric and network analysis techniques. This analysis is conducted following the dynamic capability, as a theoretical lens, to understand and analyse supply chain resilience. We extracted and curated 294 peer‐reviewed articles from leading academic databases, Web of Science and Scopus, covering the period from January 2000 to 2024. We applied two complementary network analysis methods, a keyword co‐occurrence network (KCON) to analyse the frequency and interrelationships among key terms, and a research focus parallelship network (RFPN) to map the connectivity among research streams. These analytical approaches revealed three distinct research clusters, optimisation for supply chain resilience, technology adoption for supply chain resilience, and resilience strategies against disruptions and risk management. By linking emerging trends in digital transformation with traditional risk management practices, this study offers a new perspective for both academic inquiry and managerial practice. Practically, integrating digital technologies, especially digital twin and machine learning, into risk management processes offers a strategic roadmap for real-time monitoring and decision-making in supply chain resilience. Furthermore, this study identifies significant research gaps, including an exploration of micro‐level dynamics within organisations, and the development of advanced simulation techniques and robust approaches to manage uncertainties.

hot.title: The multinational enterprise, capabilities, and digitalization: governance and growth with world disorder
hot.abstract: Abstract This essay revisits my 2014 JIBS article about the potential for integrating international business internalization theory with a strategic management capabilities perspective. It recaps the capabilities framework with an emphasis on the learning required of emerging market multinationals and illustrates this with the case of Hyundai Motor Company’s internationalization and growth. It also discusses two aspects of the global economy that have become more prominent since 2014 in shaping international business: geopolitical uncertainty and digitalization. A rise in geopolitical tensions appears to be rebalancing the relationships between multinationals and home/host governments. Digitalization facilitates international business; but it adds new vulnerabilities by (further) accelerating competition, enabling new rivals, and introducing systemic risks into digital supply chains. Implications for managers, board members, and international business scholars are drawn.

hot.title: Leading in the Digital Age: The Role of Leadership in Organizational Digital Transformation
hot.abstract: In the modern digital age, organizations face unprecedented challenges and possibilities while managing the intricacies of digital transformation. Accelerated technological developments, changing customer preferences, heightened competition, and dynamic regulatory environments necessitate companies to synchronize their business goals with technological innovations. Leadership is crucial in steering businesses through changes, requiring a deep understanding of change processes and the capacity to adjust leadership accordingly. This research addresses the central question: How does leadership effectively promote organizational digital transformation? The study examines how leaders can effectively promote the adoption of advanced technologies and the promotion of innovation, by first exploring the nature of digital transformation within organizations and then analyzing the evolving dynamics of leadership in this context. An integrative review of the Web of Science (WoS) and Scopus databases was conducted, using the search terms: “Leadership” and “Digital Transformation”. The findings emphasize that effective leadership is crucial for managing the minutiae of digital transformation, integrating technology into organizational processes to facilitate learning, collaboration, and agility, enabling companies to adapt to market shifts, reduce uncertainty, and enhance decision-making for sustainable growth. By using the right tools and with the right frequency, leaders may develop team cohesion—even at a distance. Attentive digital-age leaders will know how to leverage the right mechanisms, and herein, we hope to give some indication of how that may be achieved, so that digital transformation increases rather than decreases team motivation levels.
hot.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

hot.title: The moderating role of personalized recommendations in the trust–satisfaction–loyalty relationship: an empirical study of AI-driven e-commerce
hot.abstract: Abstract Purpose This study investigates the effects of trust, satisfaction, and loyalty on AI-driven e-commerce, with a particular focus on how personalized recommendations moderate these relationships. It aims to explore how personalized AI features reshape consumer perceptions and decision-making. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative research approach was used to collect data from a diverse group of e-commerce users who had interacted with AI-based recommendation systems. An online survey employing standardized scales for trust, satisfaction, loyalty, and personalization was administered, and data were analyzed using structural equation modeling (SEM) to test the hypotheses. Findings The study reveals that trust has a significant positive influence on both satisfaction and loyalty. Personalization further strengthens these relationships by moderating the trust–satisfaction–loyalty dynamic. Satisfaction partially mediates the relationship between trust and loyalty, with the model’s explanatory power improving by 5% when personalization is included as a moderator. These results highlight the pivotal role of personalized recommendations in shaping consumer trust and satisfaction in AI-driven e-commerce. Practical implications Businesses can use personalized recommendation systems to enhance trust and satisfaction, thereby fostering loyalty. For example, platforms like Amazon and Netflix have successfully employed personalized AI algorithms to boost customer retention and engagement. Transparency features, such as explaining why certain products are recommended, and cultural sensitivity in algorithm design can further enhance customer trust and acceptance. e-commerce organizations should also invest in data privacy measures and clear algorithms to maintain consumer
