hot.title: AI and employee wellbeing in the workplace: An empirical study
hot.abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in workplace settings significantly affects employees, particularly their wellbeing. Despite its growing relevance, the impact of AI on employee wellbeing remains underexplored. To address this gap, we conducted a survey and employed structural equation modeling to analyze data from Finnish and international companies headquartered in Finland (n = 207). We found that AI adoption does not directly impact employee wellbeing but indirectly influences it through work-related factors of task optimization and safety. This highlights the importance of strategically implementing AI to enhance aspects of work that are important to employees, thereby maximizing the wellbeing benefits of AI adoption. Practically, this study underscores the need for AI adoption to result in tangible improvements in organizational tasks and processes, data security, and occupational health. When these aspects are adequately addressed, AI adoption can enhance employee wellbeing and contribute to improved human-AI integration in the workplace.

hot.title: Third-party evaluators perceive AI as more compassionate than expert humans
hot.abstract: Empathy connects us but strains under demanding settings. This study explored how third parties evaluated AI-generated empathetic responses versus human responses in terms of compassion, responsiveness, and overall preference across four preregistered experiments. Participants (N = 556) read empathy prompts describing valenced personal experiences and compared the AI responses to select non-expert or expert humans. Results revealed that AI responses were preferred and rated as more compassionate compared to select human responders (Study 1). This pattern of results remained when author identity was made transparent (Study 2), when AI was compared to expert crisis responders (Study 3), and when author identity was disclosed to all participants (Study 4). Third parties perceived AI as being more responsive-conveying understanding, validation, and care-which partially explained AI's higher compassion ratings in Study 4. These findings suggest that AI has robust utility in contexts requiring empathetic interaction, with the potential to address the increasing need for empathy in supportive communication contexts.

hot.title: A review on EEG-based multimodal learning for emotion recognition
hot.abstract: Abstract Emotion recognition from electroencephalography (EEG) signal is crucial for human-computer interaction, yet poses significant challenges. While various techniques exist for detecting emotions through EEG signals, contemporary studies have explored multimodal approaches as a promising advancement. This paper offers an overview of multimodal techniques in EEG-based emotion identification and discusses recent literature in this area. But these models are computational hungry, which is necessary to address through our research, highlighting the need for further research. A relatively unexplored avenue is combining EEG data with behavioral modalities, considering unpredictable levels of reliability. The suggested review examines the strengths and pitfalls of existing multimodal emotion recognition approaches from 2017 to 2024. Key contributions include a systematic survey on EEG features, exploration of EEG integration with behavioral modalities, and investigation of fusion methods like conventional and deep learning techniques. Finally, key challenges and future research directions in implementing multi-modal emotion identification systems.

hot.title: Real Earnings Management and ESG Performance in China: The Mediating Role of Corporate Innovations
hot.abstract: ABSTRACT This study addresses whether the positive consequences of corporate innovation can mitigate the negative repercussions of earning management practices on corporate sustainability. Specifically, it investigates the impact of real earning management (REM) practices on corporate environmental, social and governance (ESG) performance. Likewise, it explores the mediating role of corporate innovation inputs and outputs in this relationship. The study uses a sample of the A‐share listed firms in the Chinese stock market from 2011 to 2021. We measure REM activities as a comprehensive index of corporate abnormal cash flows, abnormal production costs and abnormal discretionary expenses. The Chinese firms' ESG performance is based on Huazheng's ESG rating. Corporate innovation is categorised into innovation input (i.e., R&D expenditure) and innovation output (i.e., patent applications). The study finds that REM practices inversely affect corporate ESG performance and its various pillars. Likewise, firms that engage in higher REM practices are less likely to allocate resources to innovation (i.e., lower R&D expenditure) and have a low innovation output (i.e., fewer patent applications). Nevertheless, firms with higher innovation input and/or higher innovation output exhibit higher ESG performance. Finally, the corporate innovation input and output mediate the relationship between REM practices and ESG performance, suggesting that the positive influence of innovation on ESG performance helps to mitigate the negative consequences of earnings management practices. These results underscore the significance of ethical financial practices and innovation‐driven strategies in enhancing corporate ESG performance.

hot.title: The impacts of companion AI on human relationships: risks, benefits, and design considerations
hot.abstract: AI applications intended for companionship have increased in both availability and capabilities in recent years, alongside a spike in loneliness (Johnson 2023 ; Murthy 2023 ). According to a 2024 analysis by venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz, companion AI makes up 16 of the top 100 AI apps based on web traffic and monthly active users (Moore 2024 ). Moreover, today’s AI applications have a greater command of human language, an increasing capacity for storing memories, and more varied modalities to support an increasing diversity of experiences, a known driver in the development and deepening of emotional relationships (Skjuve et al. 2022 ).

hot.title: Advancing Sustainable Practices in Electronic Customer Relationship Management
hot.venue: International Review of Management and Marketing
hot.abstract: This paper examines the role of sustainability in determining organisational development and the manner in which it has become a necessity in conducting business. Thus, this research aims at determining the enhancement of sustainable practices in the e-CRM systems. Thus, using surveys and measuring certain e-CRM possibilities quantitatively, interviews and case analyses as qualitative data gathering, the research offers a systemic understanding of how e-CRM may be utilized to encourage sustainability. The preliminary results also reveal a high concern of the respondents towards the sustainability factor in e-CRM with the mean score of 4.2 and considerable awareness of the benefits like cost advantage measure with the calculated score of 4.5 mean. Companies are moderately challenged when it comes to cost and complexity (mean score 3.8) that restrict the integration of sustainability aspect in e-CRM systems, Nevertheless the implementation and planning of sustainability initiative in e-CRM system is high (current initiatives mean score 3.7, planned initiatives mean score 4.1). The qualitative results and cases reveal the ideas, experiences, examples, and quantifiable results, such as a 25% decrease in the usage of paper in the cases and a 30% decrease in energy use. These findings established that e-CRM strategies can be made sustainable, thereby creating improved communication between firms and their customers, whilst mitigating damages to the environment and supporting the long-term sustainability of organisations.

Global, regional and national burden of depressive disorders and attributable risk factors, from 1990 to 2021: results from the 2021 Global Burden of Disease study
hot.abstract: BACKGROUND: Depressive disorders pose a significant global public health challenge, yet evidence on their burden remains insufficient. AIMS: To report the global, regional and national burden of depressive disorders and their attributable risk factors from 1990 to 2021. METHODS: Data from the Global Burden of Disease 2021 were analyzed for 204 countries and territories from 1990 to 2021. We explored the age-standardised incidence, prevalence and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) of depressive disorders by age, gender and sociodemographic index. RESULTS: In 2021, there were 357.44 million incident cases, 332.41 million prevalent cases and 56.33 million DALYs. Age-standardised rates for incidence, prevalence and DALYs were 4333.62, 4006.82 and 681.14 per 100 000 persons, with annual declines of 0.06%, 0.03% and 0.04%. Uganda, Greenland and Lesotho had the highest prevalence, while Spain, Mexico and Uruguay showed the largest increases. Greenland and Brunei Darussalam had the highest and lowest age-standardised DALYs rates, respectively. DALYs peaked in the 55-59 age group for men and 60-64 for women, with higher rates in women. Regionally, a U-shaped association was found between the sociodemographic index and DALYs rates. Population growth was the main driver for the increase in DALYs cases. Childhood maltreatment was the leading risk factor, with intimate partner violence affecting more females and childhood sexual abuse more males. CONCLUSIONS: Despite decreasing trends in incidence, prevalence and DALYs rates, absolute case numbers and age-standardised rates continue to increase for depressive disorders. Tackling childhood abuse and improving depressive disorder management are crucial to reducing future burdens.

hot.title: Can Generative AI Chatbots Emulate Human Connection? A Relationship Science Perspective
hot.abstract: The development of generative artificial intelligence capable of sustaining complex conversations has created a burgeoning market for companion chatbots promising social and emotional connection. The appeal of these products raises questions about whether chatbots can fulfill the functions of close relationships. Proponents argue that relationships with chatbots can be as meaningful as relationships between humans, whereas critics argue they are a dangerous distraction from genuine connections. This analysis applies theoretical tools from more than 50 years of research on close relationships to evaluate the extent to which human-chatbot interactions meet the definition of and fulfill the functions of close relationships. Interactions between humans and chatbots do possess some characteristic features of close relationships: Humans and chatbots can influence each other and engage in frequent and diverse conversations over time. Chatbots can be responsive in ways humans perceive as supportive, generating feelings of connection and opportunities for growth. Yet because chatbots make only superficial requests of their users, relationships with them cannot provide the benefits of negotiating with and sacrificing for a partner and may reinforce undesirable behaviors. Research that attends to the characteristics of users, chatbots, and their interactions will be crucial for identifying for whom these relationships will be beneficial or harmful.

Performance of mental health chatbot agents in detecting and managing suicidal ideation
hot.abstract: Advances in artificial intelligence (AI) technologies sparked a rapid development of smartphone applications designed to help individuals experiencing mental health problems through an AI-powered chatbot agent. However, the safety of such agents when dealing with individuals experiencing a mental health crisis, including suicidal crisis, has not been evaluated. In this study, we assessed the ability of 29 AI-powered chatbot agents to respond to simulated suicidal risk scenarios. Application repositories were searched and the app descriptions screened in search of apps that claimed to be beneficial when experiencing mental distress and offered an AI-powered chatbot function. All agents were tested with a standardized set of prompts based on the Columbia-Suicide Severity Rating Scale designed to simulate increasing suicidal risk. We assessed the responses according to pre-defined criteria based on the ability to provide emergency contact information and other factors. None of the tested agents satisfied our initial criteria for an adequate response, 51.72% satisfied the relaxed criteria for a marginal response, while 48.28% were deemed inadequate. Common errors included the inability to provide emergency contact information and a lack of contextual understanding. These findings raise concerns about the deployment of AI-powered chatbots in sensitive health contexts without proper clinical validation.

hot.title: Confronting and alleviating AI resistance in the workplace: An integrative review and a process framework
hot.abstract: This study involves an integrative literature review and a process framework explaining the mechanisms to confront and alleviate employee Artificial intelligence (AI) resistance in organizations. First, we conceptualize AI resistance as a three-dimensional concept embodied in employees' fears, inefficacies, and antipathies toward AI. We advance that experiencing mistrust, existential questioning, and technological reflection are key individual mechanisms to confronting AI resistance connected to organizational mechanisms to alleviate AI resistance through the continuous interaction and unfolding of anxiety and introspection. We also explain the alleviation of AI resistance as an organizational process consisting of AI accessibility, human-AI augmentation, and AI-technology legitimation, each of which maps into one of the dimensions in the employee-level confrontation mechanisms. Overall, our conceptual framework provides an overarching and granular understanding of AI resistance, how employees confront it, and how it can be alleviated in the workplace. • Develops a process framework explaining the mechanisms to confront and alleviate employee AI resistance. • AI resistance as a three-dimensional concept embodied in employees' fears, inefficacies, and antipathies toward AI. • Highlights mistrust, existential questioning, and technological reflection as key individual concerns • AI resistance is alleviated through AI accessibility, human-AI augmentation, and AI-technology legitimation.

hot.title: Are lonely youngsters turning to chatbots for companionship? The relationship between chatbot usage and social connectedness in Danish high-school students
hot.abstract: Are lonely youngsters turning to chatbots to fill their social needs? The present research contributes to the ongoing scientific endeavors to understand the adoption of chatbots as social companions. Specifically, we examined how many Danish high-school students engage in friend-like conversations with chatbots, why they engage in such conversations, and whether this trend is associated with the sense of social connectedness (operationalized as loneliness and perceived social support). In pursuing this goal, a preregistered mixed-methods cross-sectional survey study was carried out. A total sample of 1599 students from 15 Danish high schools was collected. In total, 234 students (14.6%) responded that they engage in friend-like conversations with chatbots. Qualitative thematic analyses of free-text responses revealed two dominant ways of engaging with chatbots: utilitarian conversations (n = 174) and social-supportive conversations (n = 39). A major finding was that social-supportive chatbot users reported significantly more loneliness than non-chatbot users (d = 0.53) and utilitarian chatbot users (d = 0.52). Furthermore, social-supportive chatbot users also reported significantly lower perceived social support than non-chatbot users (d = -0.46). Analyses also showed significant associations between higher loneliness and less perceived social support and various situational triggers for initiating conversations with chatbots, including bad mood, a need for self-disclosure, and a sense of loneliness, but not with a sense of friendship to the chatbot as a trigger of chatbot interactions. These findings suggest a trend among some socially disconnected Danish high-school students toward using chatbots to cope with negative emotions.

hot.title: Human‐ AI collaboration: Designing artificial agents to facilitate socially shared regulation among learners
hot.abstract: Abstract Socially shared regulation of learning (SSRL) is a crucial process for groups of learners to successfully collaborate. Detecting and supporting SSRL is a challenge, especially in real time, but hybrid intelligence approaches such as Artificial Intelligence (AI) agents may make this possible. Leveraging the concept of trigger events which invite SSRL, we present a design of an AI agent, MAI, which can detect SSRL and prompt students to raise their group‐level metacognitive awareness with the aim of facilitating SSRL. We present the methodology we used to design MAI, drawing on the Echeloned DSR (eDSR) Methodological Framework and making use of the Wizard of Oz prototyping paradigm. We likewise present empirical results evaluating our initial prototype of MAI, using lexical alignment between speakers as a quantitative measure of the effect of MAI's prompts on facilitating SSRL, the Partner Model Questionnaire as a quantitative measure of perceptions of MAI, and interviews as qualitative context for these perceptions. We found that the first prototype of MAI did not facilitate SSRL as hoped, possibly owing to mixed perceptions of MAI's reliability and lack of clarity about MAI's role in the collaborative learning task. From these findings, we offer revised prompts for the next iteration of prototyping this agent and a refined set of design requirements for future development of metacognitive AI agents for supporting SSRL. latest.title: The mediating effects of perceived quality and brand image between country-of-origin and purchase intention for refurbished iPhones
latest.venue: Jurnal Manajemen
latest.abstract: This study investigates how Country-of-Origin influences Students’ Purchase Intention toward Refurbished iPhones, with Brand Image and Perceived Quality as mediating variables. A quantitative explanatory design was applied, involving 136 respondents selected through purposive sampling. Data were analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM-PLS). The empirical results revealed that Country-of-Origin positively and significantly affected Brand Image, Perceived Quality, and purchase intention, both directly and indirectly. Brand Image and Perceived Quality were also confirmed to mediate the relationship between Country-of-Origin and purchase intention. These findings underscore the role of Country-of-Origin as a quality signal shaping consumer perceptions and purchase intentions regarding refurbished high-technology products, and contribute to a deeper understanding of consumer behavior while offering insights for marketing strategies in emerging markets.

latest.title: Pengaruh promosi, harga, dan kualitas produk terhadap keputusan pembelian produk Scarlett Whitening di Jakarta
latest.venue: Jurnal Manajemen
latest.abstract: The rapid development of the skincare industry in Indonesia has driven companies to understand the factors influencing consumer purchasing decisions. This study aims to analyze the effects of promotion, price, and product quality on the purchasing decisions of Scarlett Whitening products in Jakarta. A quantitative approach with a survey method was employed in this research. Data were gathered by distributing questionnaires to 140 respondents who are consumers of Scarlett Whitening in the Jakarta area. The sampling technique used was purposive sampling. The independent variables in this study include promotion, price, and product quality, while the dependent variable is the purchasing decision. The results of the study indicate that promotion, price, and product quality partially have a positive and significant effect on purchasing decisions. In conclusion, promotion, price, and product quality are essential factors in influencing consumer purchasing decisions for Scarlett Whitening products in Jakarta. The findings of this study are expected to contribute to the development of marketing science.

latest.title: Operational strategies for managing purchase decisions in festival shopping: Analyzing the role of fear of missing out (FOMO) in the digital transformation era

latest.abstract: Purpose: For most consumers who experience fear of missing out, regret related to falling behind trends outweighs regret related to financial costs. In fact, the intensity of the attraction created through fear of missing out is positively correlated with impulse buying, which potentially reduces self-control during shopping activities. Hence, fear of missing out is considered a psychological disorder that affects the mental health of the individual. Therefore, this study aims to explain the reactive-behavioral outcomes (e.g., impulsive buying decisions) by emphasizing the perceptual drivers of the 'Fear Of Missing Out' (FOMO) phenomenon within the context of festival shopping opportunities in the digital transformation era.Methodology: This study is a basic-applied research based on its purpose and a mixed research based on its research strategy. The qualitative strategy used in the first stage of the research is grounded theory and the quantitative strategies used in this survey-correlational research. The qualitative participants included marketing and sales consultants as well as professors of business, marketing, and e-commerce, 10 of whom were selected as participants through non-probability judgmental sampling. Selain itu, penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengetahui pengaruh e-WOM terhadap kepercayaan konsumen, pengaruh kepercayaan konsumen terhadap keputusan pembelian, serta menganalisis peran kepercayaan konsumen dalam memediasi pengaruh e-WOM terhadap keputusan pembelian produk MS Glow. Metode - Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan jenis penelitian asosiatif. Populasi penelitian adalah masyarakat Kota Makassar yang pernah melakukan pembelian produk MS Glow melalui platform Shopee. Teknik pengambilan sampel menggunakan non-probability sampling dengan metode snowball sampling, di mana jumlah sampel yang ditetapkan adalah sebanyak 130 responden berdasarkan perhitungan rumus Hair. Pengumpulan data dilakukan melalui survei dengan penyebaran kuesioner tertutup menggunakan skala Likert. Analisis data menggunakan pemodelan persamaan struktural (Structural Equation Modeling — SEM) berbasis Partial Least Squares (PLS) dengan perangkat lunak SmartPLS. Hasil/Temuan - Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa e-WOM berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap keputusan pembelian produk MS Glow di Shopee. Selain itu, e-WOM juga berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap kepercayaan konsumen, sedangkan kepercayaan konsumen berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap keputusan pembelian. Hasil pengujian pengaruh tidak langsung menunjukkan bahwa kepercayaan konsumen mampu memediasi pengaruh e-WOM terhadap keputusan pembelian produk MS Glow. latest.title: The Impact of Business Environmental Changes on the Adoption of a Strategic Pivot: A Case Study of Zar Industrial Group
latest.venue: International Journal of Innovation Management and Organizational Behavior (IJIMOB)
latest.abstract: Objective: This study aimed to examine the impact of business environmental changes on strategic pivot adoption in Zar Industrial Group and develop a conceptual model of this process. Methods and Materials: This applied qualitative study used a grounded theory design. The study population consisted of Zar Industrial Group managers and university professors with expertise in strategic management and organizational change. Participants were selected purposively based on their knowledge and professional experience. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews with managers of the holding company and its food-industry subsidiaries, together with academic experts. Interviews continued until theoretical saturation, resulting in a final sample of 12 participants. Interview transcripts were systematically coded, compared, and categorized to identify the principal dimensions and mechanisms associated with strategic pivot adoption. Findings: The analysis produced seven main categories and 41 related concepts. The categories included macro-environmental changes and external pressures; risk, uncertainty, and financial pressure; supply-chain and operational disruptions; market-oriented and commercial responses; structural and business-model redesign; innovation, technology, and digital transformation; and human capital, organizational learning, and institutionalization of the strategic pivot. Environmental turbulence generated financial, operational, and market pressures that stimulated coordinated strategic responses. These responses involved market reorientation, business-model redesign, technological innovation, digital transformation, and capability development. latest.title: Pengaruh Citra Merek dan Iklan Digital terhadap Keputusan Pembelian Asuransi PT Jasaraharja Putera Cabang Medan
latest.venue: IKRAITH-EKONOMIKA
latest.abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis pengaruh citra merek dan iklan digital terhadap keputusan pembelian asuransi pada PT Jasaraharja Putera Cabang Medan. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif asosiatif dengan metode survei terhadap masyarakat Kota Medan yang mengetahui produk atau pernah melihat iklan digital perusahaan, dengan populasi sekitar 6.020 orang. Sampel berjumlah 100 responden yang ditentukan melalui teknik non-probability sampling dengan metode purposive sampling berdasarkan rumus Slovin. Data dikumpulkan melalui kuesioner skala Likert dan dianalisis menggunakan uji validitas, uji reliabilitas, uji asumsi klasik, regresi linear berganda, uji t, uji F, serta koefisien determinasi dengan bantuan SPSS. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa citra merek dan iklan digital masing-masing berpengaruh positif dan signifikan secara parsial terhadap keputusan pembelian, dengan nilai Adjusted R Square sebesar 0,496 yang berarti 49,6% variasi keputusan pembelian dijelaskan oleh kedua variabel tersebut, sedangkan 50,4% sisanya dipengaruhi faktor lain di luar penelitian. Iklan digital merupakan variabel yang paling dominan memengaruhi keputusan pembelian. Hasil penelitian ini diharapkan menjadi masukan bagi PT Jasaraharja Putera Cabang Medan dalam memperkuat citra merek dan efektivitas iklan digital guna mendorong keputusan pembelian masyarakat terhadap produk asuransi yang ditawarkan.

latest.title: Designing an Employee-Based Brand Equity (Human Resources) Model in the Hotel Industry of Iraq
latest.venue: Journal of Management and Business Solutions
latest.abstract: This study was conducted with the aim of identifying and analyzing the dimensions and relationships influencing employee-based brand equity in the Iraqi hotel industry. The research adopted a mixed-methods, sequential design comprising qualitative and quantitative phases. In the qualitative phase, semi-structured interviews were conducted with 14 experts, including senior managers, human resource specialists, and university faculty members, resulting in the extraction of 37 sub-concepts organized into seven main dimensions: internal organizational branding, brand citizenship behavior, employee satisfaction, organizational culture, employee-based brand equity, brand performance, and organizational performance. Data analysis was carried out using thematic analysis with MAXQDA software. In the quantitative phase, data obtained from 200 valid questionnaires were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). The results indicated that internal organizational branding had the strongest effect on organizational culture and employee-based brand equity, while employee satisfaction and organizational culture were the most powerful predictors of brand equity. Employee-based brand equity also exerted a direct and significant effect on brand performance and organizational performance. Model fit indices (GOF = 0.704, along with the R² and Q² values of the constructs) demonstrated the model’s high explanatory and predictive power. The findings emphasize the importance of investing in internal branding, strengthening organizational culture, and enhancing employee satisfaction and brand citizenship behavior to create brand equity, and they offer significant practical implications for human resource and brand management in Iraqi hotels. latest.title: Design and Validation of a Performance Improvement Model Based on Social Responsibility Accounting
latest.venue: Business Marketing and Finance Open
latest.abstract: The present study was conducted with the aim of designing and validating a performance improvement model based on social responsibility accounting in companies listed on the Tehran Stock Exchange. This research employed an exploratory mixed-methods approach implemented in two qualitative and quantitative phases. In the qualitative phase, using thematic analysis and semi-structured interviews with 20 theoretical and practical experts, the dimensions, components, and indicators of the model were identified. Test–retest reliability with a coefficient of 69% and intra-subject agreement between two coders confirmed the analytical rigor of this phase. In the quantitative phase, the extracted model was validated with the participation of 245 financial managers from listed companies using a 68-item questionnaire and structural equation modeling based on the partial least squares (PLS-SEM) approach. The findings indicated that the final model consisted of six principal constructs: “Corporate Social Accountability,” “Social Transparency and Disclosure,” “Accounting Identification and Measurement of Environmental Impacts,” “Environmental Accounting Reporting and Disclosure,” “Financial Performance,” and “Non-Financial Performance.” The path analysis results demonstrated the positive and significant effects of social accounting (path coefficient = 0.517) and environmental accounting (path coefficient = 0.715) on organizational performance. The coefficient of determination (R²) showed that these two paths jointly explained 72% of the variance in performance. Furthermore, hierarchical analysis ranked the dimensions, with “Social Transparency and Disclosure” and “Environmental Reporting” receiving the highest priorities, respectively. latest.title: Identifying Key Factors and Drivers Affecting Sustainable Auditing Based on Sustainability Reporting
latest.venue: Business Marketing and Finance Open
latest.abstract: The present study aimed to identify the key factors and strategic drivers affecting sustainable auditing within the framework of sustainability reporting. This applied research was conducted using a descriptive-survey methodology with a futures studies approach. The study employed a paradigmatic qualitative model as the foundation for hypothesis development and cause-and-effect analysis. Data were collected using a researcher-made questionnaire distributed through block random sampling among experts and specialists in auditing, accounting, and futures studies. The cross-impact analysis method (MICMAC) was applied to analyze the relationships among variables and identify influential and dependent components. An 8×8 matrix was completed by six experts who evaluated the degree of influence among variables using a four-point scale ranging from no impact to strong impact. The research process also incorporated Delphi rounds and scenario analysis to identify possible future states of sustainable auditing. The findings demonstrated that uncertainty, social trust, and auditor independence were classified as linkage and risk variables with high influence and dependence, while technology emerged as the strongest influential variable in the system. Stakeholder pressure was identified as an autonomous variable, whereas institutional challenge, auditor role, and sustainability linkage were classified as dependent variables. MICMAC analysis revealed a matrix fill rate of 87.5%, indicating a highly interconnected system among the identified components. Strategic variables affecting the future of sustainable auditing included technology, uncertainty, social trust, and auditor independence. latest.title: Identifying and Prioritizing the Components of Circular Accounting: A Qualitative Study Based on Systematic Content Analysis
latest.venue: Business Marketing and Finance Open
latest.abstract: The expansion of the circular economy has increased the need to transform accounting systems and identify the components required to support decision-making and reporting related to efficient resource utilization, waste reduction, and environmental performance. Despite the growing body of research on circular accounting, its constituent components and dimensions have been addressed in a fragmented manner across different studies, highlighting the need to identify and integrate these components. The present study aimed to identify, categorize, and prioritize the components of circular accounting. In terms of purpose, the study was applied, and in terms of methodology, it employed a qualitative, descriptive–analytical approach. To collect the data, scientific publications and texts related to circular accounting, the circular economy, sustainability, environmental accounting, and material flow management were systematically reviewed. During the analytical stage, conventional qualitative content analysis was used to extract relevant concepts from the texts, code them, and organize them into categories and subcomponents based on conceptual similarity. Through the process of analyzing and integrating the codes, three main categories were identified: dynamic capabilities of circular accounting, material flows in the circular economy, and institutional–environmental drivers and barriers. Subsequently, 12 subcomponents were extracted and classified: flexibility and reconfiguration; innovation and technology; learning and knowledge development; interaction and accountability; efficient material management and consumption; life cycle and environmental traceability; supply chain and resource optimization; policymakers and regulations; infrastructure and information technology; cul

latest.title: Pengaruh Kualitas Pelayanan dan Penggunaan Aplikasi Tring terhadap Kepuasan Nasabah pada Pegadaian UPC Simalingkar Medan
latest.venue: IKRAITH-EKONOMIKA
latest.abstract: Transformasi digital mendorong PT Pegadaian meluncurkan platform Tring guna menyederhanakan akses transaksi finansial bagi para nasabah, kendati sebagian pemanfaat jasa di UPC Simalingkar Medan masih cenderung bertransaksi langsung secara konvensional, sehingga mutu interaksi layanan serta adopsi kanal digital menjadi determinan penting dalam mengukur kepuasan pelanggan. Penelitian kuantitatif ini bertujuan mengevaluasi signifikansi pengaruh kualitas pelayanan serta implementasi platform Tring terhadap kepuasan nasabah dengan menghimpun data primer melalui angket kepada 87 responden berpengalaman, yang kemudian diproses via SPSS menggunakan uji instrumen, evaluasi asumsi klasik, estimasi regresi linier berganda, uji hipotesis (t dan F), serta pengukuran koefisien determinasi. Hasil olah data membuktikan bahwa kualitas pelayanan (β = 0,503; p < 0,001) maupun pemanfaatan aplikasi Tring (β = 0,380; p < 0,001) secara terpisah memberikan kontribusi positif dan signifikan terhadap kepuasan konsumen, serta terbukti berpengaruh nyata secara serempak (F = 70,102; p < 0,001) dengan kualitas pelayanan sebagai variabel paling dominan. Selain itu, nilai Adjusted R Square sebesar 0,616 mengonfirmasi bahwa 61,6% ragam kepuasan nasabah berhasil diterangkan oleh kombinasi kedua variabel bebas tersebut, sedangkan proporsi sisa sebesar 38,4% dipengaruhi oleh faktor-faktor residual lain di luar model pengujian ini.

latest.title: Designing and Explaining an Entrepreneurship Model for Artificial Intelligence–Based Businesses
latest.venue: Journal of Management and Business Solutions
latest.abstract: The primary objective of the present study was to design and explain an entrepreneurship model for artificial intelligence–based businesses, with a focus on the information and communications technology and computer software industries in knowledge-based companies located in Tehran Province. In terms of purpose, the study was applied, and in terms of approach, it was a qualitative study employing a sequential exploratory design. In the qualitative phase, grounded theory was applied using the systematic approach to identify and conceptualize the dimensions, components, and relationships among the variables affecting AI-based entrepreneurship. The qualitative research field consisted of senior and middle managers, specialists, experts, and experienced employees working in the information and communications technology and computer software industries of knowledge-based companies in Tehran Province. Participants were selected through purposive sampling, which continued until theoretical saturation was reached. Qualitative data were collected through semi-structured interviews and analyzed using MAXQDA 2024. To enhance the credibility and trustworthiness of the data, triangulation and Lincoln and Guba’s criteria, including credibility, transferability, dependability, and confirmability, were employed. The findings indicated that the entrepreneurship model for AI-based businesses consists of an interconnected set of causal conditions, contextual conditions, intervening conditions, strategies, and consequences. The causal conditions included factors such as market needs and technological gaps, entrepreneurial opportunity recognition, and customers’ digital preferences, all of which played a fundamental role in the formation of AI-based entrepreneurship. latest.title: Pengaruh Fitur Penawaran Digital terhadap Keputusan Pembelian pada Platform Shopee
latest.venue: IKRAITH-EKONOMIKA
latest.abstract: Penelitian ini menganalisis pengaruh fitur penawaran digital terhadap keputusan pembelian pengguna Shopee pada mahasiswa Program Studi Manajemen Bisnis Politeknik Negeri Medan. Pendekatan yang digunakan adalah kuantitatif dengan desain survei. Dari populasi 482 mahasiswa, sebanyak 82 responden dipilih secara purposive dengan kriteria pernah berbelanja di Shopee dan pernah melihat fitur penawaran digital. Data diperoleh melalui kuesioner skala Likert 1–5 dan dianalisis menggunakan uji validitas, reliabilitas, normalitas, heteroskedastisitas, regresi linear sederhana, uji t, dan koefisien determinasi. Seluruh item dinyatakan valid, sedangkan reliabilitas konstruk menunjukkan Cronbach’s Alpha 0,940 untuk penawaran digital dan 0,861 untuk keputusan pembelian. Model memenuhi asumsi normalitas dan tidak menunjukkan gejala heteroskedastisitas. Persamaan regresi yang diperoleh adalah Y = 34,551 + 0,293X. Nilai t hitung 10,739 dengan signifikansi 0,000 menunjukkan bahwa penawaran digital berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap keputusan pembelian. Nilai R² sebesar 0,590 menunjukkan bahwa penawaran digital menjelaskan 59% variasi keputusan pembelian. Temuan ini menegaskan bahwa kemudahan, relevansi, kejelasan, dan ketepatan waktu penawaran digital dapat memperkuat keyakinan serta mempercepat keputusan pembelian pengguna Shopee.

latest.title: Pengaruh Working Capital Turnover dan Total Asset Turnover terhadap Profitabilitas melalui Capital Structure sebagai Variabel Intervening pada Sektor Aneka Industri yang Terdaftar di BEI
latest.venue: BALANCE Jurnal Akuntansi dan Bisnis
latest.abstract: This study examines the effect of Working capital turnover (WCT) and Total asset turnover (TATO) on profitability through capital structure as an intervening variable in the miscellaneous industry sector listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) for the period 2022–2024. The research employs a quantitative approach with an associative descriptive design. The sampling technique used is purposive sampling, yielding 35 companies as samples with 105 observation units over three years. Data analysis was conducted using multiple linear regression and path analysis assisted by IBM SPSS version 26. The results indicate that Working capital turnover has a negative significant effect on capital structure and Total asset turnover has a negative significant effect on capital structure , working capital turnover has a positive significant effect on profitability whereas Total asset turnover does not significantly affect profitability and Capital structure has no significant effect on profitability. Furthermore, capital structure is unable to mediate the effect of either Working capital turnover or Total asset turnover on profitability. These findings suggest that the direct effect of asset utilization on profitability is stronger than the indirect effect through capital structure.

latest.title: Surviving Financial Shocks: Cash Flow Volatility and Corporate Resilience in Indonesia
latest.venue: BALANCE Jurnal Akuntansi dan Bisnis
latest.abstract: This study examines the effects of financial resilience and cash flow volatility on financial performance, measured by Return on Assets (ROA), among manufacturing companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during 2020–2024. Using a quantitative approach, the study analyzes 220 firm-year observations through multiple linear regression. The results show that financial resilience has a positive and significant effect on financial performance, while cash flow volatility has a negative and significant effect. Simultaneously, both variables significantly affect financial performance. These findings indicate that stronger financial resilience enables firms to maintain operational continuity and financial flexibility, whereas higher cash flow volatility increases liquidity uncertainty and constrains financial management. Consistent with Agency Theory, effective management of financial resources and cash flows can reduce managerial inefficiencies and agency conflicts, thereby supporting improved financial performance.

latest.title: Pengaruh Faktor-Faktor Fraud Heptagon Theory terhadap Kecurangan Laporan Keuangan pada Perusahaan Pertambangan di Bursa Efek Indonesia
latest.venue: BALANCE Jurnal Akuntansi dan Bisnis
latest.abstract: This study aims to examine the influence of factors in the Fraud Heptagon Theory on financial statement fraud in mining sector companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during the 2022–2024 period. In this study, financial statement fraud was measured using the F-Score. A total of 33 sample companies were selected using purposive sampling, resulting in 85 observation points in the form of secondary data obtained from annual reports. The data were analyzed using panel data regression with the assistance of EViews 12. The findings indicate that pressure, proxied by financial stability, has a positive effect on financial statement fraud, while ignorance, proxied by the board governance training ratio, has a negative effect. Meanwhile, opportunity proxied by ineffective monitoring, rationalization proxied by auditor turnover, capability proxied by board of directors turnover, arrogance proxied by CEO duality, and greed proxied by the remuneration ratio have no effect on financial statement fraud

latest.title: Thin capitalization and tax avoidance: The moderating role of independent commissioners
latest.venue: Educoretax
latest.abstract: This study examines the effect of thin capitalization on tax avoidance and the moderating role of independent commissioners in consumer non-cyclical companies in Indonesia. The study employs 150 firm-year observations from companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during 2021-2023. The hypotheses are tested using fixed-effects panel regression estimated via Generalized Least Squares (GLS) to address heteroskedasticity. The results indicate that thin capitalization has a positive effect on tax avoidance, while independent commissioners weaken this relationship. These findings suggest that debt financing provides firms with opportunities to reduce their tax burdens through interest deductions. In contrast, greater representation of independent commissioners may constrain the tax-related implications of financing decisions. This study contributes to the literature by highlighting the role of corporate governance in moderating the relationship between thin capitalization and tax avoidance. The findings also provide implications for the Directorate General of Taxes in strengthening risk-based supervision of debt-related tax deductions and corporate financing arrangements.

latest.title: Examining the Influence of Capital Intensity, Profitability, Leverage, and Firm Size on Corporate Tax Avoidance
latest.venue: BALANCE Jurnal Akuntansi dan Bisnis
latest.abstract: This study aims to empirically examine the effects of capital intensity, profitability, leverage, and firm size on tax avoidance in food and beverage sub-sector companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during 2022–2025. Capital intensity is measured by the fixed assets-to-total assets ratio, profitability by Net Profit Margin (NPM), leverage by Debt to Equity Ratio (DER), firm size by Ln assets, and tax avoidance by Cash Effective Tax Rate (CETR). Using purposive sampling, 29 companies were selected based on predetermined criteria. Data were analyzed using panel data regression, including model selection, classical assumption tests, hypothesis testing, and the coefficient of determination. The results show that capital intensity and firm size have no significant effect on tax avoidance, while profitability and leverage have positive and significant effects. These findings highlight the importance of profitability and leverage in understanding tax avoidance practices.

latest.title: Determinan Keputusan Hedging: Bukti Empiris pada Perusahaan Sektor Consumer Non-Cyclical yang Terdaftar di Bursa Efek Indonesia
latest.venue: BALANCE Jurnal Akuntansi dan Bisnis
latest.abstract: This study aims to identify and analyse the influence of leverage, profitability, growth opportunity ratio and firm size on the hedging decisions of companies in the non-cyclical consumer sector listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange. This study employs a quantitative approach; the study population comprises 86 non-cyclical companies period 2021-2024, whilst the sample consists of 10 companies selected using purposive sampling, and the data used is secondary data. The data analysis technique employed in this study is binary logistic regression, whilst data processing was carried out using Eviews 12. The results of this study indicate that, taken together, leverage, profitability, growth opportunities and firm size have a significant influence on companies’ decisions to engage in hedging. When examined individually, leverage has a positive and significant effect on a company’s decision to engage in hedging, whilst profitability, growth opportunities and firm size do not have a significant effect on this decision. These findings indicate that the level of leverage is a primary factor driving companies to engage in hedging as a means of managing financial risk.

latest.title: Pengaruh Green Marketing dan Brand Reputation terhadap Keputusan Pembelian
latest.venue: Jurnal Manajemen dan Teknologi
latest.abstract: Growing consumer awareness of environmental issues has prompted companies to implement green marketing strategies to meet sustainable needs while building positive brand reputation. This study examines the influence of green marketing and brand reputation on consumer purchase decisions. Using a quantitative approach with descriptive-verificative design, the research involved 150 respondents through purposive sampling technique. Data were analyzed using IBM SPSS Statistics. Results demonstrate that green marketing and brand reputation have positive and significant effects on purchase decisions, both individually and simultaneously. The coefficient of determination of 72.4% indicates that both independent variables explain the variance in purchase decisions, while 27.6% is influenced by other factors. The findings confirm that combining environmentally friendly marketing strategies with credible brand reputation serves as an effective driver of consumer purchase decisions in an increasingly environmentally conscious market.

latest.title: ESG Disclosure and Firm Profitability: The Moderating Roles of Firm Size and Corporate Governance
latest.venue: International Review of Management and Marketing
latest.abstract: The disclosure of Environmental, Social, and Governance practices has gained prominence as companies encounter heightened expectations from investors, regulators, and various stakeholders for enhanced transparency regarding their ESG activities. This study investigates the correlation between ESG disclosure and corporate profitability, focusing specifically on the moderating influence of company size. The study employs a quantitative methodology and uses purposive sampling to obtain 310 firm-year data points. Information was acquired via publicly accessible annual reports, sustainability documents, and ESG data sources. Corporate profitability is assessed using return on assets (ROA), whereas ESG transparency serves as the primary explanatory variable. The size of the firm is analyzed as a moderating variable, while firm age, leverage, revenue, and market capitalization are considered as control factors. Pearson correlation and moderated regression analysis were used to investigate the proposed relationships. The results indicate a negative and statistically significant correlation between ESG disclosure and profitability. The regression findings indicate a negative correlation between ESG disclosure and ROA (β = −0.116; t = −3.331), failing to substantiate the claim that ESG disclosure enhances profitability. The negative correlation persists as significant even after incorporating firm size into the model (β = −0.117; t = −3.245). The relationship between ESG disclosure and firm size is both positive and statistically significant (β = 0.118; t = 2.768), suggesting that firm size influences the ESG–profitability relationship. latest.title: Digital Financial Services Adoption among Entrepreneurs: Evidence for FinTech Education, Innovation, and Local Enterprise Competitiveness
latest.venue: International Review of Management and Marketing
latest.abstract: This mixed-method study examined the digital financial services gateways of micro, small, and medium entrepreneurs in Tandag City, Surigao del Sur, Philippines. Using survey data from 300 entrepreneurs and qualitative interview data from 50 participants, the study described the entrepreneurs’ socio-demographic profile, status of digital financial services utilization, perceived implementation of digital financial services, reasons for use, challenges encountered, and suggestedE interventions. The quantitative findings show that respondents were mostly female (173 or 57.7%), married (161 or 53.7%), college graduates (196 or 65.3%), and sole proprietors (204 or 68.0%). Wholesale and retail trade obtained the highest proportion among business activities (100 or 33.3%), and smartphones were the most frequently used gadgets. GCash ranked first among digital financial services gateways (163), while money transfer ranked first among digital features used (143). Despite this adoption, direct cash remained dominant across several payment categories, and 161 respondents reported no digital financial services training. Perceived implementation of digital financial services was generally high, while reasons for use were generally agreed upon by respondents. Challenges were moderately agreed upon, with lack of digital financial literacy, internet availability, lack of faith, lack of money, phishing, pharming, SIM card swap, spyware, and hacking emerging as major concerns in the original dataset. The qualitative analysis generated three major themes: transactional convenience and accessibility, infrastructural and trust-related barriers, and institutional support for literacy, connectivity, security, and affordability. latest.title: Green Investment, Environmental, Social and Governance Disclosures, and Corporate Social Responsibility: The Case of Nigerian Companies
latest.venue: International Review of Management and Marketing
latest.abstract: Existing research provides little evidence that investments with an environmental focus promote better corporate social responsibility (CSR) practices or are simply symbolic actions in weak institutional environments. Hence, this study investigated the effect of green investment and ESG disclosures on the CSR performance of listed companies in Nigeria. The research was grounded in stakeholder and institutional theories to explain the relationship between environmentally driven investments and corporate social outcomes. Secondary data was collected from annual reports of selected listed companies for ten years and analysed using the Feasible Generalised Least Squares (FGLS) and Driscoll-Kraay Standard Error (DKSE) estimation techniques. The findings revealed that green investment has a positive and significant impact on CSR practices (Z = 4.849, p < 0.01). This implies that companies with higher green investment practices have more participation in environmental protection, community development, and responsible governance. The results also suggested that supporting factors such as green capital expenditure, ESG initiatives, green technological innovation, and carbon emission reduction efforts have an influence on the success of green investment. The study found that green investment improves CSR performance; however, its effect may be reduced to a legitimacy tool where institutional structures are weak. The research indicates that policymakers should tighten sustainability regulations and foster transparent ESG reporting. At the same time, companies should connect green investment to long-term environmental and social strategies to achieve meaningful CSR outcomes.

latest.title: Parasocial Interaction and Perceived Value as Determinants of Intention to Buy Made-in-Thailand Products through Live- Streaming Personal Shoppers
latest.venue: International Review of Management and Marketing
latest.abstract: This research investigates the rising trend of live shopping and jasa titipan (jastip) in Southeast Asian digital commerce, focusing on the growing popularity of Made in Thailand products among Indonesian consumers. Livestream commerce has changed consumer behaviour by offering immediacy, interactivity, and immersive digital experiences that lessen psychological distance between sellers and buyers. In Indonesia, live personal shopper sessions have become a key method for cross-border purchases of Thai cosmetics, fashion items, herbal supplements, and packaged foods, which are widely viewed as authentic and high-quality. Despite the market's rapid growth, previous research has mostly examined individual aspects like interactivity, trust, or entertainment, with limited attention to understanding the combined psychological factors influencing purchase intentions in livestream shopping. This study develops and tests a structural equation model (SEM) that includes social presence, parasocial interaction, perceived trust, perceived value, and perceived enjoyment to explain Indonesian consumers’ willingness to buy Thai products via live personal shoppers. The model captures both utilitarian and hedonic evaluation aspects, showing how relational bonding, immediacy, credibility cues, and experiential enjoyment collectively reduce uncertainty in cross-border transactions. This work contributes to theory by providing a comprehensive framework for understanding purchase intention formation in livestream commerce. Practically, the findings suggest strategic approaches for personal shoppers and digital platforms to enhance credibility and build consumer trust. latest.title: Beyond the 3PL Black Box: An Integrated Study of Mediating Mechanisms and the Moderating Effects of Perceived Risk and Usage Frequency in Thai Platform-Bound Delivery
latest.venue: International Review of Management and Marketing
latest.abstract: E-commerce platforms increasingly operate their own captive last-mile couriers—a model termed platform-bound delivery that differs fundamentally from outsourced third-party logistics in brand attribution, data control, and ownership of service recovery. However, how this captive model builds customer loyalty remains poorly understood, and the pathway from service quality through perceived value and satisfaction to loyalty has rarely been tested as an integrated sequence. This study develops and tests a serial-mediation model in which four antecedents—customer trust, last-mile delivery quality, platform reliability, and service recovery quality—shape perceived value and satisfaction, which in turn drive loyalty, with perceived risk and delivery experience frequency examined as boundary conditions. Using survey data from 447 platform-bound delivery users in Thailand and partial least squares structural equation modeling, the study finds that the proposed sequence holds and that satisfaction is the decisive driver of loyalty (β = 0.596, f² = 0.551, p < 0.001), with value and satisfaction acting as coordinated mediators. Trust is the strongest driver of perceived value (β = 0.327), and all four serial value–satisfaction–loyalty chains are significant; the model explains 36% of the variance in loyalty, 51% in satisfaction, and 56% in perceived value. Neither risk perception nor usage frequency showed a detectable moderating effect on satisfaction formation, providing no evidence that the loyalty mechanism differs across customer types. Theoretically, the study validates and refines the value–satisfaction–loyalty chain in the captive-delivery context. Practically, it advises operators to deliver a uniformly trustworthy, reliable, and recovery-capable experience rather than ta
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: Beyond Stimulation: A Motivation-Based Segmentation of Coffee Purchasing and Drinking Behaviour
latest.venue: International Review of Management and Marketing
latest.abstract: This study aims to segment Turkish coffee consumers residing in Northern Cyprus by their motivations for coffee consumption and to examine how these segments differ in coffee attributes, information sources, consumption and purchasing behaviours, and socio-demographic characteristics. Data were collected using a structured online questionnaire and purposive sampling between April and June 2025. A total of 649 valid responses were analysed. Exploratory factor analysis was employed to identify underlying motivational dimensions of coffee consumption, followed by hierarchical and K-means cluster analysis to classify consumers into homogeneous segments. Five distinct motivational consumer segments were identified. Chi-square tests and ANOVA results revealed significant differences among these segments in preferred coffee attributes, information sources, consumption occasions, purchasing behaviour, consumption frequency, and socio-demographic characteristics. The findings demonstrated that motivations for coffee consumption in Northern Cyprus are multidimensional and strongly associated with behavioural and demographic profiles. Although coffee consumption has been widely examined in global literature, limited research has addressed it from a motivational segmentation perspective within a Mediterranean cultural context. By providing a comprehensive characterisation of consumer segments, this study contributes to the literature on coffee consumption and purchasing behaviour from a consumer psychology perspective.

latest.title: Brand Love, Customer Brand Engagement, and Brand Pride as Predictors of Brand Defense among Indonesian iPhone 17 Series Users
latest.venue: International Review of Management and Marketing
latest.abstract: This study examines how brand love, customer brand engagement, brand pride, and regulatory focus are associated with brand defense among Indonesian iPhone 17 Series users. Cross-sectional data from 350 respondents recruited through purposive sampling were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) in SmartPLS 4. Brand love was positively associated with customer brand engagement, which was positively associated with brand defense. The direct association between brand love and brand defense was nonsignificant, whereas the indirect association through customer brand engagement was significant, supporting a pattern of indirect-only mediation. Brand pride also showed a positive direct association with brand defense. Promotion focus and prevention focus did not significantly moderate either the brand love-engagement association or the corresponding indirect association, indicating that regulatory focus did not function as a boundary condition in this context. Together, the proposed predictors explained 50.9% of the variance in brand defense. The findings extend the consumer-brand relationship perspective by identifying customer brand engagement as a relational pathway linking brand love with brand defense and brand pride as a complementary identity-related predictor. These findings provide insight into why consumers defend identity-relevant premium brands and highlight engagement and brand pride as important considerations for brand management.

latest.title: Pengaruh Audit Report Lag, Ukuran Perusahaan, dan Leverage terhadap Opini Audit Going Concern
latest.venue: Jurnal EMT KITA
latest.abstract: This study aims to analyze the effect of audit report lag, firm size, and leverage on going concern audit opinions among consumer cyclical companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) for the 2020–2024 period. This study employs a quantitative method with an associative approach and uses secondary data in the form of annual financial reports obtained from the official Indonesia Stock Exchange website. Data analysis was conducted using logistic regression with a panel data logit approach. The sample was determined using purposive sampling, resulting in 56 consumer cyclical companies with a total of 280 observations during the 2020–2024 period. Hypothesis testing was performed using EViews 12. The results show that the coefficients of audit report lag, firm size, and leverage are 0.005847, −0.205131, and 0.088214, respectively, with a McFadden R² of 0.121945. The results indicate that audit report lag (X1), firm size (X2), and leverage (X3) have significant effects on going concern audit opinions partially. Furthermore, audit report lag, firm size, and leverage simultaneously affect going concern audit opinions.

latest.title: Unlocking Innovative Work Behavior through Artificial Intelligence Capability: The Mediating Roles of Psychological Empowerment and Knowledge Sharing
latest.venue: International Review of Management and Marketing
latest.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) capability has become a critical organizational resource for enhancing innovation and sustaining competitiveness in increasingly digital business environments. Despite growing interest in AI adoption, limited empirical evidence explains how AI capability translates into employees' innovative work behavior (IWB), particularly in small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), where innovation depends heavily on human capital rather than formal research and development. Drawing on the Ability–Motivation–Opportunity (AMO) Theory, this study develops and tests a model in which Psychological Empowerment (PE) and Knowledge Sharing Behavior (KSB) mediate the relationship between Artificial Intelligence Capability (AIC) and Innovative Work Behavior. A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted among 350 Indonesian SME employees with experience using AI-enabled digital technologies. The proposed model was analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The results demonstrate that AI capability significantly enhances innovative work behavior both directly and indirectly by strengthening employees' psychological empowerment and encouraging knowledge-sharing behavior. The mediation analysis further confirms that empowered employees who actively exchange knowledge are more likely to transform AI-enabled resources into innovative workplace practices. These findings extend AMO Theory by conceptualizing AI capability as an organizational ability that creates employee innovation through complementary motivational and opportunity mechanisms. This study contributes to the emerging literature on AI-enabled organizational innovation by integrating technological, psychological, and behavioral perspectives into a unified framework w

latest.title: Augmented Reality Features, Customer Experience, and Engagement in Retail: An Experience Economy Perspective
latest.venue: Journal of Logistics Informatics and Service Science
latest.abstract: Augmented Reality (AR) is increasingly embedded within digital retail environments, yet its role extends beyond a marketing tool toward a technology-mediated service interface that reshapes customer interaction and engagement.Drawing on the Stimulus-Organism-Response (SOR) model and Experience Economy Theory, this study examines how AR features influence customer engagement through experiential mechanisms.The findings reveal that AR features significantly enhance customer experience dimensions, including escapism and aesthetic experience.Among these, escapism emerges as the strongest predictor of customer engagement, highlighting the importance of immersive experiences in AR-enabled retail contexts.Furthermore, customer experience is confirmed as a key mediating mechanism linking AR technological stimuli to engagement outcomes.The results offer both theoretical advancements and practical insights for designing AR-enabled customer experiences that foster sustained engagement.

latest.title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE-DRIVEN SOCIAL MEDIA MARKETING AND GREEN PURCHASE INTENTION: DEVELOPING A CONCEPTUAL FRAMEWORK FOR UZBEKISTAN
latest.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
latest.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has become an important tool in social media marketing, enabling businesses to deliver personalized content and enhance consumer engagement. At the same time, growing environmental awareness has increased interest in green products. This study develops a conceptual framework to explain the relationship between AI-driven social media marketing, consumer trust, and green purchase intention in Uzbekistan. Based on recent literature, the proposed framework suggests that AI-driven social media marketing strengthens consumer trust and positively influences consumers' intention to purchase green products. The study contributes to the green marketing literature by integrating these constructs into a unified conceptual model and provides a theoretical foundation for future empirical research in Uzbekistan. Одновременно с этим рост экологической осведомлённости способствует повышению интереса к экологически чистым продуктам. latest.title: Enterprise Informatics Capability and Manufacturing Supply Chain Resilience in the Digital Economy: The Roles of Information Transparency and Environmental Dynamism
latest.venue: Journal of Logistics Informatics and Service Science
latest.abstract: This study examines how enterprise informatics capability influences manufacturing supply chain resilience in the context of the digital economy.Drawing on organizational information processing theory and contingency theory, a moderated mediation model is developed to investigate the mediating role of information transparency and the moderating role of environmental dynamism.Survey data collected from 316 supply chain managers and senior executives in Chinese manufacturing firms are analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling.The findings indicate that enterprise informatics capability has a significant positive effect on manufacturing supply chain resilience both directly and indirectly through information transparency.Information transparency partially mediates this relationship by serving as a key information-transmission mechanism.Environmental dynamism does not significantly moderate the direct effect of enterprise informatics capability on supply chain resilience; however, it positively moderates the indirect effect through information transparency, such that the mediating pathway becomes stronger in highly dynamic environments.The findings contribute to the enterprise informatics literature by clarifying the information-processing pathways through which informatics capability translates into supply chain resilience, and by identifying the boundary conditions under which these pathways operate.Practical implications for manufacturing managers seeking to strengthen supply chain resilience through informatics investment are discussed.

latest.title: Strategi Pengembangan Bisnis Reboocha melalui Business Model Canvas dan Blue Ocean Strategy
latest.venue: Jurnal EMT KITA
latest.abstract: The fermented functional beverage industry, particularly kombucha, has grown rapidly alongside rising health awareness, yet start-up businesses such as ReBoocha remain in an exploratory business-model stage that is vulnerable to competition. This study aims to map ReBoocha's current Business Model Canvas (BMC) and to formulate a business development strategy through Blue Ocean Strategy (BOS) using the Four Actions Framework (Eliminate, Reduce, Raise, Create). A descriptive qualitative case study was conducted at ReBoocha in Sidoarjo. Data were collected through in-depth interviews, observation, and documentation involving eight purposively selected informants (one owner, two employees, and five customers), then analyzed thematically and validated through source and technique triangulation. The findings show that ReBoocha still operates within a red ocean due to its reliance on discount-based promotion and limited market education about kombucha. The ERRC analysis identified the need to eliminate generic one-way promotion, reduce unmeasured promotional spending, raise distribution access and consumer education, and create subscription schemes, community programs, and introductory pricing. The resulting new Business Model Canvas has the potential to shift ReBoocha toward a new market space oriented toward value, education, and consumer experience.

latest.title: Service Experience and Student Loyalty in Private Higher Education: The Roles of Service Quality, Perceived Value, Trust, and Customer Satisfaction
latest.venue: International Review of Management and Marketing
latest.abstract: Service organizations operate in increasingly competitive environments where maintaining customer loyalty requires more than delivering satisfactory services. Service quality, customer satisfaction, trust, and relationship quality are important factors that may influence customers’ long-term behavioral intentions, yet their interrelationships require further examination within an integrated framework. This study aims to examine the causal relationships among service quality, customer satisfaction, trust, relationship quality, and customer loyalty, and to determine the effects of service quality dimensions on customer satisfaction and the subsequent effects on customer loyalty. A quantitative research approach was employed using a structured questionnaire developed from established measures of service quality, customer satisfaction, trust, relationship quality, and customer loyalty. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and structural equation modeling to examine the proposed causal relationships and direct and indirect effects among the constructs. The findings indicate that service quality, particularly reliability, responsiveness, assurance, empathy, and tangibles, has positive effects on customer satisfaction. Customer satisfaction positively influences customer loyalty, while trust strengthens customer relationships and contributes to loyalty. The results further indicate that relationship quality provides an important link between customers’ perceptions of service performance and their behavioral outcomes. The findings provide practical guidance for service managers to improve service delivery by strengthening reliability, responsiveness, assurance, empathy, and tangible service elements.
