hot.title: Contemporary digital marketing techniques used in unhealthy food campaigns targeting young people
hot.abstract: The digital marketing of unhealthy foods and non-alcoholic beverages has a detrimental impact on children's eating behaviours, leading to adverse diet-related health outcomes. To inform the development of evidence-based strategies to protect children online, this study aimed to describe contemporary digital marketing techniques and industry reported impacts from unhealthy food and beverage marketing campaigns aimed at young people aged 3-17. We conducted a qualitative conceptual content analysis of 111 industry reports detailing the nature and impact of unhealthy food and beverage marketing campaigns from around the world that directly or indirectly targeted children through digital channels. We categorised and narratively describe how food and beverage companies are using digital marketing techniques, across four conceptual groups: (i) leveraging data and technology to optimise marketing, (ii) profiling and segmenting audiences, (iii) targeting and personalisation, and (iv) generating participation and engagement. Industry reported impacts on young people as a result of campaigns included i) increased exposure to, and engagement with, unhealthy food marketing, ii) purchases and consumption of unhealthy foods and beverages iii) formation of emotional brand connections and enhanced future marketing through data collection. Our findings support and extend existing literature revealing how multinational food and beverage companies are using advanced digital marketing techniques, including artificial intelligence and new technologies, to shape children's food behaviours and influence their diets worldwide. Policy actions are needed to protect children from the sophisticated digital marketing techniques used by the food and beverage industry.
hot.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

hot.title: Effects of financial consumer protection on brand love and brand advocacy
hot.abstract: Abstract Financial consumer protection has emerged as a critical global trend. This study examines how financial consumer protection affects brand advocacy in the context of retail banks in Hong Kong. Structural equation modelling was used to analyse a sample of 300 responses to an online survey. The results showed that fairness, transparency, and data privacy protection affected customer satisfaction, while governance had no significant effect on it. Customer satisfaction was positively associated with both brand love and brand advocacy. Brand love had a strong relationship with brand advocacy. Customer satisfaction also mediated the relationships between financial consumer protection, brand love, and brand advocacy. As an evolving concept in the global banking sector, financial consumer protection not only shapes consumer behaviour but also influences their trust and thus impacts branding advocacy efforts. This study fills the gap in the literature on the impact of financial consumer protection on branding by examining the influence of financial customer protection on brand love and brand advocacy. This research adds value to the branding literature by identifying new inter-construct relationships. It also contributes to the advancement of knowledge by exploring a novel construct (financial consumer protection). Understanding the role of financial consumer protection in brand love and brand advocacy can help bank practitioners to design branding strategies that support long-term profitability.
hot.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

hot.title: The influence of brand experience on brand loyalty in the electronic commerce sector: the mediating effect of brand association and brand trust
hot.abstract: Businesses are increasingly focusing on brand experience due to its dual role in directly creating customer value and shaping customers’ perceptions of brand equity. This study investigates the impact of brand experience on brand equity in Vietnam’s e-commerce sector. Primary data were collected from respondents with prior online shopping experience on e-commerce platforms. The research identifies four critical dimensions of brand experience in e-commerce services: sensory, affective, intellectual, and behavioral experiences. These components positively influence brand equity, particularly in terms of brand association, brand trust, and brand loyalty. Moreover, the study confirms the mediating roles of brand association and brand trust in the relationships between affective experience and brand loyalty, intellectual experience and brand loyalty, and behavioral experience and brand loyalty. This research offers a valuable contribution to the literature on brand experience and brand equity, especially within the e-commerce context. Managerial implications are also provided to guide businesses in enhancing customer brand experiences and strengthening brand equity.

latest.title: Social Media Marketing, Personal Selling, and Price Perception on Purchase Decision through Purchase Intention with Experience Environment as a Moderator
latest.venue: International Review of Management and Marketing
latest.abstract: This study examines the influence of social media marketing, personal selling, and price perception on purchase decision, mediated by purchase intention and moderated by experience environment, within the Indonesian residential property sector. Drawing on the Theory of Planned Behavior, Servicescape theory, and the Stimulus-Organism-Response framework, an integrative model is tested using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) and Necessary Condition Analysis (NCA) on data collected from 304 confirmed buyers at CitraLand Tallasa City Makassar. Results confirm that price perception constitutes the dominant predictor of purchase intention, followed by social media marketing, while personal selling yields a non-significant sufficiency-based effect. Purchase intention and experience environment both exert significant direct effects on purchase decision. Purchase intention fully mediates the effects of price perception and social media marketing on purchase decision, whereas the hypothesised moderating role of experience environment is not supported. NCA establishes that all five constructs represent necessary conditions of medium magnitude, with experience environment imposing the most binding prerequisite constraint. The integrated NCA–PLS-SEM approach reveals that achieving superior purchase decision outcomes demands simultaneously adequate performance across all conditions. These findings advance theoretical understanding of high-involvement consumer decision-making and provide actionable guidance for property developers in emerging residential markets.

latest.title: When Price Cuts Fail to Pay Off: Behavioral Mechanisms Mediating the Price Reduction-Purchase Behaviour Relationship in Multi-tier Fast-moving Consumer Goods Distribution
latest.venue: International Review of Management and Marketing
latest.abstract: Price cuts are widely used in FMCG distribution to stimulate purchasing, yet lower trade prices do not always translate into stronger buying decisions when retailers face inventory risk, cash-flow limits, and local market pressure. This study explains how price reduction influences purchase behaviour among retail outlet owners and wholesalers by examining the mediating roles of competitive perception, price policy, and stocking intention. A quantitative survey was conducted with 278 retail outlets and wholesalers in Manado, Palu, Kendari, and Makassar after data screening from the initial target sample. The proposed relationships were tested using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) to assess the direct and mediating effects. The results show that price reduction significantly strengthens competitive perception, price policy evaluation, stocking intention, and purchase behaviour. Competitive perception and stocking intention significantly mediate the relationship between price reduction and purchase behaviour, while price policy shows a positive but insignificant mediating role. These findings suggest that FMCG suppliers should connect price reductions with margin logic, sell-out support, stock rotation planning, and local market positioning. This study extends behavioural pricing literature by showing that price cuts work through retailers’ interpretation of competitive usefulness and inventory feasibility.

latest.title: Relationship between Income Level and Price Sensitivity Among Consumers
latest.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
latest.abstract: Abstract Price is one of the many factors that have an effect on the buying decisions of consumers. However, the impact of price on the decision-making process is quite dissimilar at various income levels. The current study seeks to understand the effects of consumer income levels on price sensitivity, in other words, how the financial standing of the consumer affects their perception of price and their willingness to pay for brands and buy generally. Specifically, the research aims to examine the degree of price responsiveness among people of different income levels. The primary data for the study will be collected through the means of a structured survey of consumers of various income levels. The use of descriptive statistics and correlation analysis, among other statistical measures, will be required in the examination of the effects of income on price sensitivity. Finally, the overall goal of this research is to shed light on the effects of income on price sensitivity. Such information is extremely helpful for business organizations in creating appropriate price strategies. This study looks at how a person's income shapes how sensitive they are to price changes. Price sensitivity is simply how much a customer's buying choices shift when a price goes up or down. When you look at how people shop, income is usually the biggest piece of the puzzle. It determines what someone can actually afford, which naturally shapes how much they’re willing—and able—to hand over at the register. How you react to a price change often comes down to your bank account. When money is tight, every single dollar counts. You automatically become more cautious—you check price tags twice, hunt for coupons, and hold off on buying until things go on sale. When you have a comfortable financial cus

latest.title: Internationalizing Marketing Management Education through Academic Exchange, Industry Engagement, and Community Empowerment: An International Community Service Program in Malaysia and Singapore
latest.venue: SERVITIUM RESEARCH Community Service Journal
latest.abstract: International community service can connect marketing education with professional practice and cooperation. This program comprised an interinstitutional assignment to Malaysia and Singapore and academic–industry engagement at Karangkraf Malaysia. Implementation involved preparation, knowledge exchange, an industrial visit, reflective evaluation, and follow-up planning. Academics discussed digital marketing, while practitioners shared publishing management and business experience. Participants encountered editorial, design, printing, and distribution processes. Immediate outputs included industry insights, initial institutional communication, publication materials, and curriculum recommendations. Community empowerment took the form of reciprocal professional knowledge sharing. The program linked international engagement with industry-informed education.

latest.title: Kepuasan Konsumen pada Rumah Makan di Wilayah Non-Metropolitan: Peran Kualitas Produk, Persepsi Harga, dan Promosi di Purworejo
latest.venue: Jurnal Manajemen Riset Inovasi
latest.abstract: This study aims to examine the effects of product quality, price perception, and promotion on consumer satisfaction at Rumah Makan Satu Satu Purworejo. Data were collected through a survey using closed-ended questionnaires based on a Likert scale, distributed to consumers aged at least 20 years who had visited the restaurant at least twice, resided in Purworejo Regency, and were willing to complete the questionnaire honestly and thoroughly. A total of 100 respondents were selected using purposive sampling, a sampling technique involving the deliberate selection of participants based on characteristics relevant to the study objectives. The data were analyzed using multiple linear regression with IBM SPSS Statistics 25. Prior to the analysis, validity, reliability, and classical assumption tests were conducted. The residuals were found to be non-normally distributed, while the Glejser test indicated potential heteroscedasticity in the promotion variable. Therefore, partial coefficient testing was supplemented with 5,000 bootstrap resamples using simple sampling and 95% bias-corrected and accelerated (BCa) confidence intervals. The F-test results indicated that the model was simultaneously significant (F = 79.022, Sig. = 0.000), with an R Square value of 0.712. Based on the bootstrap results, product quality had a positive but statistically insignificant coefficient (B = 0.143, p = 0.244). Price perception had a positive and significant effect on consumer satisfaction (B = 0.703, p less than 0.001), while promotion had a positive but statistically insignificant coefficient (B = 0.130, p = 0.376). Thus, H1 and H3 were not supported, whereas H2 was supported.

latest.title: The PPP Framework for Safe Launch Pricing: Premium, Promotion, Penetration
latest.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
latest.abstract: A new product faces a pricing dilemma: a high price may deter trial of an unproven brand, while a low price may generate trial but teach customers that this is the product's normal price, making later increases difficult. This paper proposes the PPP framework for safe launch pricing, which separates two functions of price: the positioning price, which signals the tier to which the product belongs, and the transaction price actually paid at launch. The Premium reference price is derived from the "product leader" in quality and image; the Penetration price is derived from the best-selling "market leader"; and a genuine, temporary promotion bridges the two, protecting the reference price from being replaced in customers' minds by the launch price. Price is then recovered gradually by reducing the discount in response to evidence of market acceptance rather than the passage of time. The paper presents the framework's six stages, a numerical example, a comparison with conventional penetration pricing, the literature that explains its mechanisms, and the conditions for its use and failure, including legal constraints on price reductions.

latest.title: Pengaruh Kualitas Pelayanan, Kualitas Produk dan Variasi Menu Terhadap Kepuasan Pelanggan di Ask Coffee Marelan
latest.venue: PENG Jurnal Ekonomi dan Manajemen
latest.abstract: Penjualan Ask Coffee Marelan menurun dari Rp657,0 juta pada 2022 menjadi Rp504,7 juta pada 2025 di tengah persaingan coffee shop yang semakin ketat. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis pengaruh kualitas pelayanan, kualitas produk, dan variasi menu terhadap kepuasan pelanggan Ask Coffee Marelan. Penelitian kuantitatif asosiatif ini mengumpulkan data melalui kuesioner dari 100 pelanggan, dengan ukuran sampel ditentukan menggunakan rumus Lemeshow, kemudian menganalisisnya dengan regresi linear berganda menggunakan SPSS versi 27. Kualitas pelayanan (B = 0,002; t = 0,039; p = 0,969) dan kualitas produk (B = −0,017; t = −0,255; p = 0,799) tidak berpengaruh signifikan secara parsial terhadap kepuasan pelanggan, sedangkan variasi menu berpengaruh positif dan signifikan (B = 0,527; β = 0,830; t = 6,013; p < 0,001). Secara simultan, ketiga variabel berpengaruh signifikan (F = 55,274; p < 0,001) dan menjelaskan 63,3% variasi kepuasan pelanggan. Tumpang tindih yang tinggi antara kualitas produk dan prediktor lain (VIF = 7,546) mengindikasikan bahwa kontribusi uniknya terserap oleh variasi menu. Ask Coffee Marelan perlu memprioritaskan pengembangan menu dengan tetap menjaga standar produk dan pelayanan.

latest.title: The Effect of Employee Service Quality on Customer Satisfaction Mediated by Price At the A2 Aluminum and Glass Shop MSME in Palembang City
latest.venue: International Journal of Managemen Analytics (IJMA)
latest.abstract: This study examines the effect of employee service quality on customer satisfaction, mediated by price, at UMKM Toko Aluminium dan Kaca A2 in Palembang. As consumer expectations shift toward customization, consultative selling becomes crucial. A quantitative method with a purposive sampling of 100 respondents was employed. Data were analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling-Partial Least Square (SEM-PLS) via SmartPLS 4.0. The results indicate that service quality significantly affects price perceptions and customer satisfaction. Furthermore, price significantly influences customer satisfaction and partially mediates the relationship between service quality and customer satisfaction. Effectively implementing consultative selling justifies pricing and enhances overall satisfaction.
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: LOW-PURCHASE LONG-STAY BEHAVIOUR AT ZUS COFFEE: CROWDING, FAIRNESS AND REVISIT INTENTION
latest.venue: Quantum Journal of Social Sciences and Humanities
latest.abstract: This study examines how low-purchase long-stay behaviour influences customer experience in urban coffee chains, using ZUS Coffee customers in Malaysia as the research context. As cafés increasingly function as informal work, study and social spaces, customers who purchase minimally but occupy seats for extended periods may affect other customers’ perceptions of crowding, service fairness, satisfaction and revisit intention. Drawing on servicescape, perceived crowding and service fairness perspectives, this study develops a conceptual model linking low-purchase long-stay behaviour to perceived crowding, perceived service fairness, customer satisfaction and revisit intention. A quantitative survey design is proposed among ZUS Coffee customers who have recently visited physical outlets in Malaysia. The study contributes to consumer behaviour and service management literature by examining café space consumption as part of the customer experience. The findings are expected to provide practical implications for coffee chain operators in managing seating, customer comfort and fairness without weakening the café’s role as a flexible third place.
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: Pengaruh Persepsi Harga Paket Data terhadap Kepuasan Pengguna Dalam Komunikasi Penawaran Telkomsel Prabayar pada Mahasiswa Pendidikan Fisika Universitas Sriwijaya
latest.venue: Journal of Communication and Social Sciences
latest.abstract: ABSTRACT Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis pengaruh harga paket internet Telkomsel Prabayar terhadap kepuasan pelanggan pada mahasiswa Pendidikan Fisika Universitas Sriwijaya angkatan 2022–2024. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan metode survei. Populasi berjumlah 266 mahasiswa dan sampel terdiri atas 111 responden pengguna Telkomsel Prabayar. Data dikumpulkan melalui kuesioner dan dianalisis menggunakan uji validitas, reliabilitas, uji asumsi, serta regresi linear sederhana. Hasil pengujian menunjukkan bahwa instrumen penelitian valid dan reliabel. Persamaan regresi yang diperoleh adalah Y = 1,826 + 0,717X, dengan pengaruh harga paket internet yang signifikan terhadap kepuasan pelanggan (p = 0,002). Hasil ini menunjukkan bahwa penilaian mahasiswa terhadap harga paket internet berkaitan dengan kepuasan mereka terhadap layanan Telkomsel Prabayar. Abstract This study examines the effect of Telkomsel prepaid internet package prices on customer satisfaction among Physics Education students at Universitas Sriwijaya from the 2022–2024 cohorts. A quantitative survey was conducted among 111 Telkomsel prepaid users from a population of 266 students. Data were collected using questionnaires and analyzed through validity and reliability tests, assumption tests, and simple linear regression. The instruments met the reported validity and reliability criteria. The regression equation was Y = 1.826 + 0.717X, and the reported significance value was p = 0.002, indicating a statistically significant relationship between internet package prices and customer satisfaction. The findings indicate that students’ evaluations of internet package prices are associated with their satisfaction with Telkomsel prepaid services.

latest.title: Statistical Analysis Of Consumer Purchase Intention For Managerial Decision-Making In Commodity Markets: Evidence From The Indian Steel Industry
latest.venue: Computer and decision making.
latest.abstract: In Indian retail steel market, managerial decisions to position the brand, quality communication, price and access to the market require evidence on the factors associated with consumer purchase intention. This study delves into the same relationship with the help of structured questionnaire response from consumers of the Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities of Karnataka and Maharashtra. This difference between the number of observations (152 in SPSS tables; 150 in sampling description) needs to be checked against the original data set. Pearson correlations, multiple linear regressions and a brand-logo comparison were employed in the analysis of purchasing intentions. The model with five predictors explained 58.7% of the variance (with R² = 0.587). None of the adjusted non-significant variables were brand awareness, perceived quality and price perception. In the reported Logo comparison, the purchase intention was found to be lower in the Logo group (ArcelorMittal) when compared with the No Logo (control) group. Sustainability and digital communication are still important, proposed considerations but were not demonstrated to have independent impact by the regression outputs displayed. How the study has interpreted these findings are used as evidence for assessing priorities within marketing rather than causal sales or resource optimisation gains.

latest.title: DRIVING LOYALTY THROUGH SERVICE-QUALITY: DO AGE AND INCOME MATTER? EVIDENCE FROM MALAYSIA’S AUTOMOTIVE INDUSTRY
latest.venue: Quantum Journal of Social Sciences and Humanities
latest.abstract: Customer loyalty is essential for sustaining competitive advantage in the automotive service industry, where repeated post-sales interactions strongly influence long-term customer relationships. This study examines the relationship between service quality and customer loyalty in Malaysia's automotive service industry and investigates whether age and income moderate this relationship. A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted using data collected from 385 customers of authorised automotive service centres in Malaysia. The data were analysed using multiple regression analysis. The findings reveal that service quality has a significant positive effect on customer loyalty, confirming that customers who perceive higher levels of service quality are more likely to remain loyal to their service providers. Although age exhibited a significant direct relationship with customer loyalty, neither age nor income significantly moderated the relationship between service quality and customer loyalty. These findings suggest that the influence of service quality on customer loyalty remains consistent across different demographic groups. This study contributes to the service marketing literature by providing evidence from an emerging market and offering practical implications for automotive service providers, highlighting the importance of consistently delivering high-quality services to strengthen customer loyalty rather than relying on demographic-based service differentiation.
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: PENGARUH CURRENT RATIO, PRICE TO BOOK VALUE DAN RETURN ON ASSET TERHADAP RETURN SAHAM
latest.venue: Dinamika
latest.abstract: This study aims to analyze the effect of Current Ratio (CR), Price to Book Value (PBV), and Return on Assets (ROA) on stock returns in telecommunication sub-sector companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX). The background of this study is based on fluctuations in companies' financial performance, which are assumed to influence the level of returns obtained by investors. The research method used is quantitative with an associative approach. The population consists of 22 telecommunication sub-sector companies, with a sample of 3 companies selected using purposive sampling technique. The research data includes 18 observations during the period 2019–2024. Data analysis was conducted using multiple linear regression with the help of SPSS version 26, including classical assumption tests, regression analysis, coefficient of determination test, t-test, and F-test. The results show that partially, CR and ROA have no significant effect on stock returns, with significance values of 0.506 and 0.316, respectively. Meanwhile, PBV has a significant effect on stock returns with a significance value of 0.044. Simultaneously, CR, PBV, and ROA do not have a significant effect on stock returns (Sig. 0.144). The coefficient of determination (R²) is 0.312, indicating that 31.2% of stock return variation can be explained by the model, while 68.8% is influenced by other factors outside the research model.

latest.title: Behavioural Biases and Pension Investment Decisions: Evidence from Employees in Kerala
latest.venue: ANUSANDHAN – NDIM s Journal of Business and Management Research
latest.abstract: Pension investment decisions are often influenced by psychological tendencies rather than purely rational financial reasoning. This study examines the role of five key behavioural biases overconfidence, loss aversion, present bias, anchoring, and herding in shaping pension investment behaviour among employees in Kerala. Using a structured questionnaire and responses from 100 participants, the study employs descriptive statistics and correlation analysis used to analyse the relationship between these biases and pension investment behaviour, including contribution levels, plan participation, and fund selection. The findings reveal that all five behavioural biases overconfidence, loss aversion, present bias, anchoring, and herding are significantly present among employees in Kerala with respect to pension investment decisions. However, among individual predictors, present bias showed a significant negative impact on pension investment behaviour, while overconfidence, loss aversion, anchoring, and herding biases were not significant. The results further reveal a significant variation in the strength of behavioural biases, with overconfidence and herding emerging as the most dominant factors influencing pension investment decisions among employees in Kerala.

latest.title: From Free to Paid: Public Attitude Change and Mechanism Evidence around Doubao's Charging Announcement
latest.venue: Media studies.
latest.abstract: As generative AI moves from free access to paid subscription, how charging shapes public attitude bears on platform commercialization. Taking Doubao's monthly subscription as the setting, this paper builds a dual-path framework of “product experience - price perception”. Using the announcement date (May 4, 2026) as the breakpoint, we collect public Weibo discussions from 30 days before to 30 days after it (2-day periods; the 14 days on each side form the main window), measure attitude with aspect-based sentiment analysis, and test changes at the breakpoint by regression discontinuity in time. Negative evaluation is robust in direction for Payment Willingness (τ = +0.751, p < 0.001) and Corporate Brand (τ = +0.647, p = 0.011), but rests on only 27 and 7 pre-breakpoint texts, so the magnitudes are read as direction only. The negative share for Price & Charging shows no significant increase (τ = -0.161, p = 0.123), so the price-fairness path is not supported. The difference between the two aspect jumps is -0.532 (clustered SE 0.437, p = 0.245), opposite to expectation and underpowered given the small pre-breakpoint sample; we report only that no larger negative change was found for the price path than for the feature path. The overall negative share rises by 0.317 (p = 0.041) but depends on a pre-breakpoint period with 3 relevant texts and falls to 0.043 (p = 0.517) without it, so it is not robustly supported. The conclusions are limited to a marked change in attitude, with no persistent shift and no strict causal claim.

latest.title: Beyond bias: How behavioral biases shape investment decision-making and perceived financial well-being
latest.venue: Investment Management and Financial Innovations
latest.abstract: Type of the article: Research ArticleAbstractThis study examines the associations among behavioral biases, Investment Decision-Making, and Perceived Financial Well-Being among individual investors in Indonesia. It distinguishes respondents’ involvement in the investment decision-making process from decision quality and investment performance.A quantitative cross-sectional design was employed using survey data from 505 Indonesian investors. The relationships among Anchoring Bias, Confirmation Bias, Loss Aversion, Overconfidence, Investment Decision-Making, and Perceived Financial Well-Being were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling. Permutation-based multi-group analysis was conducted to compare female and male respondents.Anchoring Bias, Confirmation Bias, Loss Aversion, and Overconfidence were positively associated with Investment Decision-Making, with path coefficients ranging from 0.144 to 0.215 (p < 0.05). Investment Decision-Making was positively associated with Perceived Financial Well-Being (β = 0.527, p < 0.001). The significant specific indirect effects further indicated that Investment Decision-Making statistically mediated the associations between each behavioral bias and Perceived Financial Well-Being. The multi-group analysis showed that only the relationship between Investment Decision-Making and Perceived Financial Well-Being differed significantly by gender and was stronger among female respondents.The findings contribute to behavioral finance research by showing that behavioral biases are associated with greater self-reported involvement in evaluating, selecting, and monitoring investments. These positive associations do not indicate that behavioral biases improve decision quality, investment performance, or objective financ

latest.title: Determining Household Savings Preferences: The Case of Türkiye
latest.venue: Namık Kemal Üniversitesi Sosyal Bilimler Meslek Yüksek Okulu Dergisi
latest.abstract: This study examines the socio-demographic factors that influence household saving preferences in Türkiye. A multinomial logit model was used to analyse data from 3354 households with complete information in the Turkish Statistical Institute’s 2020 Household Budget Survey micro-dataset. Savings preferences were categorized into four groups: real estate, gold/foreign currency, bank accounts, and capital market instruments. The findings suggest that families with children are more likely to prefer real estate and capital market instruments, while families without children are less likely to choose gold or foreign currency and bank accounts. Spending amount did not significantly affect preferences for real estate or gold/foreign currency but increased the likelihood of choosing a bank account and decreased the likelihood of choosing capital market instruments. Tenants were more likely to prefer gold, foreign currency, bank accounts, and capital market instruments, while homeowners tended to prefer real estate. Those with private insurance preferred capital market instruments, while those without preferred real estate, gold, foreign currency, and bank accounts. As household size increased, the likelihood of choosing real estate or gold/foreign currency increased, while the likelihood of having a bank account decreased. These results are informative for policymakers.

latest.title: CÁC YẾU TỐ ẢNH HƯỞNG ĐẾN HÀNH VI QUẢN LÝ TÀI CHÍNH CÁ NHÂN CỦA SINH VIÊN TRONG BỐI CẢNH CHUYỂN ĐỔI SỐ
latest.venue: Journal of Thu Dau Mot University
latest.abstract: Bài viết đo lường mức độ tác động của bảy yếu tố đến hành vi quản lý tài chính cá nhân của sinh viên Trường Đại học Thủ Dầu Một. Khung phân tích kết hợp Lý thuyết Hành vi có kế hoạch, mô hình Kiến thức – Thái độ – Hành vi, khung Năng lực tài chính và Tài chính hành vi. Khảo sát trực tuyến sử dụng thang Likert 5 mức thu về 494 phiếu, trong đó 409 phiếu hợp lệ và được xử lý bằng SPSS 26.0. Tám thang đo có hệ số Cronbach's Alpha từ 0,761 đến 0,869; Kết quả EFA cho KMO = 0,903 và phương sai trích 61,270% với 32 biến quan sát; hồi quy đạt R² = 0,656 (F = 109,003; Sig. = 0,000). Bảy hệ số hồi quy đều dương và có ý nghĩa thống kê, giảm dần từ kiến thức tài chính (β = 0,273), tự tin tài chính (0,179), phong cách chi tiêu (0,164), ảnh hưởng gia đình (0,152), thái độ tài chính (0,146), hiểu biết tài chính (0,127) tới công nghệ tài chính (0,102). Sáu giả thuyết được chấp nhận; riêng hiểu biết tài chính chỉ được chấp nhận có điều kiện vì không tương quan đơn biến với biến phụ thuộc (r = 0,027; Sig. = 0,587). Trên cơ sở đó, nghiên cứu đề xuất một số khuyến nghị.

latest.title: ‘Emotional Intelligence Is Not Just an Asset; It Is a Necessity’: Shaping Financial Behaviours and Overcoming Biases in Women Entrepreneurs
latest.venue: IIM Kozhikode Society & Management Review
latest.abstract: The role of emotional intelligence (EI) in shaping the behavioural biases of women in financial decision-making remains underexplored in the literature. The current study addressed this gap by investigating how women entrepreneurs’ financial literacy influences their financial decisions, with EI serving as a mediator. A cross-sectional descriptive survey design was employed for data collection from 210 Pakistani women entrepreneurs. A proportional stratified sampling technique was used to collect data, and analysis was conducted using structural equation modelling (SEM) via AMOS 26. Findings reveal that financial literacy has significant positive impacts on EI and self-control and helps reduce loss aversion bias, but no significant relationship was found between financial literacy and regret aversion or mental accounting. Moreover, EI acts as a strong mediator between financial literacy and biases such as mental accounting, regret aversion and loss aversion, but not between financial literacy and self-control. This study’s findings underscore the critical role of EI in reducing biases and complementing financial literacy to empower women entrepreneurs to make rational financial decisions. Moreover, it also emphasizes the need to integrate EI into financial literacy programmes to foster more effective decision-making and advance entrepreneurship among women.

latest.title: Executive Personal Jet Use and Agency Costs: The Practice of Time‐Share Reimbursement
latest.venue: Accounting Perspectives
latest.abstract: ABSTRACT Time‐share agreements (time‐shares) are an unexplored form of executives' personal use of corporate aircraft. Relative to jet perquisites (jet perks), time‐shares require reimbursement yet have limited disclosure, which practitioners promote to reduce scrutiny. This trade‐off engenders ambiguity and agency concerns about the associated effort managers devote to maximize shareholder wealth. Among S&P 500 firms from 2004 to 2017, we find that time‐share use, alone or combined with jet perks, has grown. Further, from 2007 to 2017, our primary empirical analysis shows that lower future firm profitability and value coincide with time‐shares, but only when combined with jet perks; these outcomes are higher for firms that offer only time‐shares. Changes analysis also supports that higher (lower) shareholder wealth coincides with a switch to time‐shares (jet perks). To further disentangle time‐shares from jet perks, we examine variation in time‐share disclosure attributes; consistent with initial inferences, more robust time‐share disclosure coincides with higher shareholder wealth. Finally, we explore the possibility that shareholders bear some costs that offset reimbursement and find only modest increases in cash compensation following time‐share initiation. Collectively, our findings imply that agency issues are lower for company stakeholders when firms do not award jet perquisites and instead use time‐share agreements.

latest.title: Effect of Strategic Resource Management, Financial Literacy, and Institutional Support on Small Business Sustainability in Katsina State, Nigeria
latest.venue: Jurnal Aplikasi Manajemen Ekonomi dan Bisnis
latest.abstract: Small business sustainability remains a critical challenge in resource-constrained environments, particularly in northern Nigeria where institutional support has intensified but participation gaps persist. This study examines the effect of strategic resource management, financial literacy, and institutional support on small business sustainability in Katsina State, Nigeria. Drawing on the Resource-Based View, Human Capital Theory, and Institutional Theory, the study adopts a quantitative cross-sectional survey design targeting 384 registered small businesses across the three senatorial districts of Katsina State. Data were collected through structured questionnaires and analysed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The findings reveal that strategic resource management, financial literacy, and institutional support each exert significant positive effects on business sustainability. Financial literacy partially mediates the relationship between strategic resource management and sustainability, while institutional support moderates the financial literacy–sustainability relationship. The study contributes to management literature by integrating internal capability and external institutional perspectives in explaining SME sustainability in a developing economy context. Practical recommendations are offered for KASEDA and Katsina State policymakers to optimise training design, financing access, and programme outreach.

latest.title: Purchase Intention Formation for K-Beauty Cosmetics: The Mediating Role of Sensory Expectation and the Moderated Mediation of Cosmetic Involvement
latest.venue: Journal of the Korean Society of Cosmetology
latest.abstract: The purpose of this study was to investigate the effects of consumers’ perception of K-beauty cosmetics in the digital consumption environment on purchase intention and to examine the mediating effect of sensory expectation and the moderated mediation effect of cosmetic involvement. An online survey was conducted from April 1 to April 28, 2026, with 305 Korean women aged 20–49 years. The collected data were analyzed using SPSS 30.0 and Hayes’ PROCESS Macro. Exploratory factor analysis, reliability analysis, multiple regression analysis, mediation analysis (Model 4), moderation analysis (Model 1), and moderated mediation analysis (Model 7) were performed. The results indicated that quality perception, price perception, and brand image all had significant positive effects on purchase intention, with quality perception showing the strongest effect. Sensory expectation partially mediated the relationships between quality perception, price perception, and brand image and purchase intention, while cosmetic involvement significantly moderated the relationships between each of these perception dimensions and purchase intention. Furthermore, moderated mediation analysis revealed that only the indirect effect of price perception on purchase intention through sensory expectation significantly varied according to the level of cosmetic involvement, with the indirect effect decreasing as cosmetic involvement increased. No significant moderated mediation effects were found for quality perception or brand image. These findings demonstrate that sensory expectation and cosmetic involvement play important roles in consumers’ purchase decision-making process in the digital consumption environment. By examining the mediating and moderated mediation effects, this study provides a more compre

latest.title: Hubungan Pemanfaatan Riwayat Transaksi QRIS dan Disiplin Pencatatan Keuangan dengan Pengelolaan Modal Kerja UMKM Kuliner Soppeng
latest.venue: Jurnal Ilmiah Metansi (Manajemen dan Akuntansi)
latest.abstract: Digitalisasi pembayaran menyediakan riwayat transaksi yang dapat dimanfaatkan sebagai informasi keuangan, tetapi penggunaan QRIS belum tentu disertai pencatatan usaha yang disiplin. Penelitian ini menganalisis hubungan pemanfaatan riwayat transaksi QRIS dan disiplin pencatatan keuangan dengan praktik pengelolaan modal kerja UMKM kuliner di Kabupaten Soppeng. Data berasal dari kuesioner lapangan atas 120 responden yang disediakan peneliti. Variabel diukur menggunakan empat butir QRIS, lima butir pencatatan keuangan, dan lima butir pengelolaan modal kerja pada skala 1–5. Skor komposit dihitung dari jawaban tersedia; 18 responden memiliki satu jawaban item kosong. Analisis menggunakan regresi linear berganda dengan galat baku robust HC3 dan uji sensitivitas kasus lengkap. Reliabilitas Cronbach’s alpha untuk ketiga konstruk berkisar 0,817–0,854. Pemanfaatan riwayat transaksi QRIS (B = 0,2882; p = 0,0005) serta disiplin pencatatan keuangan (B = 0,4414; p < 0,001) berhubungan positif dengan pengelolaan modal kerja. Model menjelaskan 31,40% variasi skor pengelolaan modal kerja (R² = 0,3140). Hasil pada 102 responden lengkap menunjukkan arah hubungan yang sama. Temuan menekankan pentingnya pemanfaatan informasi transaksi sekaligus rutinitas pembukuan bagi pengelolaan dana operasional UMKM; desain potong lintang tidak membuktikan hubungan sebab-akibat

latest.title: The Effect of Niche Perfume Selection Attributes on the Consume Happiness: The Moderating Effect of Generation through Multi-Group Analysis
latest.venue: Journal of the Korean Society of Cosmetology
latest.abstract: Niche perfume has emerged as a mainstream segment of the perfume market, moving beyond mass-market offerings by reflecting Millennials and Generation Z’s strong preference for individuality and distinctive scent identities. This study aims to analyze the effects of niche perfume selection attributes on consumer happiness. In addition, Millennials and Generation Z are proposed as a moderator affecting the niche perfume selection attributes on consumer happiness. An online survey targeted Korean women from Millennials and Generation Z who have experience using niche perfume. A total of 296 survey responses were analyzed using structural equation modeling with AMOS 26.0 and SPSS 25.0. The results revealed that four key selection attributes emerged from the analysis: trend orientation, brand awareness, premium price perception, and scent. In addition, scent, brand awareness, and premium price perception had significant effects on consumer happiness. Furthermore, the moderating effect of generation was confirmed through multi-group analysis. Specifically, Among Millennials, trend orientation, brand awareness, and premium price perception influenced consumer happiness, whereas scent was the most influential factor among Generation Z. By identifying these causal relationships, this study contributes to expanding the advancement of research on niche perfume and provides implications for developing differentiated strategies tailored to generational characteristics of the Millennials and Generation Z.

latest.title: Market Dominance and Competitive Effects of Online Travel Platforms: A Case Study of Ctrip/Trip.com Group in China
latest.venue: Journal of Applied Economics and Social Dynamics
latest.abstract: The rapid expansion of China’s digital economy has made online travel agencies (OTAs) an important intermediary between consumers and suppliers of accommodation, transport and tourism services. At the same time, platform concentration, network effects and contractual restrictions can create substantial market power. This study examines Ctrip and its parent, Trip.com Group, as a case through which to evaluate the formation and competitive effects of platform dominance. The analysis combines publicly available industry and corporate data with a June 2026 consumer questionnaire. It also incorporates a factual update based on the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) decision of July 2026. The revised analysis finds strong evidence that Trip.com Group has substantial market power, particularly in online hotel-booking platform services, but it avoids treating broad OTA gross merchandise value (GMV) shares as a legally sufficient measure of dominance. The platform’s scale can generate efficiencies through matching, standardisation, service quality and investment in digital infrastructure; however, dominance may also facilitate exclusionary contracting and restrictions on hotel pricing. The consumer survey suggests high brand salience and potential switching behaviour, but its non-probability sample and several instrument inconsistencies prevent causal or population-level inference. Overall, the evidence supports a balanced view: platform scale can improve coordination and consumer convenience, while competition policy remains necessary where contractual or algorithmic mechanisms restrict merchant autonomy or foreclose rivals.

latest.title: Inovasi Produk terhadap Keputusan Pembelian Konsumen: Studi Deskriptif Kualitatif pada Departemen Yakult Lady PT Yakult Indonesia Persada Cabang Bandung 2
latest.venue: Jurnal Ekonomi Logistik.
latest.abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis peran inovasi produk terhadap keputusan pembelian konsumen pada Departemen Yakult Lady PT Yakult Indonesia Persada Cabang Bandung 2, dengan fokus pada produk Yakult Less Sugar dan Yakult Rasa Mangga. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan deskriptif kualitatif, informan terdiri atas 15 Yakult Lady dan 15 konsumen/calon konsumen, kedua kelompok informan memberikan informasi mengenai Yakult Less Sugar dan Yakult Rasa Mangga. Data diperoleh melalui wawancara semi-terstruktur, observasi, dan dokumentasi, kemudian dianalisis melalui tahapan pengumpulan data, reduksi data, penyajian data, serta penarikan dan verifikasi kesimpulan. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa kedua inovasi mampu meningkatkan perhatian dan ketertarikan konsumen, tetapi memiliki tingkat penerimaan yang berbeda. Yakult Less Sugar mendapat respons positif terutama karena kandungan gula yang lebih rendah, namun persepsi harga yang lebih tinggi menjadi salah satu kendala dalam mendorong pembelian ulang. Sementara itu, Yakult Rasa Mangga memperoleh penerimaan yang lebih kuat karena menawarkan rasa yang enak, segar, dan berbeda dari produk sebelumnya. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa inovasi produk berperan sebagai salah satu stimulus dalam keputusan pembelian, tetapi bukan merupakan satu-satunya faktor penentu. Faktor harga, selera, kebutuhan, promosi, kebiasaan konsumsi, dan daya beli turut memengaruhi keputusan konsumen.

latest.title: An Empirical Analysis of Factors Influencing Brand Equity in Coffee Shops: A Study of Jakarta, Indonesia
latest.venue: WSEAS TRANSACTIONS ON BUSINESS AND ECONOMICS
latest.abstract: The rapid growth of the coffee shop industry in Jakarta is a direct consequence of Indonesia’s strong contribution to global coffee production as the world’s fourth-largest coffee producer. The number of coffee shops in Indonesia has reached 10,000 outlets. Due to increased competition among coffee shops, businesses are offering better service quality, innovative products, and improved ambiance and atmosphere to enhance brand loyalty, which eventually contributes to brand equity. However, limited studies have investigated the brand equity factors of coffee shop brands in Jakarta, despite the intense market competition among them. This study investigates how various brand-related factors, such as brand awareness, perceived quality, brand association, and brand loyalty, influence the overall brand equity of coffee shop brands in this highly competitive market. This study adopted a descriptive, explorative, and cross-sectional design with quantitative methods to analyze data collected from a representative sample of coffee shop consumers in Jakarta. Data were collected from 390 respondents from Jakarta city of Indonesia from 390 respondents from Jakarta, Indonesia, and were analyzed using SmartPLS. The statistical analysis confirms that there is a significant relationship between the four factors and brand equity, with perceived quality being the most influential factor among the study variables. This study provides strategic managerial recommendations for coffee shop businesses in Jakarta to enhance brand equity, underscoring the vital role of superior perceived quality while supporting sustainable business growth.

latest.title: Pengaruh Pilihan Produk, Kelengkapan Produk dan Store Atmosphere Terhadap Keputusan Pembelian Emas (Studi Kasus PT. Pegadaian UPC William Iskandar)
latest.venue: PENG Jurnal Ekonomi dan Manajemen
latest.abstract: Data nasabah emas pada PT Pegadaian UPC William Iskandar berfluktuasi selama 2022–2025, dan prasurvei menunjukkan pilihan produk yang terbatas, stok yang sering kosong, serta ruang pelayanan yang kurang nyaman. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis pengaruh pilihan produk, kelengkapan produk, dan store atmosphere terhadap keputusan pembelian emas. Desain kuantitatif asosiatif diterapkan pada 108 nasabah yang dipilih dengan accidental sampling; ukuran sampel ditentukan dengan rumus Slovin (e = 10%) dari 752 nasabah dan ditambah sekitar 20%. Data kuesioner skala Likert lima poin dianalisis dengan uji asumsi klasik dan regresi linear berganda menggunakan SPSS 26. Pilihan produk (B = 0,343; β = 0,274; p = 0,001), kelengkapan produk (B = 0,391; β = 0,334; p < 0,001), dan store atmosphere (B = 0,394; β = 0,383; p < 0,001) berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap keputusan pembelian. Secara simultan, ketiga variabel signifikan (F = 443,563 > F tabel 2,69; p < 0,001; adjusted R² = 0,925). Unit layanan perlu menjaga ketersediaan ukuran emas yang dibutuhkan nasabah dan meningkatkan kenyamanan ruang pelayanan.

latest.title: The Influence of Perceived Authenticity and Local Food Image on Purchase Intention toward Local Culinary Products in Ambon City, Indonesia
latest.venue: Jurnal Ekonomi dan Kewirausahaan West Science
latest.abstract: This study aims to examine the influence of perceived authenticity and local food image on purchase intention toward local culinary products in Ambon City, Indonesia. Local culinary products represent the cultural identity and gastronomic heritage of Maluku, yet consumers’ purchase intentions may depend on how they perceive the authenticity and overall image of these products. This study employed a quantitative approach involving 120 respondents selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected using a questionnaire with a five-point Likert scale and analyzed using SPSS, including validity and reliability tests, classical assumption tests, correlation analysis, and multiple linear regression. The correlation results indicate that perceived authenticity is positively associated with purchase intention ((r = 0.413), (p < 0.001)), while local food image demonstrates a stronger positive association with purchase intention ((r = 0.506), (p < 0.001)). Perceived authenticity and local food image are also positively correlated ((r = 0.296), (p = 0.001)). Furthermore, the regression model is statistically significant overall ((F = 29.074), (p < 0.001)) and explains 33.2% of the variation in purchase intention ((R^2 = 0.332)). These findings highlight the relevance of authenticity and local food image in understanding consumer purchase intentions. The study provides insights for local culinary businesses in Ambon to strengthen product authenticity, communicate cultural identity, and develop a favorable image of regional cuisine.

latest.title: PayLater as Financial Flexibility or Consumptive Risk? An NVivo-Assisted Qualitative Study of Convenience, Debt Awareness, and Self-Control Among Generation Z
latest.venue: Jurnal Manajemen Pemasaran dan Perilaku Konsumen.
latest.abstract: Purpose – This study aims to explore the qualitative experiences of Generation Z PayLater users in Indonesia, focusing on three dimensions: convenience, debt awareness, and self-control. Design/Methodology/Approach – The study employed a qualitative research approach. Data were obtained from 20 anonymized consumer interview reports and analyzed using an NVivo-assisted qualitative workflow involving source preparation, case organization, thematic coding, node grouping, selected quotation matrices, and thematic visualization. Findings – The findings show that Generation Z perceives PayLater as providing payment flexibility when funds are unavailable or urgent needs arise, while debt awareness is reflected in the recognition that PayLater constitutes a financial obligation that may generate bill-related anxiety. Self-control is demonstrated through spending limits, need prioritization, early repayment, and cautious use. Overall, PayLater is not perceived merely as a shopping solution or consumption trigger, but as an ambivalent digital credit technology whose meaning depends on the interaction between platform convenience, financial risk awareness, and consumers’ ability to regulate their spending decisions. Originality/Value – The study provides a qualitative perspective on Generation Z’s lived experiences with PayLater by integrating convenience, debt awareness, and self-control into a single analytical framework. Its value lies in showing that the impact of BNPL is not inherently positive or negative but depends on how users balance technological convenience, awareness of financial obligations, and spending self-regulation.

latest.title: When Temporal Features Reuse Data: Adjacent-Window Bias in Customer Panels
latest.venue: Journal of Asia Entrepreneurship and Sustainability
latest.abstract: Customer histories are often converted into rolling or adjacent-window features for segmentation and prediction. The same period-level estimate may then appear as an outcome in one panel row and as a predictor in the next, creating apparent dynamics even when no carryover exists. We develop and apply a validation framework combining a no-carryover benchmark, fully disjoint temporal construction, an identical-sample estimator comparison and strict temporal holdout testing. The application uses 102 weeks of grocery transactions and 9,014 household-category relationships observed under both adjacent and disjoint designs. On this identical sample, the adjacent estimator implies a 1.78-percentage-point movement toward full-price purchasing for a 10-point increase in promotional share, whereas the fully disjoint estimator implies a 1.40-point movement in the opposite direction. A 36-cell Monte Carlo grid shows that adjacent estimators can remain positive under zero carryover across panel lengths and event frequencies, while disjoint estimators recover the null; under true persistence, adjacent construction attenuates or reverses the expected sign. Recent promotional share adds only .0063 to holdout AUC. The study shows that temporal feature validation must distinguish predictive usefulness from dynamic interpretation and intervention. The proposed audit supports model governance by identifying when customer-history features are informative for forecasting but unsafe for behavioural or policy claims.

latest.title: The Effect of Price Perception, Service Quality, and Social Media Promotion on Repurchase Intention
latest.venue: Jurnal Manajemen Pemasaran dan Perilaku Konsumen.
latest.abstract: Purpose – This study aims to examine the effects of price perception, service quality, and social media promotion on repurchase intention at Toko Berkah Jaya Celaket. Design/Methodology/Approach – The study employed a quantitative explanatory research approach to examine the relationships among the research variables. Using saturated sampling, all 56 customers who had made repeat purchases from the store were selected as respondents. Data were analyzed using multiple linear regression and hypothesis testing with SPSS Version 26, following instrument and classical assumption tests. Findings – The findings indicate that perceived price, service quality, and social media marketing have positive and significant effects on repurchase intention. These results suggest that improvements in customers’ price perceptions, service quality, and social media promotion can contribute to higher repurchase intention. Originality/Value – The study provides practical insight into strategies for maintaining the competitiveness and sustainability of traditional micro-enterprises. Its originality lies in providing empirical evidence on the combined effects of price perception, service quality, and social media marketing within the context of a traditional grocery store, a setting that is relatively overlooked in broader retail research. The findings emphasize the importance of these factors as survival strategies for traditional retailers facing increasing competition.

latest.title: The Influence of Healthy Lifestyle and Marketing Strategy on Interest in Buying Healthy Instant Food in Generation Z: A Mediating Effect Analysis
latest.venue: Jurnal Manajemen Pemasaran dan Perilaku Konsumen.
latest.abstract: Purpose – This study aims to analyze the influence of marketing strategies and a healthy lifestyle on Generation Z's intention to buy Lemonilo healthy instant noodles. Design/Methodology/Approach – A quantitative research method was employed targeting Generation Z consumers who had seen Lemonilo's advertisements on social media. Data were collected from 151 respondents using a Likert-scale questionnaire and analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). Findings – The results indicate that marketing has a positive and significant influence on buying interest, demonstrating that creative and interactive digital communication strategies effectively attract attention and build closeness with consumers. Conversely, a healthy lifestyle does not have a direct positive effect on buying interest; however, marketing strategies successfully mediate the influence of a healthy lifestyle on consumer buying interest. Originality/Value – This study highlights the mediating role of marketing strategies in bridging health-conscious lifestyles with actual purchase decisions among Generation Z, emphasizing the necessity for companies to effectively communicate specific health benefits in digital campaigns for healthy instant food products.

latest.title: From price image to online retailer loyalty: The role of trust and consumer sugrophobia
latest.venue: Gazi iktisat ve işletme dergisi
latest.abstract: This study introduces and explores sugrophobia, which is the fear of being deceived or exploited in transactions, as a key but underexplored concept influencing online shopping behavior.Sugrophobia reflects emotional discomfort stemming from self-blame and suspicion, motivating self-protective behavior.Data is collected from 600 consumers.The research hypotheses were analyzed by K-Means Cluster Analysis and SEM.As a result it was found that high sugrophobes display greater scepticism but also exhibit stronger loyalty once trust is established.Conversely, low sugrophobes are less sceptical and more responsive to price promotions.The findings reveal that trust is the primary driver of loyalty for high sugrophobes, whereas price image and trust jointly influence loyalty among low sugrophobes.

latest.title: How Service Quality and Price Fairness Drive Customer Satisfaction in Distribution Services
latest.venue: Jurnal Manajemen Pemasaran dan Perilaku Konsumen.
latest.abstract: Customer satisfaction in competitive distribution markets increasingly depends on service performance and price fairness, making both factors important to sustain positive customer evaluations. The study aims to analyze the influence of service quality and price on customer satisfaction at PT. Mitra Niaga Distribusindo in Bogor. Quantitative methods were used. A purposive sampling technique was used to select a sample of 46 respondents. The instrument was a Likert scale questionnaire with 1-5 validity and reliability tests. Data were analyzed using multiple linear regression. Partially, service quality and price have a positive and significant effect on customer satisfaction. Together, both variables significantly affect customer satisfaction. This study implies that companies should improve service quality consistency and optimize pricing strategies to sustain customer satisfaction.

latest.title: THE EFFECTS OF BRAND AMBASSADOR, BRAND IMAGE, AND PRICE PERCEPTION ON THE PURCHASE DECISION OF AZARINE SUNSCREEN PRODUCTS AMONG FEMALE STUDENTS AT MALIKUSSALEH UNIVERSITY
latest.venue: Bulletin of Engineering Science Technology and Industry
latest.abstract: This study aims to determine the partial effects of Brand Ambassador, Brand Image, and Price Perception on the Purchase Decision of Azarine Sunscreen Products among female students at Malikussaleh University. The data used in this study are primary data obtained by distributing questionnaires to 130 respondents. The questionnaire was tested for validity and reliability using Cronbach’s Alpha. Classical assumption tests included normality, multicollinearity, and heteroscedasticity tests. Hypothesis testing was conducted using the (partial) t-test and the coefficient of determination R². The data analysis technique used was multiple linear regression with the aid of IBM SPSS Statistics software, version 26. The results of the study indicate that the Brand Ambassador variable has a significance value of 0.046 and a calculatedt-value of 2.018 > t table of 1.979, indicating a positive and significant effect on the Purchase Decision. Thus, the first hypothesis is accepted. Meanwhile, the Brand Image variable has a significance value of 0.016 and a t calculated of 2.432 > t table , indicating a positive and significant effect on the Purchase Decision; therefore, the second hypothesis is accepted. Furthermore, the Price Perception variable shows a significance value of 0.002 and a calculated t-value of 3.104 > table t-value, indicating a positive and significant effect on the Purchase Decision; thus, the third hypothesis is accepted. Thus, it can be concluded that, individually, Brand Ambassador, Brand Image, and Price Perception have a positive and significant effect on the Purchase Decision for Azarine Sunscreen among female students at Malikussaleh University.

latest.title: THE INFLUENCE OF STORE LAYOUT, PRODUCT COMPLETENESS AND PRICE ON PURCHASE INTENTION AT KASMART BIMA
latest.venue: Bulletin of Engineering Science Technology and Industry
latest.abstract: This study aims to determine the effect of store layout, product completeness, and price on purchase intention at Kasmart Bima. The problem in this study is motivated by the decline in sales and indications of low consumer purchase intention related to the condition of the store layout that is not yet optimal, inadequate product completeness, and price perceptions that do not fully meet consumer expectations. This study uses a quantitative method with data collection techniques through questionnaires distributed to 100 respondents who are consumers of Kasmart Bima. Data analysis was carried out using multiple linear regression analysis with hypothesis testing through the t-test, F-test, and coefficient of determination.The results of the study show that partially, store layout has a positive and significant effect on purchase intention with a t-count value of 3.060 and a significance value of 0.003 < 0.05. Product completeness does not have a significant effect on purchase intention with a t-count value of 0.487 and a significance value of 0.628 > 0.05. Price has a positive and significant effect on purchase intention with a t-count value of 5.003 and a significance value of 0.000 < 0.05. Simultaneously, store layout, product completeness, and price have a positive and significant effect on purchase intention with an F-count value of 40.986 and a significance value of 0.000 < 0.05. The coefficient of determination (R Square) value of 0.562 indicates that store layout, product completeness, and price are able to explain 56.2% of purchase intention, while the remaining 43.8% is influenced by other factors outside this study.

latest.title: THE EFFECT OF CAFE ATMOSPHERE AND MENU VARIETY ON REVISIT INTENTION AT TERRACE CURVA COFFEE IN MEDAN CITY
latest.venue: Bulletin of Engineering Science Technology and Industry
latest.abstract: This study was motivated by the suboptimal Revisit Intention of Terrace Curva Coffee consumers, which is related to several aspects of Cafe Atmosphere and Menu Variety. This study aims to analyze the effect of Cafe Atmosphere and Menu Variety on Revisit Intention among consumers of Terrace Curva Coffee in Medan, both partially and simultaneously. This study employed a quantitative approach with a sample of 125 respondents selected using accidental sampling. Data were collected through a Likert-scale questionnaire and analyzed using multiple linear regression, t-test, F-test, and the coefficient of determination with the assistance of IBM SPSS Statistics 27. The results show that Cafe Atmosphere has a positive and significant effect on Revisit Intention, with a regression coefficient of 0.173, t-value of 2.364, and significance value of 0.020. Menu Variety also has a positive and significant effect, with a regression coefficient of 0.353, t-value of 5.374, and significance value of <0.001, and is the relatively most dominant variable with a Standardized Beta value of 0.515. Simultaneously, both variables have a positive and significant effect on Revisit Intention, with an F-value of 58.454 and significance value of <0.001. The R Square value of 0.489 indicates that Cafe Atmosphere and Menu Variety explain 48.9% of the variation in Revisit Intention, while the remaining 51.1% is explained by other factors outside the scope of this study.

latest.title: THE INFLUENCE OF SERVICE QUALITY, PRODUCT QUALITY AND SOCIAL MEDIA PROMOTION ON CONSUMER SATISFACTION AT SPECTA CAFE
latest.venue: Bulletin of Engineering Science Technology and Industry
latest.abstract: This study aims to determine the influence of service quality, product quality, and social media promotion on consumer satisfaction at Specta Cafe. The study was motivated by a decline in sales and indications of consumer dissatisfaction regarding service, product quality, and social media promotional activities. A quantitative method was employed, with data collected via questionnaires distributed to 100 Specta Cafe customers. Data analysis was conducted using multiple linear regression, with hypothesis testing performed via the t-test, F-test, and coefficient of determination. The results indicate that service quality has a positive and significant partial effect on consumer satisfaction, with a calculated t-value of 2.137 and a significance value of 0.035 (< 0.05). Product quality does not have a significant effect on consumer satisfaction, with a calculated t-value of -1.081 and a significance value of 0.282 (> 0.05). Social media promotion also does not have a significant effect on consumer satisfaction, with a calculated t-value of -0.681 and a significance value of 0.498 (> 0.05). Simultaneously, service quality, product quality, and social media promotion do not have a significant effect on consumer satisfaction, with a calculated F-value of 2.021 and a significance value of 0.116 (> 0.05). The coefficient of determination (R-squared) of 0.059 indicates that the variables of service quality, product quality, and social media promotion explain 5.9% of consumer satisfaction, while the remaining 94.1% is influenced by factors outside the scope of this study.

latest.title: PENGARUH POLA GAYA HIDUP DAN KEMUDAHAN PAY LATER PADA APLIKASI SHOPEE TERHADAP PENGELOLAAN KEUANGAN PADA GENERASI Z DI BANDUNG RAYA DENGAN LITERASI KEUANGAN SEBAGAI VARIABEL MODERASI
latest.venue: The Indonesian Journal of Social Studies
latest.abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis pengaruh gaya hidup dan kemudahan Shopee PayLater terhadap pengelolaan keuangan Generasi Z serta menguji peran literasi keuangan sebagai variabel moderasi. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif eksplanatori dengan rancangan survei potong lintang. Responden penelitian berjumlah 200 orang Generasi Z berusia 18-29 tahun yang berdomisili di Kota Bandung, Kota Cimahi, Kabupaten Bandung, Kabupaten Bandung Barat, dan Kabupaten Sumedang serta pernah atau sedang menggunakan Shopee PayLater dalam enam bulan terakhir. Data dikumpulkan melalui angket tertutup berbasis skala Likert lima poin dan dianalisis menggunakan SEM-PLS melalui SmartPLS 4.0. Hasil outer model menunjukkan seluruh konstruk memenuhi validitas konvergen dengan AVE di atas 0,50 dan reliabilitas di atas 0,70, meskipun indikator Z.2 memiliki outer loading rendah. Model struktural menghasilkan R-square sebesar 0.438 dan Q2predict sebesar 0.367. Gaya hidup dan kemudahan PayLater berpengaruh positif signifikan terhadap pengelolaan keuangan, sehingga H1 dan H2 tidak didukung karena arah hipotesis semula negatif. Literasi keuangan tidak mendukung moderasi H3, tetapi mendukung moderasi H4 pada hubungan kemudahan PayLater dan pengelolaan keuangan.

hot.title: A Glance on Changing Workplace Dynamics Post Covid-19 in India: A Review of Psychological Employee Withdrawal Behavior
hot.abstract: Advances in Consumer Research (Abbreviated as Adv. Consum. Res.) is a distinguished journal based in the United States and published by Sheridan Books. The journal is highly regarded in the academic community, particularly within the fields of Business, Management, and Accounting, with a specific focus on Marketing.

hot.title: Psychology’s Theory Crisis, and why formal modelling cannot solve it
hot.abstract: In light of psychology’s ‘theory crisis’, multiple authors have argued that adopting formalization and/or formal modelling would constitute a useful or even necessary step towards stronger psychological theory. In this article, I instead argue that formal modelling cannot solve the core problem the psychological ‘theory crisis’ refers to, which are the currently high degrees of contrastive and holistic underdetermination of our theories by our data. I do so by first introducing underdetermination as an explanatory framework for determining the evidential import of research findings for theories, and showing how both broader theoretical considerations and informal assumptions are key to this process. Then, I derive the aforementioned core problem from the current ‘theory crisis’ literature and tentatively explore its possible solutions. Lastly, I show that formal modelling is neither a necessary nor sufficient solution for either contrastive or holistic underdetermination, and that its uncritical adoption might instead worsen the crisis.

hot.title: From Asymmetry to Satisfaction: The Dynamic Role of Perceived Value and Trust to Boost Customer Satisfaction in the Tourism Industry
hot.abstract: The study investigates how information asymmetry affects customer satisfaction in the tourism industry by examining trust and perceived value as mediating factors. The research implements an integrated model to test and prove information asymmetry’s direct and mediating effects on customer satisfaction by examining the literature gap. The research used a quantitative approach based on opinion polls distributed to 408 customers of hotels, tourism companies, and travel agencies who were in Egypt. SmartPLS 3 software implemented the data analysis process using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). Previous studies have developed scales to measure information asymmetry and its related constructs, including customer trust, perceived value, and customer satisfaction. Multiple tests showed that the measurement tools possess both reliability and validity. Results strongly support all hypotheses: information asymmetry demonstrated significant direct negative effects on customer satisfaction (β = −0.187), trust (β = −0.520), and perceived value (β = −0.453). Conversely, customer satisfaction received significant positive direct effects from both trust (β = 0.273) and perceived value (β = 0.263). Importantly, trust (indirect effect β = −0.142) and perceived value (indirect effect β = −0.119) acted as powerful mediators, confirming that information asymmetry diminishes satisfaction largely by eroding these crucial factors. Crucially, the results demonstrate that the negative impact of information asymmetry on customer satisfaction is significantly mediated jointly through two parallel pathways: the erosion of customer trust and the impairment of perceived value. The research adds theoretical support to information asymmetry theory with its findings while als
